scenario:
The insurer Moravska Jistota wants to simplify the reporting of property damage. Insured events are handled by the Claims Department, whose employees act in the responsibility of claims adjuster. Insured clients can report damage through two channels: by telephone on the claims line, or via a web form in the client zone. Both channels lead to the same offering – the settlement of the insured event, which the client perceives as a single service. Once damage has been reported, the claims adjuster verifies the insurance cover, assesses the extent of the damage and decides on the amount of the payout; the results are recorded in the claim file. The insurer registers around 40,000 claims a year and roughly a quarter of reports now arrive by telephone.

The director of customer service is considering closing the claims line and needs a business layer model that makes clear through which channels the client accesses which service, who provides the service, what triggers internal processing and what information the process works with. She does not require application detail at this stage.
question: Which model best captures the situation and answers the concern of the director of customer service?
options: The Claims Department is a Business Actor assigned (assignment) to the Business Role “Claims adjuster”, which performs the Business Process “Insured event handling”; the process realizes the Business Service “Insured event settlement” serving (serving) the role “Policyholder”. The claims line and the web form are two Business Interfaces composed (composition) in the Claims adjuster role and assigned to the service. The Business Event “Damage reported” triggers the process, which writes to the Business Object “Claim file”.

The Claims Department is a Business Actor assigned (assignment) to the Business Role “Claims adjuster”, which performs the Business Process “Insured event handling”; the process realizes the Business Service “Insured event settlement” serving (serving) the role “Policyholder”. The claims line and the web form are merged into a single Business Interface “Damage contact point”, which is assigned (assignment) to the service. The Business Event “Damage reported” triggers the process, which writes to the Business Object “Claim file”.

The Claims Department is a Business Actor assigned (assignment) to the Business Role “Claims adjuster”, which performs the Business Process “Insured event handling”; the process realizes the Business Service “Insured event settlement” serving the role “Policyholder”. The claims line and the web form are modelled as two further Business Roles (“Line operator”, “Web form”) assigned (assignment) to the process as its additional performers. The Business Event “Damage reported” triggers the process, which writes to the Business Object “Claim file”.

The Business Service “Insured event settlement” realizes (realization) the Business Process “Insured event handling”, to which the Business Role “Claims adjuster” is assigned; this role is in turn assigned (assignment) to the Business Actor “Claims Department”. The claims line and the web form are two Business Objects that the policyholder reads (access) when reporting damage. Reporting damage is a separate Business Process “Damage reporting”, which writes to the Business Object “Claim file” and passes it to the claims adjuster.
explanation: The 5-point model separates the actor (the department) from the responsibility (the role) and the internal process from the service it realizes, and it models both channels as separate Business Interfaces assigned to the service – which is exactly what the director needs for her decision about the claims line; the report is a Business Event that triggers the process. The 3-point option is valid, but by merging the channels into one interface it loses the very information for which the model is being built. The 1-point option models the channels as roles, i.e. as responsibilities, not as access points to the service. The 0-point option reverses realization (a service does not realize a process), assigns the role to the actor in the opposite direction (assignment runs from the actor to the role) and mistakes the channels for passive objects.

scenario:
The mortgage bank Vltava arranges mortgages in two ways: through its own branches and through independent brokerage firms with which it has cooperation agreements. Branch employees and brokers must fulfil the same obligations when arranging a mortgage – an advisory interview, the collection of documents and the submission of the application – and the bank collectively refers to them as the responsibility of the mortgage adviser. On the client side, it is common for one person to be the borrower on one loan and the guarantor on another loan (for example for a son); the obligations of a borrower and a guarantor differ fundamentally.

The head of compliance is preparing a control methodology. She wants a model of the process “Mortgage arrangement” that will make clear who bears which responsibility regardless of whether it is performed by a branch employee or a broker, and that will make it possible to capture one person in several positions at the same time.
question: Which model best meets the requirement of the head of compliance?
options: The Business Roles “Mortgage adviser”, “Borrower” and “Guarantor” are assigned (assignment) to the respective steps of the Business Process “Mortgage arrangement”. The Business Actors “Bank branch” and “Brokerage firm” are both assigned (assignment) to the role Mortgage adviser. The Business Actor “Client” is assigned to both the Borrower and Guarantor roles at the same time, because one person can fulfil both.

The Business Roles “Mortgage adviser”, “Borrower” and “Guarantor” are assigned (assignment) to the respective steps of the Business Process “Mortgage arrangement”. The Business Actors “Bank branch”, “Brokerage firm” and “Client” are connected to their roles by an association relationship; the client is connected in this way to both the Borrower role and the Guarantor role.

The Business Roles “Borrower” and “Guarantor” are assigned to the steps of the Business Process “Mortgage arrangement” and the Business Actor “Client” is assigned to both roles. The adviser's responsibility is captured by the Business Collaboration “Mortgage advisory”, which aggregates (aggregation) the Business Actors “Bank branch” and “Brokerage firm” and is assigned (assignment) to the advisory steps.

Borrower, Guarantor, Bank adviser and Broker are modelled as Business Actors assigned (assignment) directly to the steps of the Business Process “Mortgage arrangement”. The client's position is expressed by the Business Role “Client” assigned (assignment) to the actors Borrower and Guarantor, and similarly by the Business Role “Adviser” assigned to the actors Bank adviser and Broker.
explanation: The best model separates responsibilities (Business Roles) from the parties that perform them (Business Actors): both the branch and the brokerage firm are assigned to the same adviser role and one client can be assigned to both the borrower and the guarantor role (5). The 3-point option has the right elements, but an association relationship instead of assignment does not express who performs the responsibility, which is the core of the compliance concern. The 1-point option wrongly uses a Business Collaboration, which means joint performance of behaviour – yet the branch and the broker each arrange the mortgage independently. The 0-point option models positions as actors and assigns roles to actors in the reverse direction, which ArchiMate does not allow (assignment always runs from the actor to the role).

scenario:
The freight forwarding company Labe Logistic is reworking its end-to-end processes “Container import”, “Shipment export” and “Transit through the EU”. In all three processes a customs declaration has to be prepared and filed. This work is done by a team of customs declarants in Usti nad Labem with specific expertise, authorisation to deal with the customs administration and access to customs systems; the team serves all branches of the company. Customs administration is long-term stable for the company – the processes change roughly every two years, while the way customs administration is provided remains. Today, however, each process describes the customs steps in its own way.

The operations director wants a business layer model that captures customs administration as a stable area of expertise delimited by competencies and resources, separate from the processes being reworked, and shows which processes depend on it – so that a change to a process does not require changing the definition of customs administration.
question: Which model best corresponds to the operations director's requirement?
options: Model customs administration as the Business Function “Customs declaration”, to which the Business Role “Customs declarant” is assigned (assignment). The function realizes the internal Business Service “Shipment customs clearance” and this service serves (serving) all three Business Processes – Container import, Shipment export and Transit through the EU.

Model customs administration as the Business Process “Customs declaration”, to which the Business Role “Customs declarant” is assigned (assignment). The process realizes the internal Business Service “Shipment customs clearance” and this service serves (serving) all three end-to-end Business Processes – Container import, Shipment export and Transit through the EU.

Model customs administration as the Business Function “Customs declaration” with the Business Role “Customs declarant” assigned (assignment). The function is composed (composition) of the Business Processes Container import, Shipment export and Transit through the EU, which thus form its internal parts and share its competencies and resources.

Model customs administration as the Business Interface “Customs counter” assigned (assignment) to all three Business Processes. Knowledge of customs regulations is the Business Object “Customs regulations”, which is assigned (assignment) to the Business Role “Customs declarant” and determines which process steps the declarant performs.
explanation: A Business Function groups behaviour by competencies and resources and is stable over time, so it best captures customs administration; through the internal Business Service the processes are tied to a service, not to the internal steps of the function, and a change to a process does not change the definition of the administration (5). The model with a Business Process is valid, but a process is a sequence of steps leading to a specific result, not a stable area of expertise, so it captures the requirement less well (3). The 1-point option does choose a function, but by composition it claims that whole end-to-end processes are part of customs administration, which contradicts the required separation. The 0-point option mistakes behaviour for an interface and a passive object and uses assignment relationships that ArchiMate does not permit between these elements.

scenario:
Lipova City Hospital is introducing, with Horizont Health Insurance, a new procedure for approving expensive biological treatment. The indication is decided by a joint online consilium, at which the hospital's attending physician and the insurer's review physician jointly assess the medical documentation and agree on a conclusion. Neither of them can approve the treatment alone – the attending physician is responsible for the medical indication, the review physician for compliance with the reimbursement rules. The result is the approval of the treatment, which the patient perceives as a service. The consilium has no organisational status of its own, yet it has operated for a long time with fixed rules. Until now each institution ran its own approval process and their conclusions often diverged, which delayed the start of treatment.

The hospital's quality manager needs a model in which it will be explicitly visible who takes part in the decision and that this is joint behaviour of both parties, distinct from the hospital's and the insurer's own processes.
question: Which model best captures the joint decision-making according to the quality manager's requirement?
options: The Business Collaboration “Indication consilium” aggregates the Business Roles “Attending physician” and “Review physician” and is assigned (assignment) to the Business Interaction “Joint indication assessment”. The interaction realizes the Business Service “Approval of expensive treatment”, which serves (serving) the role “Patient”. The hospital and the insurer are Business Actors assigned to the respective roles.

The Business Roles “Attending physician” and “Review physician” are assigned (assignment) through an AND junction to the Business Process “Indication assessment”, which realizes the Business Service “Approval of expensive treatment” serving (serving) the role “Patient”. The hospital and the insurer are Business Actors assigned to the respective roles; the consilium does not appear in the model as a separate element and its rules are described in documentation.

The Business Roles “Attending physician” and “Review physician” are each assigned by a separate assignment relationship to the Business Process “Indication assessment”, which realizes (realization) the Business Service “Approval of expensive treatment” serving (serving) the role “Patient”. The hospital and the insurer are Business Actors assigned to the respective roles and the consilium is described by the process documentation.

The consilium is represented by a single Business Role “Consilium physician”, which is held alternately by the attending and the review physician and which is assigned (assignment) to the Business Interaction “Joint indication assessment”. The Business Service “Approval of expensive treatment” realizes this interaction, and the hospital and the insurer are the Business Object “Contracting parties”, which the interaction accesses (access) and from which it draws the result.
explanation: Joint behaviour of at least two participants is expressed by a Business Interaction, which is performed by a Business Collaboration aggregating the participating roles; a collaboration need not have organisational status, so it corresponds exactly to the consilium (5). Assigning both roles to the process through an AND junction is a valid alternative for collective behaviour, but less explicit – the consilium as a unit is missing from the model (3). Two separate assignment relationships without a junction mean that each role can perform the behaviour alone, which contradicts the fact that nobody can approve the treatment alone (1). The 0-point option builds the interaction on a single role (an interaction requires at least two participants), reverses the direction of realization between the service and the interaction, which ArchiMate does not permit, and mistakes the participating organisations for a passive object.

scenario:
The bank Krokus is launching “Business Account Plus” for sole traders and small firms. For a single monthly fee the client gets the maintenance of a business account, unlimited domestic payments, a personal banker on the telephone and access to internet banking, where the client manages payments and statements on their own. The account is arranged by a framework agreement, which includes a price list and a guaranteed time for handling requests. Until now the bank offered these services separately at itemised prices; the new package is to combine them into one whole with a single contract. Marketing wants to present the account as a package that saves the entrepreneur time.

The product manager needs a model that shows exactly what is part of the offered whole (including the contractual terms and the digital channel) and captures the value that the product brings to the client. The model is also to serve as a template for the bank's other product packages.
question: Which model best captures Business Account Plus?
options: The Product “Business Account Plus” aggregates (aggregation) the Business Services “Account maintenance”, “Domestic payments” and “Personal banker”, further the Application Service “Online payment and statement management” and the Contract “Framework agreement”, which includes the price list and the guaranteed handling times. The Value “Entrepreneur's time saving” is associated (association) with the product.

The Product “Business Account Plus” aggregates (aggregation) the Business Services “Account maintenance”, “Domestic payments” and “Personal banker”, further the Application Service “Online payment and statement management” and a generic Business Object “Framework agreement” with the price list and the guaranteed times. The Value “Entrepreneur's time saving” is associated (association) with the product.

The Product “Business Account Plus” aggregates (aggregation) the Business Services “Account maintenance”, “Domestic payments” and “Personal banker”, the Contract “Framework agreement” with the price list and the guaranteed times, and also the Application Component “Internet banking” as a whole application. The Value “Entrepreneur's time saving” is associated (association) with the product.

Business Account Plus is a Business Service that realizes (realization) the Contract “Framework agreement” and is composed of the Business Processes “Account maintenance”, “Domestic payments” and “Personal banker”. Internet banking is a Business Interface assigned to this service and the entrepreneur's time saving is a Business Object that the service accesses (access).
explanation: A Product is a composite element that aggregates services of any layer and passive elements together with a contract; the contractual terms, including the price list and the guaranteed times, belong in a Contract (a specialization of Business Object), and value is attached to the product by an association with a Value (5). Modelling the contract as a generic Business Object is valid but less precise – it loses the fact that this is an agreement on rights and obligations (3). ArchiMate 3.2 does not permit aggregating an Application Component into a product; a product should contain the service that the application provides, not active structure (1). The 0-point option mistakes the product for a service, reverses the realization of the contract, composes a service of processes and models value as a passive object.

scenario:
The e-shop Kolo-Expres sells bicycles and parts and in the season ships over 300 parcels a day; between sales and the warehouse, there is often uncertainty about who should start when. After an order is received, the sales department waits for payment; once the bank confirms the incoming payment, the order is released to the warehouse. The warehouse picks the goods, packs them and then hands the parcel over to the carrier. The sales department also passes the warehouse a picking list with the order items. Every evening at 22:00, moreover, the sales department initiates the cancellation of orders that have not been paid within seven days.

The head of operations wants a business process model that clearly shows what triggers the individual steps (including the time-driven cancellation), in what order they follow one another and what information is passed between sales and the warehouse. He does not require applications or technology in this model.
question: Which model best corresponds to the head of operations' requirement?
options: The Business Event “Payment received” triggers (triggering) the Business Process “Picking and packing”, which triggers “Handover to carrier”. A flow relationship leads from the process “Order receipt” to the process “Picking and packing”, and the Business Object “Picking list” is associated with it. The Business Event “Daily at 22:00” triggers the Business Process “Cancellation of unpaid orders”.

The Business Process “Payment receipt” triggers (triggering) the Business Process “Picking and packing”, which triggers “Handover to carrier”. A flow relationship leads from the process “Order receipt” to the process “Picking and packing”, and the Business Object “Picking list” is associated with it. The Business Event “Daily at 22:00” triggers the Business Process “Cancellation of unpaid orders”.

The Business Event “Payment received” is connected by a flow relationship to the Business Process “Picking and packing”, from which a flow leads to “Handover to carrier”; the order of steps is thus expressed by flows. The Business Object “Picking list” is associated with the flow from “Order receipt” to “Picking and packing”. The Business Event “Daily at 22:00” triggers (triggering) “Cancellation of unpaid orders”.

The Business Object “Picking list” triggers (triggering) the Business Process “Picking and packing”, and payment is represented by the Business Role “Payer” assigned to the process “Handover to carrier”. Cancellation is the Business Event “Cancellation of unpaid orders”, which every evening realizes the Business Process “Order receipt”, thus closing the whole order cycle.
explanation: An instantaneous state change (the receipt of payment, the time 22:00) is expressed by a Business Event, the order of steps by a triggering relationship and the passing of information by a flow relationship, with which the Business Object being passed can be associated – the 5-point model thus answers all three of the head of operations' questions. Modelling the receipt of payment as a process is valid, but it obscures that this is an external state change that triggers processing (3). Using flow instead of triggering is a category error: flow describes a transfer without causality, so the model does not say what triggers what (1). The 0-point option lets a passive object trigger behaviour and an event realize a process, which ArchiMate does not permit, and moreover mistakes payment for a role.

scenario:
The Building Department of the Dolni Lhota Municipal Office handles building permit applications. A citizen can submit the application on a paper form at the registry office, or fill in an electronic form and send it through a data mailbox. The content of the application is the same in both cases (builder, plot of land, description of the building); only the form differs. The office then issues a permit decision, which it delivers either as a stamped paper document or as an electronically signed document. The office receives around 800 applications a year and the share of electronic submissions is growing quickly; so far, however, the two forms have been recorded in separate registers.

The office's information manager is unifying the records. In the business layer model she wants to separate the information that the agenda works with from the forms in which this information exists, so that it can be demonstrated that the paper and the electronic application carry the same information and that the process treats them in the same way.
question: Which model best meets the information manager's requirement?
options: The Representations “Paper form” and “Electronic form” realize (realization) the Business Object “Building permit application”; the Representations “Paper decision” and “Electronic decision” realize the Business Object “Permit decision”. The Business Process “Application handling” reads (access) the Application and writes the Decision, because it works with the content, not the form.

Model the paper and electronic application as two Business Objects (“Paper application”, “Electronic application”) that are specializations of the generic Business Object “Building permit application”; similarly, the two forms of the decision specialize the Business Object “Permit decision”. The Business Process “Application handling” reads (access) the generic Application and writes the generic Decision.

Four Data Objects – “Paper form”, “Electronic form”, “Paper decision” and “Electronic decision” – realize (realization) the Business Object “Building permit application” and “Permit decision” respectively. The Business Process “Application handling” reads (access) the Business Object Application and writes the Business Object Decision.

Model the application as the Business Event “Application submitted” and the paper and electronic forms as Business Interfaces, to which the Business Object “Permit decision” is assigned (assignment). This Business Object then realizes (realization) the Representation “Paper decision”, which the application handling process issues to the applicant after the decision becomes final.
explanation: A Representation is a perceptible form of the information carried by a Business Object, and one object can have several representations; the 5-point model thus precisely separates the content (application, decision) from its paper or electronic form, and the process works with a single object. A Business Object specialization is valid and captures the shared content of both forms, but it models the form (paper, electronic) as a subtype of the information although it is only its perceptible form (3). A Data Object belongs to the application layer and represents data for automated processing, so a paper form or paper document modelled as a Data Object is a layer error (1). The 0-point option mistakes passive structure for an event and interfaces and reverses the direction of realization between an object and a representation.

scenario:
The distribution company Energie Jih connects new consumption points to the distribution grid; customers have long complained about the unclear course of handling and the regulator monitors compliance with deadlines. The process starts at the moment a connection application is received. A technician first carries out a technical assessment of the grid capacity in the given location. Depending on the result, either a standard connection takes place (the capacity is sufficient) or – if the capacity is not sufficient – a grid reinforcement study and the conclusion of a contract with connection conditions. The two branches never take place at the same time. In both cases the process ends with informing the applicant of the result.

The process owner wants a model in which it will be unambiguously clear what triggers the process, what steps it consists of, where the decision between two mutually exclusive variants is made and where the branches converge again.
question: Which model best captures the consumption point connection process?
options: The Business Event “Connection application received” triggers (triggering) the step “Technical assessment”, which triggers an OR junction with labelled branches to the steps “Standard connection” and “Grid reinforcement study”. The two branches converge in another OR junction and trigger “Informing the applicant”. The steps are sub-processes of which the Business Process “Consumption point connection” is composed (composition).

The Business Event “Connection application received” triggers (triggering) the step “Technical assessment”, which triggers an OR junction with labelled branches to the steps “Standard connection” and “Grid reinforcement study”. The two branches converge in another OR junction and trigger “Informing the applicant”. The steps are sub-processes of which the Business Function “Customer connection” is composed (composition).

The Business Event “Connection application received” triggers (triggering) the step “Technical assessment”, from which two separate triggering relationships, each labelled with a condition, lead to the steps “Standard connection” and “Grid reinforcement study”. Both steps then trigger “Informing the applicant” and all the steps are sub-processes of which the Business Process “Consumption point connection” is composed (composition).

Connect the steps “Technical assessment”, “Standard connection”, “Grid reinforcement study” and “Informing the applicant” with flow relationships, because documents and technical calculations travel between them. Model the decision as the Business Object “Assessment result”, which, according to the capacity found, triggers (triggering) both variants, and the received application as the Business Role “Applicant” assigned (assignment) to the first step.
explanation: Mutually exclusive branches are expressed by an OR junction on triggering relationships with labelled conditions, and the convergence of the branches by a second OR junction; the event triggers the process and the sub-processes form the composition of the overall process (5). The same behaviour wrapped in a Business Function is valid, but a function groups behaviour by competencies and resources, not as a flow from a trigger to a result, so it is less apt (3). Two separate triggering relationships without a junction express that the step triggers both variants – the condition labels are only informal text, so the model expresses neither the mutual exclusion of the branches nor the place where they converge (1). The 0-point option replaces the order with flows without causality and lets a passive object trigger behaviour, which ArchiMate does not permit.

image.alt: Two examples of a junction on a triggering relationship between processes: an AND junction (filled circle) and an OR junction (hollow circle), each with its reading.

scenario:
The AgroHold holding brings together four subsidiaries (a dairy, a bakery, a malt house and a trading company), each of which is a separate legal entity with its own processes. A shared service centre in Olomouc processes incoming invoices and payroll for all of them. The subsidiaries' procurement processes cannot work without invoice processing, and HR administration depends on payroll processing. Inside the centre, scanning, data extraction, an approval workflow and checking take place – these steps are documented in detail in separate process models.

The holding's chief financial officer is preparing a new system of intra-group prices, which are to be derived from the number of documents and employees processed. They need a one-page model that shows which services the centre provides and which processes of which subsidiaries use them; they do not want to see the centre's internal workings in it.
question: Which model best matches the chief financial officer's concern?
options: The shared service centre is a Business Actor assigned (assignment) to the Business Function "Shared financial services", which realizes (realization) the Business Services "Incoming invoice processing" and "Payroll processing". These serve (serving) the processes "Procurement" and "HR administration", to which the subsidiaries are assigned as Business Actors.

The shared service centre is a Business Actor assigned (assignment) to the Business Process "Invoice processing", which is composed (composition) of the subprocesses Scanning, Data extraction, Approval workflow and Checking; the payroll processing process is broken down in the same way. The processes realize Business Services, which serve (serving) the Procurement and HR administration processes of the subsidiaries.

The shared service centre is a Business Actor assigned (assignment) to the Business Function "Shared financial services", which realizes (realization) the Business Services "Incoming invoice processing" and "Payroll processing". The Business Processes "Procurement" and "HR administration" of the subsidiaries are connected to the services by a serving relationship leading from these processes to the centre's services.

The shared service centre is a Business Role assigned (assignment) to the Procurement and HR administration processes of all the subsidiaries. The services "Incoming invoice processing" and "Payroll processing" realize (realization) these processes and are aggregated (aggregation) in the Business Object "Centre service catalogue", which the subsidiaries share and on the basis of which the intra-group prices will be charged.
explanation: The 5-point model shows the centre as a provider of internal Business Services that serve (serving) the subsidiaries' processes; the internal steps are hidden behind the function, which matches the required level of abstraction. Breaking out the internal subprocesses is correct ArchiMate, but it is needlessly detailed for a one-page view and contradicts the chief financial officer's explicit wish (3). A serving relationship leading from the consumer to the provider is reversed – serving must point from the service to the process that uses it (1). The 0-point option claims that the centre performs the subsidiaries' processes, reverses the realization between the service and the process, and places the services in a passive object, which the relationship tables do not permit.

image.alt: ArchiMate generic metamodel: internal and external active structure, internal behavior, service, event and passive structure with the relationships assigned to, realizes, serves, accesses, triggers/flows to and composed of.

scenario:
The transport company Expres Cargo is reorganising its structure. The Transport division consists of depots in Brno and Ostrava, and the Warehouses division operates the central warehouse in Olomouc. Dispatchers work in both depots, and their duties are the same everywhere. In total the company employs over 900 people, and the new structure is to take effect on 1 January. In addition, the company has set up a project team for six months to introduce a new transport system, into which it has seconded analysts from the IT department and specialists from the Transport division; the team has no organisational status of its own and will cease to exist when the project ends.

The HR director needs a model for the Organization viewpoint that shows the organisational units and their composition, where the units are located, what responsibilities exist in them, and how the temporary project team is represented.
question: Which model best suits the HR director?
options: The divisions and depots are Business Actors, and the Transport division is composed (composition) of the Brno and Ostrava depots. The Locations "Brno", "Ostrava" and "Olomouc" aggregate (aggregation) the respective units. Both depots are assigned (assignment) to the Business Role "Dispatcher". The project team is a Business Collaboration aggregating the roles "IT analyst" and "Transport specialist".

The divisions and depots are Business Actors, and the Transport division is composed (composition) of the Brno and Ostrava depots. The Locations "Brno", "Ostrava" and "Olomouc" aggregate the respective units, and both depots are assigned to the Business Role "Dispatcher". The project team is another Business Actor, which is a permanent part (composition) of the IT department.

The divisions and depots are Business Actors, the Transport division is composed (composition) of the Brno and Ostrava depots, and both depots are assigned (assignment) to the Business Role "Dispatcher". The project team is a Business Collaboration aggregating (aggregation) the roles "IT analyst" and "Transport specialist". Location is expressed by an assignment relationship leading from each unit to the Locations "Brno", "Ostrava" and "Olomouc" respectively.

The divisions are Groupings and the depots are Business Collaborations grouped in them. The Business Role "Dispatcher" is assigned (assignment) to the Brno and Ostrava depots, which employ the dispatchers. The project team is the Location "Transport system project" and the central warehouse is the Business Role "Olomouc warehouse" of the Warehouses division.
explanation: Organisational units are Business Actors (composition expresses the organisational structure), location is modelled in ArchiMate 3 by aggregation from the Location, the dispatchers' identical duties are shared by a single Business Role, and a temporary team without organisational status is a typical Business Collaboration (5). Modelling the team as a permanent organisational unit is valid but loses its temporary and cross-cutting nature (3). Connecting a location to elements with an assignment relationship is reminiscent of ArchiMate 2 – in version 3 the location aggregates the elements, and an assignment relationship from an organisational unit to a Location is not permitted by the relationship tables (1). The 0-point option confuses organisational units with collaboration and grouping, assigns the role to the actor in the opposite direction, and uses a location for the team.

scenario:
The Polabi Regional Hospital uses the MedIS hospital information system. Patient admission at the internal medicine clinic is carried out by admission nurses: they verify the patient's health insurance, create a medical record for them and schedule the initial examination. Both the insurance verification and the creation of the record are provided by the patient management module of MedIS, and the nurses work with it through the clinical desktop – the system's only user interface. When the record is created, a patient record is produced in MedIS, which doctors then work with.

In two years' time the hospital plans to replace the patient management module with another product. The owner of the admission process and the application architect therefore want a model that shows which application services support which admission steps, through which interface the nurse works with them and what data is produced – and in such a way that the links between the process and the application do not depend on the internal design of the system.
question: Which model best matches the requirement of the process owner and the application architect?
options: The Application Component "MedIS" is assigned to the Application Function "Patient management", which realizes the Application Services "Insurance verification" and "Medical record creation" serving (serving) the respective steps of the process "Patient admission". The Application Interface "Clinical desktop", part of MedIS, is assigned to the services and serves the role "Admission nurse". The function writes (access) the Data Object "Patient record".

The Application Component "MedIS" serves (serving) the Business Process "Patient admission", to whose steps the role "Admission nurse" is assigned. MedIS writes (access) the Data Object "Patient record" and is composed (composition) of the Application Interface "Clinical desktop", which serves the nurse role; application services and functions do not appear in the model because they would needlessly burden it.

The Application Component "MedIS" is assigned to the Application Function "Patient management", which realizes the Application Services "Insurance verification" and "Medical record creation" serving the steps of the Business Process "Patient admission". The clinical desktop is a Business Interface of the role "Admission nurse", assigned (assignment) to both application services. The function writes (access) the Data Object "Patient record".

The Business Process "Patient admission" serves (serving) the Application Function "Patient management", which is performed by MedIS, and the Data Object "Patient record" triggers (triggering) this function after each creation of a new patient record. The clinical desktop is an Application Service assigned (assignment) to the role "Admission nurse", who uses this service to verify insurance and schedule the examination.
explanation: The 5-point model separates the component (who), the function (what it does internally) and the application services (what it offers externally); the process steps are tied to the services, so replacing the module does not change the process's links, and the GUI is an Application Interface serving the nurse role. A direct serving relationship from the component to the process is a valid derived relationship, but it omits the services the process owner cares about and ties the process directly to a specific system (3). Modelling the clinical desktop as a Business Interface is a layer error, and ArchiMate does not permit assigning a business interface to an application service (1). The 0-point option reverses the direction of support (in the scenario the application serves the process, not the other way round), lets passive data trigger behaviour and confuses an interface with a service.

scenario:
The sports e-shop Horal Sport runs three main applications: the WebShop e-commerce platform, the Orion ERP enterprise system and the SkladPro warehouse system. A new order is passed from WebShop to the ERP; the ERP then sends a picking request to SkladPro, and SkladPro returns the shipment status to the ERP. Every 15 minutes the ERP sends the current stock levels to WebShop. Integration currently runs via files and REST calls, but their technical form will change next year. Integration outages have repeatedly caused shipping delays over the past year.

The IT director is preparing a replacement for the Orion ERP and needs a model in the spirit of the Application Cooperation viewpoint: which applications exchange information, in which direction and what information is transferred in each exchange. They do not require technology or business processes in this view.
question: Which model best serves the IT director?
options: Connect the Application Components "WebShop", "ERP Orion" and "SkladPro" with flow relationships: WebShop → ERP, ERP → SkladPro, SkladPro → ERP and ERP → WebShop. Each flow is associated (association) with a Data Object that expresses the information transferred – "Order", "Picking request", "Shipment status" and "Stock levels".

Connect the Application Components "WebShop", "ERP Orion" and "SkladPro" with flow relationships in the correct directions: WebShop → ERP, ERP → SkladPro, SkladPro → ERP and ERP → WebShop. The flows are neither named nor connected to data objects, because the technical form of the integrations will change next year.

Connect the Application Components "WebShop", "ERP Orion" and "SkladPro" with triggering relationships: WebShop → ERP, ERP → SkladPro, SkladPro → ERP and ERP → WebShop. Each relationship is associated with a Data Object expressing the information transferred – "Order", "Picking request", "Shipment status" and "Stock levels".

Model ERP Orion as an Application Component composed (composition) of the components WebShop and SkladPro, because it shares data with them. The Data Objects "Order", "Shipment status" and "Stock levels" are assigned (assignment) to the components that send them, and trigger (triggering) the components that receive and further process them.
explanation: The exchange of information between applications is expressed by the flow relationship (a transfer without necessary causality), and a Data Object can be associated with the flow to say what is transferred – the 5-point model thus answers all of the IT director's questions and does not depend on the technical form of the integration. Unnamed flows are correct but incomplete – they lack the transferred information, which is essential for replacing the ERP (3). Triggering expresses a temporal or causal sequence of behaviour, not a transfer of data; the model with it does list data objects, but relationships of the wrong category claim something other than what happens between the applications (1). The 0-point option claims that independent applications are part of the ERP, and leads assignment and triggering relationships from the data objects, which ArchiMate does not permit.

image.alt: Overview of the notation of all ArchiMate relationships divided into structural, dependency, dynamic and other, including the AND and OR junctions.

scenario:
The water utility Aqua Vysocina used to match incoming payments with issued invoices manually – accountants went through the bank statement every morning. Now this is done automatically by the AquaBill billing system: as soon as the bank delivers an electronic statement to it, a batch job is started that loads the statement, matches the payments to invoices by variable symbol and records the payment status on the matched invoices. The business process "Payment matching" is thus no longer performed by any person; accountants handle only exceptions in a separate process. This amounts to roughly 60,000 payments a month.

The application architect wants to describe the new state in a model that shows what triggers the batch processing, which application performs it, what data it works with and that the business process is now fully automated. The model will serve as a basis for operational documentation and for an audit of accounting procedures.
question: Which model best captures the new state?
options: The Application Event "Bank statement delivered" triggers (triggering) the Application Process "Automatic payment matching", to which the Application Component "AquaBill" is assigned (assignment). The process reads the Data Object "Bank statement", writes the Data Object "Invoice payment status" and realizes (realization) the Business Process "Payment matching".

The Application Component "AquaBill" is assigned (assignment) to the Application Function "Payment matching", which reads (access) the Data Object "Bank statement", writes the Data Object "Invoice payment status" and realizes (realization) the Business Process "Payment matching". Neither the delivery of the statement nor the triggering of the batch appears in the model.

The Application Event "Bank statement delivered" triggers (triggering) the Application Process "Automatic payment matching", which reads (access) the Data Object "Bank statement" and writes the Data Object "Invoice payment status". The Application Component "AquaBill" is assigned (assignment) to the Business Process "Payment matching".

The Business Process "Payment matching" realizes (realization) the Application Process "Automatic payment matching", and the role "Accountant" is assigned (assignment) to the Application Component "AquaBill". The bank statement is an Application Event that the process accesses (access), and the invoice payment status is a Business Event that this process triggers.
explanation: The automation of a business process is expressed by an Application Process that realizes it; the trigger of the batch is an Application Event, the performer is an Application Component, and reading or writing of data is expressed by access relationships (5). An Application Function is valid and also expresses automation, but it does not capture the batch trigger, which the architect explicitly asks about (3). Assigning an application component to a business process is an ArchiMate 2 construct that version 3 does not permit – automation is modelled by realization (1). The 0-point option reverses the direction of realization, assigns a business role to an application and confuses passive data with events.

scenario:
The transport company Rychla zasilka runs the TrackIT system, which provides information on the status and location of shipments. Three groups of users use the same functionality today: customer line operators work through a web operator interface (GUI), while the company's mobile app for recipients and the systems of partner e-shops query shipment status through a public REST API. Both the operator GUI and the REST API are part of the TrackIT system and both call the same shipment tracking logic.

The solution architect plans separate versioning of the REST API and a replacement of the operator GUI in a year. They therefore need an application-layer model that shows through which access points the tracking functionality is made available, who uses which access point and that the same application service stands behind both. They do not require details of TrackIT's technology platform in this model.
question: Which model best suits the solution architect?
options: The Application Component "TrackIT" is composed (composition) of two Application Interfaces, "Operator GUI" and "Tracking REST API", both of which are assigned (assignment) to the Application Service "Shipment tracking". The operator GUI serves (serving) the Business Role "Customer line operator", and the REST API serves the Application Components "Mobile app" and "Partner e-shop".

The Application Component "TrackIT" is composed (composition) of a single Application Interface "TrackIT interface", which is assigned (assignment) to the Application Service "Shipment tracking". This interface serves (serving) the Business Role "Customer line operator" as well as the Application Components "Mobile app" and "Partner e-shop", so all users use a single access point.

The Application Component "TrackIT" contains the Application Interface "Operator GUI" assigned (assignment) to the Application Service "Shipment tracking", which serves the Business Role "Customer line operator". The REST API is modelled as another Application Service "Tracking API", which TrackIT realizes (realization) and which serves (serving) the components "Mobile app" and "Partner e-shop".

The operator GUI and the REST API are Technology Interfaces assigned (assignment) to the TrackIT component, because both run on its servers. The Application Service "Shipment tracking" is assigned (assignment) to both interfaces and makes them available to operators, while the mobile app and the partner e-shops are Business Actors that use these interfaces when querying the status and location of shipments.
explanation: An access point through which an application service is made available to a user (GUI) or to another application (API) is an Application Interface; two interfaces composed in the component and assigned to the same service show that the same functionality stands behind them and that they can be versioned and replaced separately (5). A single shared interface is valid but blurs the distinction between the GUI and the API, which is the reason the model is being created (3). Modelling the API as another application service confuses an access point (active structure) with behaviour and creates a seeming second service (1). The 0-point option moves the interfaces into the technology layer, reverses the assignment relationship between the service and the interface, and confuses applications with business actors.

scenario:
The bank Horizont authorises card payments in real time. Each authorisation request is evaluated jointly by two systems: the card system CardHost checks the card's balance and limits, and the FraudGuard system evaluates the risk of fraud. During the evaluation the two systems exchange intermediate results, and the approval decision arises only from their joint work – neither of them can authorise the transaction alone. The result is made available as the application service "Card transaction authorisation", which is called by the payment processor's system. The bank authorises more than 200 million transactions a year in this way.

The operations team will manage both systems as one logical whole with a common SLA and common monitoring. The application architect therefore wants an application-layer model in which the joint behaviour of the two systems and their logical grouping are expressed explicitly as part of the architecture, not just in textual documentation.
question: Which model best matches the application architect's requirement?
options: The Application Collaboration "Authorisation platform" aggregates the Application Components "CardHost" and "FraudGuard" and is assigned (assignment) to the Application Interaction "Joint authorisation evaluation", because this is joint behaviour. The interaction realizes the Application Service "Card transaction authorisation", which serves (serving) the Application Component "Payment processor system".

The Application Components "CardHost" and "FraudGuard" are assigned (assignment) via an AND junction to the Application Process "Authorisation evaluation", which realizes the Application Service "Card transaction authorisation" serving (serving) the component "Payment processor system". The shared platform does not appear in the model as a separate element; the cooperation of the two systems is expressed by the junction.

The Application Components "CardHost" and "FraudGuard" are each assigned by a separate assignment relationship to the Application Process "Authorisation evaluation", which realizes the Application Service "Card transaction authorisation" serving (serving) the component "Payment processor system". The common SLA is stated in the description of the process.

Only the CardHost component is assigned (assignment) to the Application Interaction "Joint authorisation evaluation", while FraudGuard is a Data Object that the interaction reads (access). The Application Service "Card transaction authorisation" realizes (realization) this interaction, and the whole is formed by the Node "Authorisation platform" composed (composition) of both systems.
explanation: The collective behaviour of two or more components is expressed by an Application Interaction performed by an Application Collaboration that aggregates the components; the collaboration also represents the required logical whole (5). An AND junction on the process is a valid way to express that both components are needed for the behaviour, but the logical platform is missing from the model (3). Two separate assignment relationships without a junction mean that the process can be performed by either component alone, which contradicts the scenario (1). The 0-point option builds the interaction on a single component, confuses a system with data, reverses the realization between the service and the interaction and composes the application components into a technology node, which the relationship tables do not permit.

scenario:
The energy supplier Energie Pro runs the BillCore billing system. It consists of two separately deployable modules: Rating prices consumption – it reads meter readings and the valid price list and writes the priced consumption; Invoicing reads the priced consumption and writes the issued invoices. The modules do not communicate with each other directly, they are linked only by the shared priced consumption, and both work on a common database. During the monthly closing the system slows down considerably, and the support team suspects database locks during concurrent reading and writing.

The application architect is preparing a performance audit and needs a model of BillCore's internal structure in the spirit of the Application Structure viewpoint, from which it will be clear which modules the system consists of, what behaviour each module performs and which data each module reads and which it writes.
question: Which model best serves the performance audit?
options: The Application Component "BillCore" is composed (composition) of the components "Rating" and "Invoicing", assigned to the Application Functions "Consumption pricing" and "Invoice issuing" respectively. Pricing reads (access) the Data Objects "Meter reading" and "Price list" and writes "Priced consumption"; Issuing reads "Priced consumption" and writes "Invoice".

The Application Component "BillCore" is composed (composition) of the components "Rating" and "Invoicing", assigned (assignment) to the Application Functions "Consumption pricing" and "Invoice issuing" respectively. Both functions are connected to the Data Objects "Meter reading", "Price list", "Priced consumption" and "Invoice" by an access relationship without indicating whether the data is read or written.

The Application Component "BillCore" realizes (realization) two Application Services – "Rating" and "Invoicing" – which in the model represent its separately deployable modules. The Rating service reads (access) the Data Objects "Meter reading" and "Price list" and writes "Priced consumption"; the Invoicing service reads "Priced consumption" and writes "Invoice".

The modules Rating and Invoicing are Application Functions of the BillCore system. The Data Objects "Meter reading", "Price list" and "Priced consumption" are assigned (assignment) to the Rating function, which they trigger when they change, and the Data Object "Invoice" is composed (composition) of the priced consumption, which is taken over by the Invoicing module.
explanation: Separately deployable modules are Application Components composed in BillCore, their behaviour is expressed by Application Functions, and an access relationship with an arrowhead determines reading or writing – exactly what a lock audit needs (5). Access without a marked direction is valid (unspecified access), but it does not distinguish reading from writing, on which the audit rests (3). Modelling the modules as application services confuses active structure with external behaviour – a service is not a module but functionality made available externally (1). The 0-point option lets passive data perform and trigger behaviour, which ArchiMate does not permit, and reduces the modules to functions without a performer.

scenario:
The building society Domov processes loan applications in an automated workflow that runs on the FlowMaster BPM platform. The workflow first obtains the client's score from the Scoring system, then has the DocGen system generate the loan agreement and finally stores the agreement in the DMS document system. The steps must run in exactly this order; the society processes around 4,000 applications a month and every delay in the workflow prolongs the loan approval time. Scoring, DocGen and DMS all offer their functionality as application services, which other systems of the society also use.

The solution architect is assessing how the workflow will be affected by the planned replacement of the DocGen system with a new product. They need an application-layer model that shows which application executes the workflow, what steps it consists of and in what order they take place, and which services of the other systems the individual steps use.
question: Which model best matches the solution architect's need?
options: The Application Component "FlowMaster" is assigned (assignment) to the Application Process "Loan application processing", which is composed (composition) of the steps "Score retrieval", "Agreement generation" and "Agreement archiving" connected by triggering relationships. A serving relationship leads to each step from the respective Application Service – "Score calculation" (Scoring), "Document generation" (DocGen) and "Document storage" (DMS).

The Application Component "FlowMaster" is assigned (assignment) to the Application Function "Loan orchestration". Serving relationships lead to this function from the Application Services "Score calculation" (Scoring), "Document generation" (DocGen) and "Document storage" (DMS); the order of the service calls is described only in the textual documentation of the workflow.

The Application Component "FlowMaster" is assigned (assignment) to the Application Process "Loan application processing", which is composed (composition) of the steps "Score retrieval", "Agreement generation" and "Agreement archiving" connected by triggering relationships. Serving relationships lead from the individual steps to the Application Services "Score calculation" (Scoring), "Document generation" (DocGen) and "Document storage" (DMS).

FlowMaster is composed (composition) of the Scoring, DocGen and DMS systems. The Application Services "Score calculation" (Scoring), "Document generation" (DocGen) and "Document storage" (DMS) are assigned (assignment) to the workflow steps, which execute these services in a fixed order given by the workflow definition in FlowMaster.
explanation: Orchestration with a fixed order of steps is expressed by an Application Process performed by the FlowMaster platform; its steps are connected by triggering relationships and the services of the other systems serve (serving) specific steps, so the impact of replacing DocGen is visible down to the level of the step (5). An Application Function is valid, but a function does not express sequence, so the order the architect needs cannot be read from the model (3). The reversed direction of serving claims that the workflow steps provide functionality to the services of the other systems, which is the opposite of the real dependency (1). The 0-point option composes independent systems into FlowMaster although they are not part of it, and assigns services to steps, which ArchiMate does not permit – a service is behaviour and cannot perform behaviour.

scenario:
The insurance company Jistota is launching a new client zone. The application is delivered as the package klientska-zona.war and runs in the Apache Tomcat application server on the APP01 server with the Linux operating system. The client profile data is stored in the klienti_db database, which is managed by the PostgreSQL database system on a separate server, DB01. Both servers are physical machines in the insurance company's data centre, and the operations team manages them as two separate platforms – an application platform and a database platform.

The head of operations is planning capacity and preparing an upgrade of Tomcat to a new major version. They need a model in the spirit of the Implementation and Deployment viewpoint that shows exactly where the client zone and its data run, on which system software they are deployed, and what realizes the application component "Client zone" and the data object "Client profile".
question: Which model best matches the needs of the head of operations?
options: The Node "Application platform" is composed (composition) of the Device "APP01" and the System Software "Linux" and "Apache Tomcat"; the Artifact "klientska-zona.war", which realizes the Application Component "Client zone", is deployed (assignment) directly on Tomcat. Similarly, the Node "Database platform" consists of the Device "DB01" and the System Software "PostgreSQL", on which the Artifact "klienti_db", which realizes the Data Object "Client profile", is deployed.

The Node "Application platform" is composed (composition) of the Device "APP01" and the System Software "Linux" and "Apache Tomcat", and the Node "Database platform" of the Device "DB01" and the System Software "PostgreSQL". Each node directly hosts (assignment) its artifact – "klientska-zona.war" realizing the Application Component "Client zone" and "klienti_db" realizing the Data Object "Client profile" respectively.

The Device "APP01" is composed (composition) of the Node "Application platform", which includes the System Software "Linux" and "Apache Tomcat"; the Artifact "klientska-zona.war", which realizes the Application Component "Client zone", is deployed (assignment) on Tomcat. Similarly, the Device "DB01" contains the Node "Database platform" with the System Software "PostgreSQL", on which the Artifact "klienti_db" realizing the Data Object "Client profile" is deployed.

The Application Component "Client zone" realizes (realization) the Artifact "klientska-zona.war", from which an assignment relationship leads to the Node "Application platform" with the System Software "Linux" and "Apache Tomcat". The Data Object "Client profile" realizes (realization) the Artifact "klienti_db", from which an assignment relationship leads to the Node "Database platform", on which the PostgreSQL database system runs on the DB01 server.
explanation: In ArchiMate 3.2 a Node is composed of devices and system software, an artifact is deployed by an assignment relationship from the system software it runs on, and artifacts realize both the application component and the data object – the 5-point model thus shows exactly what the Tomcat upgrade will affect. Deploying artifacts directly on the whole node (assignment from the node) is valid, but it does not show which system software hosts them, which is essential for the upgrade (3). Composing a node in a device corresponds to ArchiMate 3.1, where Device was a specialisation of Node; in version 3.2 the relationship tables do not permit this direction (1). The 0-point option reverses the key relationships: neither the component nor the data object realizes the artifact (realization goes in the opposite direction), and an artifact cannot be assigned to a node – assignment leads from the node to the artifact.

image.alt: Deployment chain: a node composed of a device and system software, system software assigned to an artifact, and the artifact realizing an application component and a data object.

scenario:
The Vychod hospital network operates two data centres – a primary one in Hradec and a backup one in Pardubice. The hospital information system's database is replicated synchronously from the primary to the backup centre. From the architects' point of view the replication is one logical connection between the two database servers; physically, however, it runs over two independent leased WAN lines from two different operators and, in each centre, over a local LAN with redundant switches. During last year's outage of one operator the replication failed nonetheless, because the two lines actually shared part of their route. Under the cybersecurity act the hospital must demonstrate the resilience of its critical systems.

The infrastructure architect is preparing a redundancy assessment. They need a technology-layer model that distinguishes the logical connection used by the replication from the physical communication infrastructure that realizes it, and that also captures the network devices in both centres.
question: Which model best serves the redundancy assessment?
options: The Communication Networks "WAN operator A", "WAN operator B", "LAN Hradec" and "LAN Pardubice" realize (realization) the Path "Replication link" between the Nodes "DB Hradec" and "DB Pardubice". Each LAN aggregates (aggregation) its redundant switches, modelled as Devices.

The Nodes "DB Hradec" and "DB Pardubice" are connected directly by an association relationship to the Communication Networks "WAN operator A", "WAN operator B", "LAN Hradec" and "LAN Pardubice"; each LAN aggregates (aggregation) its switches, modelled as Devices. The replication link does not appear in the model as a separate element.

The Path "Replication link" between the Nodes "DB Hradec" and "DB Pardubice" is realized (realization) by redundant switches and routers, which are modelled as Devices. The WAN lines of both operators and the local LANs are listed as properties (attributes) of this path.

The replication link is an Application Service used by both databases. The lines WAN operator A and WAN operator B are Communication Networks assigned (assignment) to the database Application Components, and the LANs are Paths that are realized (realization) by the individual switches.
explanation: A Path is a logical connection over which technology elements exchange data, and a Communication Network is the physical infrastructure that realizes the path; the network may in turn aggregate network devices (5). Without the path the model shows only the physical networks and loses the logical connection whose redundancy the architect is assessing (3). Realization of a path by devices is not permitted in ArchiMate 3.2 – the path is realized by networks, and devices are part of them, and hiding the networks in attributes makes analysis of the shared route impossible (1). The 0-point option moves the connection into the application layer, assigns networks to application components and lets devices realize paths, which the relationship tables do not permit.

scenario:
The brewery Dolni Hana brews lager on its own premises. The brewing system (kettles and a lauter tun) processes malt, hops and water into wort, which the fermentation and lagering tanks turn into beer; this is then filled into kegs on the filling line. The brewing system is controlled by the brewmaster via a control panel right next to the equipment. All the equipment stands in the brewery's main building, which is located in the village of Dolni Hana.

The production director is planning an extension with a new lagering cellar and needs a model in the spirit of the Physical viewpoint: which equipment processes which raw materials and products, in which building the equipment is located, where the brewery is situated and which role operates the equipment. They do not require the brewery's IT systems or the sales business processes in this model, because these will be the subject of separate views.
question: Which model best matches the production director's requirement?
options: The Equipment "Brewing system", "Fermentation and lagering tanks" and "Filling line" are assigned (assignment) to the steps of the Technology Process "Beer production", which read (access) the Material "Malt", "Hops" and "Water" and write the Material "Beer". The Facility "Brewery main building" contains the equipment, the Location "Dolni Hana" aggregates it, and the Brewing system serves (serving) the Business Role "Brewmaster".

The brewing system, the fermentation and lagering tanks and the filling line are Devices assigned (assignment) to the steps of the Technology Process "Beer production", which read (access) the Material "Malt", "Hops" and "Water" and write the Material "Beer". The Facility "Brewery main building" contains the equipment, the Location "Dolni Hana" aggregates it, and the brewing system serves (serving) the Business Role "Brewmaster", who controls it.

The Equipment "Brewing system", "Fermentation and lagering tanks" and "Filling line" are assigned (assignment) to the steps of the Technology Process "Beer production", which read (access) the Business Objects "Malt", "Hops" and "Water" and write the Business Object "Beer". The Facility "Brewery main building" contains the equipment, the Location "Dolni Hana" aggregates it, and the Brewing system serves (serving) the Business Role "Brewmaster".

Model beer production as a Business Event "Beer brewed", which triggers (triggering) the filling of kegs on the filling line. The Material "Malt", "Hops" and "Water" are assigned (assignment) to the Equipment "Brewing system", and the Business Role "Brewmaster" is composed (composition) of the Facility "Brewery main building", in which they work and from which they control the brewhouse.
explanation: Physical machines that process material are Equipment assigned to technology behaviour (physical elements have no behaviour of their own), the raw materials and beer are Material with reading and writing, the building is a Facility, the village is a Location, and operation is expressed by serving from the equipment to the role (5). Modelling the machines as Devices is less precise – a Device is IT hardware for system software and artifacts – but it remains a physical element of the technology layer that the Physical viewpoint takes into account, so the structure of the model fits (3). Raw materials and product as Business Objects move physical matter into the business layer as information, that is, outside the Physical viewpoint, and the model stops describing the physical world (1). The 0-point option models production as a business event, assigns passive material to equipment and composes a role from a building, which ArchiMate does not permit.

image.alt: Four ArchiMate physical elements with icons: Equipment, Facility, Distribution Network and Material.

scenario:
The IT department of the statutory city of Lipnik runs a shared PostgreSQL database cluster for its line-of-business applications – three servers with system software for replication and automatic failover. The platform team offers it as the service "Database as a service": applications get a database, backup and monitoring and connect through a single connection endpoint, without knowing on which server the primary instance is currently running. The service is currently used by the applications Resident Registry, Parking System and Records Management; more are on the way. The platform team is responsible for the availability of the service, and the application teams are responsible only for the content of their databases.

The head of the platform team wants to publish in the service catalogue a technology-layer model that shows which technology service is used by which applications and through which access point. The internal layout of the cluster should not be in it, because it will change next year.
question: Which model best suits the head of the platform team?
options: The Node "PostgreSQL cluster" is assigned (assignment) to the Technology Function "Database operation", which realizes the Technology Service "Database as a service". The Technology Interface "Connection endpoint" is part of the node and is assigned to the service, which serves (serving) the Application Components "Resident Registry", "Parking System" and "Records Management".

The Node "PostgreSQL cluster" serves (serving) the Application Components "Resident Registry", "Parking System" and "Records Management" directly. The technology service and the connection endpoint do not appear separately in the model; their description is given in the node's documentation, which is attached to the service catalogue as a text appendix.

The Node "PostgreSQL cluster" is assigned (assignment) to the Technology Function "Database operation", which realizes (realization) the Technology Service "Database as a service" with the Technology Interface "Connection endpoint" assigned to it. Serving relationships lead from the applications Resident Registry, Parking System and Records Management to this technology service.

The Node "PostgreSQL cluster" is assigned (assignment) to the applications Resident Registry, Parking System and Records Management, which run on it. The Technology Service "Database as a service" realizes (realization) the individual Application Components, and the connection endpoint is an Application Interface that the cluster provides to the applications.
explanation: A technology service realized by a node's function and made available through a Technology Interface is exactly what a service catalogue needs: applications depend on the service (serving), not on specific servers, and the inside of the cluster stays hidden (5). A direct serving relationship from the node to the applications is a valid derived relationship, but it lacks the service and the access point that the catalogue is meant to publish (3). A reversed serving relationship claims that applications provide functionality to the database service – the opposite of the real dependency (1). The 0-point option models the deployment of applications with an assignment relationship from the node to the components and the realization of the components by a technology service, which ArchiMate 3.2 does not permit (a component is realized by an artifact).

image.alt: ArchiMate generic metamodel: internal and external active structure, internal behavior, service, event and passive structure with the relationships assigned to, realizes, serves, accesses, triggers/flows to and composed of.

scenario:
The Kamenice University Hospital is acquiring a second magnetic resonance imaging machine. The existing MR scanner is installed in a shielded room in Pavilion C, whose floors underwent structural reinforcement because of the weight of the machine. The scanner is operated by a control workstation – a computer supplied by the manufacturer as part of the machine, on which the control software runs. Pavilion C stands in the hospital campus on Kamenny Hill; the new machine will be located in a new Pavilion E in the same campus.

The technical director is preparing an investment proposal and needs a model in the spirit of the Physical viewpoint, from which it will be clear what is the physical machine and what is IT hardware, in which building the machine is installed (because of shielding and structural load) and where the buildings are located. They do not require clinical processes or image-handling applications in this model.
question: Which model best matches the technical director's needs?
options: The Equipment "MR scanner" is composed, among other things, of the Device "MR control workstation", on which the System Software "MR control software" runs (assignment). The Facility "Pavilion C" contains (composition) the Equipment "MR scanner", and the Location "Kamenny Hill campus" aggregates (aggregation) both the Facility "Pavilion C" and the planned Facility "Pavilion E".

The Equipment "MR scanner" is composed (composition), among other things, of the Device "MR control workstation", on which the System Software "MR control software" runs (assignment). Pavilion C is a Location "Pavilion C", which aggregates (aggregation) the Equipment "MR scanner", and the Location "Kamenny Hill campus" aggregates the Location "Pavilion C" and the planned Location "Pavilion E" for the new machine.

The Equipment "MR scanner" is composed (composition) of the Application Component "MR control workstation", which controls the machine and stores its settings. The Facility "Pavilion C" contains (composition) the Equipment "MR scanner", and the Location "Kamenny Hill campus" aggregates (aggregation) both the Facility "Pavilion C" and the planned Facility "Pavilion E" for the new machine.

The MR scanner is a Business Actor "MR unit" assigned (assignment) to the Location "Pavilion C", where the machine is installed in a shielded room. The control workstation is a Material that the unit accesses (access) during every examination, and the hospital campus is a Facility "Kamenny Hill campus" composed (composition) of the business actors based there, including the future unit in Pavilion E.
explanation: A physical machine is Equipment, a computer with control software is a Device (IT hardware) that can be part of the machine, a building with shielding and reinforced structure is a Facility, and the campus is a Location that aggregates the buildings (5). Modelling the pavilion as a Location is valid, but a Location is just a place, whereas a Facility is a physical structure with properties (shielding, structural load), which is what the technical director cares about (3). The control workstation as an Application Component confuses hardware with an application, and ArchiMate does not permit the composition of an application component in Equipment (1). The 0-point option models the machine as a business actor, the computer as material and the campus as a building composed of actors – it completely misses the distinction between physical and IT elements.
