scenario:
The pharmaceutical distributor FarmaLog supplies pharmacies from its central warehouse in Jihlava via regional transshipment hubs in Brno and Ostrava. Between the central warehouse and the two hubs run the company's own refrigerated trucks along the D1 motorway; in addition, part of the shipments to Ostrava travel by rail. The medicines are carried in thermoboxes that maintain a temperature of 2–8 °C. The warehouse and the hubs are buildings equipped with cooling chambers. The company operates 25 trucks and delivers over 40,000 shipments a year.

The logistics director wants a model of physical distribution that shows the logical connections between the warehouses, the physical transport networks that realize these connections, what the medicines are transported by and what is actually being transported. The model is to serve as a basis for assessing the impact of a planned several-week closure of part of the D1 motorway on the supply of both regions.
question: Which model best serves the logistics director?
options: The Facilities "Central warehouse Jihlava", "Hub Brno" and "Hub Ostrava" are connected by two Paths. The Distribution Network "D1 road" realizes (realization) both paths, and the Distribution Network "Railway" additionally realizes the path to Ostrava. The trucks are Equipment assigned (assignment) to the Technology Process "Refrigerated transport", which accesses (access) the Material "Medicines".

The Facilities "Central warehouse Jihlava", "Hub Brno" and "Hub Ostrava" are connected by two Paths, both of which are realized (realization) by a single Distribution Network "Transport network" comprising both roads and railway. The trucks are Equipment assigned (assignment) to the Technology Process "Refrigerated transport", which accesses (access) the Material "Medicines".

The Facilities "Central warehouse Jihlava", "Hub Brno" and "Hub Ostrava" are connected by two Paths. The Communication Network "D1 road" realizes (realization) both paths, and the Communication Network "Railway" additionally realizes the path to Ostrava. The trucks are Equipment assigned (assignment) to the Technology Process "Refrigerated transport", which accesses (access) the Material "Medicines".

The medicines are a Business Object assigned (assignment) to the trucks, which are modelled as Devices with thermoboxes as their parts. The trucks realize (realization) the paths between the warehouses, and the warehouses are Locations aggregated (aggregation) into the Distribution Network "D1 road"; the railway is modelled similarly.
explanation: The logical connection over which material is transported is a Path, and the physical transport infrastructures (road, railway) that realize it are Distribution Networks; vehicles are Equipment performing the technology process of transport, and the medicines are Material (5). Merging road and railway into a single distribution network is valid, but it loses precisely the distinction that is key to assessing the D1 closure (3). A Communication Network serves to transfer data, not material, so it is the wrong type of element for a transport network (1). The 0-point option confuses physical material with business information assigned to vehicles and lets equipment realize paths, which ArchiMate does not permit.

image.alt: Four ArchiMate physical elements with icons: Equipment, Facility, Distribution Network and Material.

scenario:
The public transport company of the city of Lipnik has equipped 600 buses with contactless card validators. A validator is a small computer with the Embedded Linux operating system, on which runs a ticketing application delivered as the installation package validator-app 4.2. The validators are mounted in the buses, but during repairs they are routinely moved to a different vehicle. They communicate with the central ticketing system over the LTE mobile network. The new application version 5.0 requires a newer version of the operating system, which only some of the validators have so far. Distribution is handled by a small team that can service at most 50 vehicles a week.

The head of IT is planning a gradual distribution of the new version, vehicle by vehicle. They need a model that shows which validator is in which vehicle, which system software and which application version run on it, and by what route the validator communicates with the central system.
question: Which model best serves the planning of the new version's distribution?
options: The Equipment "Bus" aggregates (aggregation) the Device "Validator", on which the System Software "Embedded Linux" runs (assignment); the Artifact "validator-app 4.2", which realizes the Application Component "Ticketing application", is deployed (assignment) directly on it. The Communication Network "LTE network" realizes the Path between the validators and the Node "Central ticketing system".

The Equipment "Bus" aggregates (aggregation) the Device "Validator", on which the Artifact "validator-app 4.2" realizing (realization) the Application Component "Ticketing application" is deployed (assignment) directly; the validator's operating system does not appear separately in the model. The Communication Network "LTE network" realizes the Path between the validators and the Node "Central ticketing system".

The Equipment "Bus" aggregates (aggregation) the Device "Validator", on which the System Software "Embedded Linux" runs (assignment); an assignment relationship leads from it to the Application Component "Ticketing application" in version 4.2, without an artifact. The Communication Network "LTE network" realizes (realization) the Path between the validators and the Node "Central ticketing system".

The validator is Equipment, of which the Artifact "validator-app 4.2", which realizes (realization) the Application Component "Ticketing application", is a part (composition); the Embedded Linux operating system is given in an attribute of the validator. The LTE network is a Path realized by the validators themselves, and the bus is a Business Actor to which the validators are assigned (assignment) by the vehicle's registration number.
explanation: A validator is a Device on which System Software runs, and the deployment of the application is expressed by an artifact deployed (assignment) on the system software that realizes the application component; the bus is Equipment (a vehicle) that aggregates the validator – aggregation without existence dependency matches the fact that a validator can be moved; communication is shown by a Path realized by the LTE network (5). Deploying the artifact directly on the device is valid, but it omits the operating system, on whose version the distribution depends (3). An assignment relationship from system software directly to an application component is not permitted by ArchiMate 3.2 – what is deployed is the artifact that realizes the component (1). The 0-point option composes a device from an artifact, lets a device realize a path and confuses a vehicle with a business actor.

image.alt: Deployment chain: a node composed of a device and system software, system software assigned to an artifact, and the artifact realizing an application component and a data object.

scenario:
The logistics company TransMorava backs up the database of its transport system every night at 1:00. The backup is performed by the BackupPro backup software installed on a backup server: it reads the database's data files from the database server and creates a backup set from them, which it stores on a disk array. After the backup finishes, BackupPro verifies the integrity of the set and sends a report to the administrators. Both the backup server and the database server are located in the company's data centre. Last year a test restore showed that some of the backups were unreadable, so the integrity verification step was added.

At the ISO/IEC 27001 certification audit the security manager has to demonstrate how backup works. They need a technology-layer model that shows what triggers the backup, who performs it, what steps it consists of and in what order they take place, and which artifacts are read and which are created.
question: Which model best serves the security manager at the audit?
options: The Technology Event "Daily at 1:00" triggers (triggering) the Technology Process "Nightly backup", to which the System Software "BackupPro" is assigned (assignment). The process is composed (composition) of the steps "Creating the backup set" and "Integrity verification" connected by a triggering relationship; the first step reads (access) the Artifact "DB data files" and writes the Artifact "Backup set".

The System Software "BackupPro", deployed on the Node "Backup server", is assigned (assignment) to the Technology Function "Backup", which reads (access) the Artifact "DB data files" and writes the Artifact "Backup set". The function also includes the integrity verification of the backup; the start time and the order of the steps are given only in the backup operating documentation.

The Application Event "Daily at 1:00" triggers (triggering) the Application Process "Nightly backup", to which the Application Component "BackupPro" is assigned (assignment). The process is composed (composition) of the steps "Creating the backup set" and "Integrity verification" connected by a triggering relationship; the first step reads (access) the Data Object "DB data files" and writes the Data Object "Backup set".

The Artifact "Backup script" triggers (triggering) the Node "Database server", and the Artifact "DB data files" is assigned (assignment) to the Technology Process "Nightly backup", which thereby performs it. The backup set is a Technology Event that arises when the backup on the disk array finishes, ends the process and sends the report to the administrators. The integrity verification is recorded in an attribute of the set.
explanation: The scheduled start is a Technology Event, the backup is performed by System Software assigned to a Technology Process whose steps are connected by a triggering relationship, and access relationships to artifacts show what is read and what is created – exactly what the audit requires (5). The model with a Technology Function is valid, but the trigger is missing from it and a function does not express the order of steps, which the auditor asks about (3). Modelling backup in the application layer with data objects is a layer error: it is an infrastructure operations job over files, that is, artifacts (1). The 0-point option lets passive artifacts trigger a node and perform behaviour and confuses the resulting artifact with an event, which ArchiMate does not permit.

scenario:
The pension company Klidne stari must, under the DORA regulation, demonstrate what its critical activities depend on. One of them is the monthly payment of pensions. The business process "Pension payment" uses the application service "Payment calculation", which is provided by the pension management system PensionCore; the calculation is performed by its benefit calculation function. PensionCore is deployed as the package pensioncore.ear on the JBoss application server, which runs on the APP cluster. PensionCore processes participants' account data as the data object "Participant account", physically stored in the database table ACCOUNTS; from the business point of view it is the business object "Participant account".

The auditor wants to see a complete, unabridged chain of dependencies from the business process through the application layer down to the technology, including how the account information is realized in the individual layers.
question: Which model best meets the auditor's requirement?
options: The process "Pension payment" is served (serving) by the Application Service "Payment calculation", which is realized by the Application Function "Benefit calculation" performed (assignment) by the component "PensionCore". The component is realized by the Artifact "pensioncore.ear" deployed on the System Software "JBoss", which runs on the Node "APP cluster". The Artifact "ACCOUNTS" realizes the Data Object "Participant account", which realizes the Business Object of the same name.

The Node "APP cluster" serves (serving) the Business Process "Pension payment" and the Artifact "ACCOUNTS" realizes (realization) the Business Object "Participant account". Both relationships are validly derived from the detailed model, so PensionCore, its service and function, the artifact pensioncore.ear and the data object are not shown separately in the auditor's view.

The Technology Service "JBoss runtime environment" realizes (realization) the Business Process "Pension payment" and is realized (realization) by the node "APP cluster", on which JBoss runs. The Artifact "ACCOUNTS" realizes the Data Object "Participant account", which realizes the Business Object of the same name; the PensionCore system does not appear separately in the process's chain of dependencies.

The Business Object "Participant account" realizes (realization) the Data Object "Participant account" and that realizes the Artifact "ACCOUNTS" in the cluster's database. An assignment relationship leads from the Artifact "pensioncore.ear" to the Node "APP cluster", and the Application Component "PensionCore" is assigned (assignment) to the Business Process "Pension payment", which it thus performs itself, including the benefit calculation.
explanation: The auditor requires the complete chain, so the 5-point model shows every layer: the process is served by an application service realized by a function of the component, the component is realized by an artifact deployed on the system software of the node, and the information is realized from the table through the data object up to the business object. Derived relationships (a node serves the process, an artifact realizes a business object) are valid, but they omit exactly the intermediate layers the auditor wants to see (3). Realization of a business process by a technology service is not permitted in ArchiMate 3.2 and in addition skips the application that exists in the scenario (1). The 0-point option reverses the direction of realization between layers, assigns the artifact to the node the wrong way round and uses the assignment of a component to a business process from ArchiMate 2.

image.alt: Example of cross-layer links: a technology service serves an application component, an application service serves a business process, a data object realizes a business object, and artifacts realize the data object and the application component.

scenario:
The mobile operator TeleNova manages customer data. From the business point of view it works with the information "Customer" (name, address, national ID number, tariff). In the CRM system this information is kept as a customer record that the CRM works with; physically it resides in the CUSTOMER table of an Oracle database on the DB-PROD cluster. In addition, every new customer signs a paper registration form, which is archived at the branch.

The data protection officer is preparing records of processing activities and responses to data subject requests. They need a model that shows, for the information "Customer", in which application it is processed and where it is physically stored, so that the whole chain can be traversed from the business concept through the logical level to the physical storage and back, and that also captures the paper form.
question: Which model best matches the officer's needs?
options: The Representation "Registration form" and the Data Object "Customer record" both realize (realization) the Business Object "Customer"; the Application Component "CRM" accesses (access) the data object. The Artifact "CUSTOMER table", deployed (assignment) on the System Software "Oracle DB" on the Node "DB-PROD", realizes the Data Object "Customer record".

The Artifact "CUSTOMER table" realizes (realization) the Business Object "Customer", as does the Representation "Registration form"; the Application Component "CRM" accesses (access) the business object. The artifact is deployed (assignment) on the System Software "Oracle DB" on the Node "DB-PROD"; the Data Object "Customer record" does not appear separately in the model.

The Representation "Registration form" realizes (realization) the Business Object "Customer". The CUSTOMER table is modelled as a Data Object that realizes (realization) this Business Object, and the customer record in the CRM as an Artifact that realizes the Data Object and that the Application Component "CRM" accesses (access).

The Business Object "Customer" realizes (realization) the Data Object "Customer record", which in turn realizes (realization) the Artifact "CUSTOMER table". The registration form is a Business Interface to which the Business Object "Customer" is assigned (assignment), and the CRM is a Node in the DB-PROD cluster on which the data runs.
explanation: The conceptual, logical and physical levels of information are linked in ArchiMate by realization going upwards: an artifact realizes a data object, which realizes a business object, and the paper form is a Representation of the same business object – the officer can thus traverse the chain in both directions (5). Direct realization of a business object by an artifact is a valid derived relationship, but it omits the logical level of the data object that the application works with (3). Swapping the types – the table as a Data Object and the CRM record as an Artifact – confuses the logical and physical levels (1). The 0-point option reverses the direction of realization between layers, confuses a form with an interface and an application with a node.

image.alt: Example of cross-layer links: a technology service serves an application component, an application service serves a business process, a data object realizes a business object, and artifacts realize the data object and the application component.

scenario:
The Labour Office is introducing a new housing allowance agenda, in which it processes over 120,000 applications a year. The business process "Allowance application processing" has three steps. Entitlement verification runs completely automatically: the agenda system itself queries the basic registers, calculates the entitlement and stores the result. The decision is issued by a clerk, to whom the agenda system offers the application service "Decision proposal" with pre-filled text. Payment is carried out without human intervention by the payment system in a nightly batch.

The process owner at the ministry wants a model from which it will be clear which steps are fully automated and by which application, and which are performed by a human supported by an application service. The model is to be used to evaluate the degree of digitalisation of the agenda and will be updated with every further stage of automation; within two years the ministry wants to automate decision-making in simple cases as well.
question: Which model best matches the process owner's requirement?
options: The step "Entitlement verification" is realized (realization) by the Application Process "Automatic entitlement verification" of the agenda system, and the step "Payment" is realized by the Application Process "Batch payment" of the payment system. The Business Role "Clerk" is assigned (assignment) to the step "Decision", because a human decides, and the Application Service "Decision proposal" serves (serving) this step.

The step "Entitlement verification" is realized (realization) by the Application Process "Automatic entitlement verification" of the agenda system, and the step "Payment" is realized by the Application Process "Batch payment" of the payment system. A serving relationship leads to the step "Decision" from the Application Service "Decision proposal"; the model does not state who performs this step.

The step "Entitlement verification" is realized (realization) by the Application Service "Automatic entitlement verification" and the step "Payment" is realized by the Application Service "Batch payment". The Business Role "Clerk" is assigned (assignment) to the step "Decision" and the Application Service "Decision proposal" serves (serving) this step.

A realization relationship leads from the steps "Entitlement verification" and "Payment" to the Application Processes of the agenda and payment systems, because the steps determine what the systems are to do. The Business Role "Clerk" is assigned (assignment) to the Application Component "Agenda system", which they work with when deciding on entitlement.
explanation: Full automation of a step is expressed by application behaviour (an Application Process) that realizes the step, whereas support of human work is expressed by an application service that serves the step (serving), with a business role remaining assigned to the step – the 5-point model thus distinguishes both cases precisely. A model without the role captures the automation correctly, but for the decision it does not show that a human performs it, which is the second half of the concern (3). An application service cannot realize a business process – it can be realized by an application process, function or interaction, while a service only serves it; the key links are thus built on an impermissible relationship (1). The 0-point option reverses the direction of realization between layers and assigns a business role to an application component, which ArchiMate does not permit.

scenario:
The bank Krokus offers clients the business services "Payments" and "Payment card management" through three channels: at a branch, through a telephone line and, newly, in a mobile app. From the business point of view the mobile app is one of the bank's channels, equal to the branch and the telephone. Technically it is the user interface of the Mobile Banking system, which offers clients the application services "Payment entry" and "Card blocking". The share of clients served in the mobile app exceeded half this year for the first time, and the bank plans to add further services to the app gradually.

The sales channel manager wants a model that links the business view of the mobile channel with its application realization: through which application interface the channel is implemented and which application services are available in it to the client. They do not need to model the branch and the telephone line yet.
question: Which model best links the business and application views of the mobile channel?
options: The Business Interface "Mobile channel" is assigned (assignment) to the Business Services "Payments" and "Payment card management" and serves the role "Client". The Application Interface "Mobile app UI", part of the component "Mobile Banking", realizes (realization) this Business Interface and is assigned to the Application Services "Payment entry" and "Card blocking".

The Application Interface "Mobile app UI", part (composition) of the Application Component "Mobile Banking", is assigned (assignment) to the Application Services "Payment entry" and "Card blocking" and serves (serving) the Business Role "Client" directly. The Business Interface "Mobile channel" and the bank's business services do not appear in this model, because the channel is formed by the application itself.

The Business Interface "Mobile channel" is part (composition) of the Application Component "Mobile Banking" and is assigned (assignment) to the Business Services "Payments" and "Payment card management". The Application Services "Payment entry" and "Card blocking" serve (serving) the Business Role "Client", who uses the channel.

The Business Interface "Mobile channel" realizes (realization) the Application Interface "Mobile app UI". The Application Component "Mobile Banking" is assigned (assignment) to the Business Services "Payments" and "Payment card management", which it thus performs in place of bank staff at the branch and on the telephone line.
explanation: From the business point of view a channel is a Business Interface assigned to the services available through it, and its application implementation is expressed by realization of the Business Interface by an application interface, which in turn is assigned to the application services available in the channel (5). Direct serving of the role by the application interface is valid, but it lacks the link to the business channel and services that the channel manager needs (3). ArchiMate does not permit composing a business interface into an application component – layers are linked by realization and serving, not by composition (1). The 0-point option reverses the direction of realization between layers (the lower layer realizes the higher one) and assigns an application component to a business service, which the relationship tables do not permit.

scenario:
The insurance company Vltava Pojisteni has introduced automatic settlement of small travel insurance claims. The ClaimsAuto system checks the claim, calculates the payout and pays it out without human intervention. However, if the fraud score exceeds a set threshold, ClaimsAuto suspends processing and requests a manual review from an insurance fraud specialist; after their verdict the automatic processing continues. The specialists perform the reviews according to their own procedure and offer the same review as a service to other departments of the insurance company as well. The system processes around 30,000 claims a year, and roughly four percent of them end up in a manual review.

The solution architect wants to show explicitly in the model that the automated process depends on human work at a certain point, who performs this work and in what form it is provided to the automated process. The model will also serve for capacity planning of the specialist team.
question: Which model best captures the dependence of the automated processing on human work?
options: The Application Component "ClaimsAuto" is assigned to the Application Process "Automatic settlement". The Business Role "Insurance fraud specialist" performs (assignment) the Business Process "Suspicion review", which realizes the Business Service "Manual review of a suspicious event", and that serves (serving) this application process.

The Application Component "ClaimsAuto" is assigned to the Application Process "Automatic settlement". The Business Role "Insurance fraud specialist" serves (serving) this application process directly; the review procedure and the service that the specialists also offer to other departments do not appear in the model separately, to keep the model simple.

Model the manual review as the Application Function "Suspicion review" of the ClaimsAuto system, to which the Business Role "Insurance fraud specialist", who enters their verdict into the function, is also assigned (assignment). The function serves (serving) the Application Process "Automatic settlement", to which the Application Component "ClaimsAuto" is assigned.

The Business Process "Suspicion review" realizes (realization) the Application Process "Automatic settlement", because the review determines whether the settlement can continue. The Business Role "Insurance fraud specialist" is assigned (assignment) to the Application Component "ClaimsAuto", to which they thus pass their verdict on the suspicious claim.
explanation: Human work on which an automated process depends is modelled as a Business Service realized by a business process performed by a role; this service serves (serving) the application process – serving can also lead from the business layer to the application layer (5). A direct serving relationship from the role to the application process is valid, but it captures neither the form of provision (the service) that the architect asks about nor the specialists' procedure (3). Modelling the human review as an application function disguises the fact that it is performed by a human, and ArchiMate does not permit assigning a business role to application behaviour (1). The 0-point option reverses the direction of realization between layers and assigns a business role to an application component, which the relationship tables do not permit.

scenario:
The gas supplier Plyn Morava runs a customer line. Operators handle customers' calls using softphones connected to the company's IP PBX telephone exchange, which runs on two servers in the data centre. The calls themselves do not pass through any business application – the CRM is a separate system and is not integrated with telephony. The exchange provides voice connection, call forwarding and call recording; the line handles around 2,000 calls a day.

Within a year the company will replace its own exchange with a cloud telephony service from an external provider. The operations director wants a model that shows which business processes and roles depend on telephony, in such a way that when the exchange is replaced only the technology realization of telephony changes, not the links to the business. They do not want to include the application layer in the model, because the change does not concern it.
question: Which model best matches the operations director's requirement?
options: The Node "Telephone exchange" is assigned (assignment) to the Technology Function "Telephony", realizing the Technology Service "Voice connection", which directly serves (serving) the Business Process "Customer call handling". The Technology Interface "Softphone", assigned to the service, serves the Business Role "Customer line operator".

The Node "Telephone exchange" serves (serving) the Business Process "Customer call handling" and the Business Role "Customer line operator" directly. The technology service and interface do not appear in the model, because when the exchange is replaced by a cloud service it is enough to rename the node in the model to the new provider.

Model telephony as an Application Component "Telephony", whose Application Service "Voice connection" serves (serving) the Business Process "Customer call handling" and the role "Customer line operator". The component is realized by the Artifact "PBX software" deployed (assignment) on the Node "Telephone exchange" in the data centre.

The Business Role "Customer line operator" is assigned (assignment) to the Node "Telephone exchange", which they work with through a softphone on their computer, and the Business Process "Customer call handling" realizes (realization) the Technology Service "Voice connection", because it uses it in every call with a customer.
explanation: Technology can serve the business layer directly, without an application layer: a technology service serves the business process and a technology interface serves the business role; when the exchange is replaced by a cloud service only the realization of the service changes and the links to the business remain (5). A direct serving relationship from the node is a valid derived relationship, but it ties the business to a specific exchange, so replacing the realization cannot be separated from the links to the business (3). An invented application component for telephony is a layer error – in the scenario the calls pass through no application (1). The 0-point option assigns a business role to a node and lets a business process realize a technology service, which ArchiMate does not permit.

scenario:
The retail chain Potraviny Hvezda runs 40 applications. The architecture department has a detailed model in its repository: application components, their application functions, application services, interfaces and the links of the services to the company's business functions (Purchasing, Logistics, Sales, Marketing, Finance). The IT director is preparing a decision on portfolio rationalisation and needs a one-page map for the board showing which applications support which business functions, so that duplications are visible – for example three different applications supporting Marketing. The board members do not know the ArchiMate notation and will have only a few minutes at the presentation. The detailed model is up to date and the architects trust it.

The architect is to create from the repository a view that will be understandable to the board members and at the same time will be a correct ArchiMate model, that is, will contain only relationships that actually follow from the detailed model.
question: How should the architect build the view for the board?
options: Show only Application Components and Business Functions and connect them with serving relationships from the components to the functions, which are derived from the chain component –assignment→ application function –realization→ application service –serving→ business function. Leave the intermediate elements, that is, functions, services and interfaces, out of the view.

Show only Application Components and Business Functions and connect them with association relationships labelled "supports", which capture the connection without having to deal with a specific ArchiMate relationship type. Leave the intermediate application functions, services and interfaces out of the view so that the map is clear for the board.

Show only Application Components and Business Functions and connect them with assignment relationships from each component to the business functions it supports, because the component performs automated work for the business function. Leave the intermediate application functions, services and interfaces out of the view.

Show the Business Functions as wholes that include the applications supporting them, so that, for example, Marketing will contain three marketing applications. Draw serving relationships from the business functions to the applications that use them. Leave the intermediate application functions, services and interfaces out of the view.
explanation: Derived relationships are full-fledged ArchiMate relationships: from the chain assignment – realization – serving a valid serving relationship from the component to the business function follows (the structural chain yields realization, which combined with the dependency serving yields serving), so the compact view is correct and understandable to the board (5). Association is always permitted, but it expresses neither the direction nor the kind of support, so the view loses the meaning that follows from the detailed model (3). Assigning an application component to a business function is a construct from ArchiMate 2 that version 3 does not permit (1). The 0-point option nests applications in business functions, which the relationship tables do not permit, and reverses the direction of support.

image.alt: Example of relationship derivation: a role assigned to a process, the process realizes a service, the derived relationship role realizes service, and the order of strength of structural relationships.

scenario:
The e-shop Elektro Plus has launched an automated warehouse in Kolin. Order picking is no longer done by warehouse workers: the AutoGrid robotic system itself takes crates of goods out of the grid rack and brings them to a delivery station, where a packing machine packs them. The robotic system is controlled by the WMS warehouse system, which passes it picking instructions through its application service "Picking control". The business process "Order picking" is thus performed fully automatically; people only deal with faults and replenish stock. The warehouse picks around 15,000 orders a day and operates around the clock.

The operations director wants a model that shows that the business process is now realized by physical automation, not by people, what performs this automation, what it physically handles and which application controls it. The model will serve as a basis for the decision on automating the second warehouse.
question: Which model best suits the operations director?
options: The Equipment "AutoGrid robotic system" is assigned (assignment) to the Technology Process "Robotic picking", which realizes (realization) the Business Process "Order picking" and accesses (access) the Material "Goods". The Application Service "Picking control" of the WMS system serves this technology process.

The Equipment "AutoGrid robotic system" is assigned (assignment) to the Technology Process "Robotic picking", which realizes (realization) the Business Process "Order picking" and accesses (access) the Material "Goods". The WMS system, which passes instructions to the robots, does not appear in the model.

The Equipment "AutoGrid robotic system" is assigned (assignment) to the Business Process "Order picking", which it thus performs in place of warehouse workers, and accesses (access) the Material "Goods". The Application Service "Picking control" of the WMS system serves (serving) the robotic system and passes instructions to it.

The Business Process "Order picking" realizes (realization) the Technology Process "Robotic picking". The goods are a Business Object assigned (assignment) to the robotic system, and the WMS is Equipment composed (composition) of the individual robots and the packing machine, which it controls.
explanation: Physical automation of a business process is expressed by a technology process performed by equipment (Equipment), which realizes the business process and works with material; control by the WMS is shown by an application service serving the technology process (5). A model without the WMS captures the automation correctly, but it lacks the application that controls the robots, which the director explicitly asks about (3). ArchiMate does not permit assigning equipment directly to a business process – a performer from the technology layer is tied to business behaviour through its own technology behaviour and realization (1). The 0-point option reverses the direction of realization between layers, confuses physical goods with information and an application with equipment.

scenario:
The online bank FinPrime is subject to the Czech National Bank's outsourcing rules and must keep a record of where client data is processed and stored. The bank's back office is based in Brno, and the customer centre for the bank is operated by an external partner in Bratislava. The client database (the artifact klientska_db, which realizes the data object "Client data") runs on a database node in a cloud region in Frankfurt, and an analytics node with a copy of the data stands in a region in Dublin. The regulator asks in particular about data processed outside the Czech Republic.

The compliance officer wants a model that shows, across the business, application and technology layers, in which places the organisational units operate and where the nodes and artifacts with client data are located, so that they can answer the regulator's questions quickly. They want the places in the model as separate elements, not just as text in names.
question: Which model best serves the compliance officer?
options: The Locations "Brno", "Bratislava", "Frankfurt" and "Dublin" aggregate (aggregation) the elements located in them: the Business Actors "Back office" and "Customer centre (partner)", the Nodes "DB node" and "Analytics node" and the Artifact "klientska_db", which realizes (realization) the Data Object "Client data".

The Groupings "Czechia and Slovakia" and "Rest of the EU" aggregate (aggregation) the Business Actors "Back office" and "Customer centre (partner)", the Nodes "DB node" and "Analytics node" and the Artifact "klientska_db" realizing the Data Object "Client data"; the specific cities are given only in the textual documentation of the two groups.

Brno, Bratislava, Frankfurt and Dublin are Facilities that aggregate (aggregation) the Business Actors "Back office" and "Customer centre (partner)", the Nodes "DB node" and "Analytics node" and the Artifact "klientska_db", which realizes (realization) the Data Object "Client data".

The places are Business Roles "Brno", "Bratislava", "Frankfurt" and "Dublin", to which the organisational units and both nodes are assigned (assignment). The Data Object "Client data" realizes (realization) the Artifact "klientska_db", which is thus physically stored in Frankfurt.
explanation: A Location is a composite element that by aggregation groups elements of any layer by place – business actors, nodes and artifacts – and thus answers the question "where" directly (5). A Grouping is valid, but it has no meaning of place, and grouping by regions loses the specific locations the regulator asks about (3). A Facility is a physical structure (a building, a data centre), not a city, and the relationship tables do not permit aggregation of business actors or artifacts by a Facility (1). The 0-point option confuses places with business roles, assigns nodes to them and reverses the direction of realization between the data object and the artifact.

scenario:
Vltava Bank is preparing for a compliance inspection under the EU Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA). The head of internal audit requires a model that makes clear, for each regulatory requirement, which processes and applications fulfil it and how this contributes to the measurable outcome that the audit will verify at the end of the year.
The architect found the following: the bank has set the goal "Ensure DORA compliance" and, as the measure of success, "DORA compliance inspection for 2026 closed without a serious finding". From the regulation it derived specific requirements for its solutions, e.g. "Incidents are classified automatically according to DORA criteria" and "Contracts with ICT suppliers are kept in a central register". Incident classification is provided by the business process "ICT incident management" supported by the ServiceDesk Pro application, and the contract register will now be kept in the VendorHub application. The regulation itself is an external driver that motivates the bank to change.
question: Which model best matches the concern of the head of internal audit?
options: Associate the driver "DORA regulation" with the goal "Ensure DORA compliance". Both requirements –realization→ outcome "DORA inspection 2026 without a serious finding" –realization→ goal. The business process "ICT incident management" and the application component "ServiceDesk Pro" –realization→ the first requirement; the application component "VendorHub" –realization→ the second requirement.

Associate the driver "DORA regulation" with the goal "Ensure DORA compliance" and connect both requirements directly: requirement –realization→ goal. The business process "ICT incident management" and the application component "ServiceDesk Pro" –realization→ the first requirement; the application component "VendorHub" –realization→ the second requirement. State the measure of success only in the description of the goal.

Associate the driver "DORA regulation" with the goal "Ensure DORA compliance". Lead the refinement from top to bottom: goal –realization→ outcome "DORA inspection 2026 without a serious finding" –realization→ both requirements. The business process "ICT incident management" and the application components "ServiceDesk Pro" and "VendorHub" –realization→ the respective requirements.

Model the DORA regulation as a business object and the business process "ICT incident management" –access→ this object. Model both requirements as business services: the application components "ServiceDesk Pro" and "VendorHub" –realization→ these services, and capture DORA compliance as an attribute of the process. Leave out the motivation elements.
explanation: The audit needs traceability from processes and applications through requirements to a measurable outcome: the chain core element → requirement → outcome → goal, with realization relationships leading upwards to the more abstract intent, satisfies this exactly (5). The 3-point option is valid in ArchiMate 3.2 (realization from a requirement to a goal is permitted), but it lacks the outcome – precisely the measurable result that the audit verifies. The 1-point option has the correct links of the applications, but goal → outcome and outcome → requirement as realization are reversed and not permitted in 3.2 (only influence and association are allowed). The 0-point option converts motivation into passive structure and behaviour, so the link to the regulation and the goals disappears from the model entirely.

scenario:
The board of Horizont Insurance has launched a programme to digitalise claims settlement, and the supervisory board wants to see how the individual initiatives of the programme contribute to its goals. At a workshop with the chief executive the following statements were made, which the enterprise architect is to capture in a Goal Realization view:
(1) "Increase client satisfaction with claims settlement."
(2) "By the end of 2027 the average settlement time of a simple claim will fall below 5 days."
(3) "We enter client data only once and share it across all systems."
(4) "When a claim is reported, the new client portal automatically pre-fills the client's data from the client database."
(5) "The portal may be operated only in the insurance company's private cloud."
The chief executive wants to be able to read from the model what is a general rule for the whole company, what concerns a specific system, what is a measurable result and what merely restricts the realization, and how the statements contribute to one another.
question: Which capture of the statements best matches ArchiMate 3.2 and the chief executive's concern?
options: (1) goal, (2) outcome, (3) principle, (4) requirement and (5) constraint. Realization leads upwards: requirement (4) –realization→ principle (3) –realization→ outcome (2) –realization→ goal (1). The constraint is associated with the portal's requirement, whose realization it restricts.

(1) goal, (2) outcome, (3) principle, and statements (4) and (5) as two requirements. Realization leads upwards: requirement (4) –realization→ principle (3) –realization→ outcome (2) –realization→ goal (1). Requirement (5) is associated with requirement (4), because it concerns the same portal.

(1) goal, (2) outcome, (3) requirement, (4) principle and (5) constraint. Realization leads upwards: requirement (3) –realization→ principle (4) –realization→ outcome (2) –realization→ goal (1). The constraint (5) is associated with the principle (4), whose realization it restricts.

Model all five statements as requirements and one goal "Digital claims settlement" –aggregation→ these requirements. Further, stakeholder "Chief executive" –realization→ goal, and order the requirements by priority with triggering relationships.
explanation: A principle is a general rule valid for all systems in a given context, a requirement describes a property of a specific system, an outcome is a measurable and time-bound result, and a constraint restricts the way of realization (hence it is only associated with the portal's requirement); realization leads upwards requirement → principle → outcome → goal (5). Capturing operation in the private cloud as an ordinary requirement is acceptable, because a constraint is its specialisation, but the distinction between a required property and a restriction, which the director explicitly asks about, is lost (3). Swapping principle and requirement does use valid relationships, but the general rule and the requirement for a specific portal get the wrong types, so the model claims the opposite of reality (1). The 0-point option uses neither outcome nor principle and contains impermissible relationships: 3.2 permits neither stakeholder –realization→ goal nor goal –aggregation→ requirement, and triggering between requirements does not exist.

scenario: The online shop Domov a Hobby, which sells supplies for the house and garden, lost a quarter of its regular customers over the past year. The chief executive and the head of logistics want to see, even before setting goals, a Stakeholder view that captures what is troubling them and why. Interviews showed that the executive is interested primarily in profitability and customer satisfaction, and the head of logistics in delivery speed. An internal analysis found that we deliver orders in 3 days on average, whereas the main competitor delivers by the next day (a weakness), and that our own warehouse in Brno has 30% free capacity (a strength). An external influence that none of the internal stakeholders owns is the arrival of large foreign marketplaces on the Czech market, which puts pressure on both prices and delivery speed (a threat). Management is considering the goal "Speed up delivery" and wants the view to make clear which findings this goal is based on.
question: Which model best captures the situation in the Stakeholder view?
options: Associate the stakeholders "Chief executive" and "Head of logistics" with the drivers "Profitability", "Customer satisfaction" and "Delivery speed"; leave the external driver "Marketplace arrival" without a stakeholder. Model the findings of the analysis (slow delivery, free warehouse capacity, marketplace price pressure) as assessments associated with the respective drivers. Associate the goal "Speed up delivery" with the assessments it is based on.

Associate the stakeholders "Chief executive" and "Head of logistics" with the drivers "Profitability", "Customer satisfaction" and "Delivery speed" and add the external driver "Marketplace arrival". Reflect the results of the analysis directly in the names of the drivers, for example "Slow delivery compared with the competition" or "Free capacity of the Brno warehouse". Then associate the goal "Speed up delivery" directly with these drivers.

Model the chief executive and the head of logistics as business actors associated with the drivers "Profitability", "Customer satisfaction" and "Delivery speed". Model the findings of the analysis (slow delivery, free warehouse capacity, marketplace price pressure) as assessments associated with the respective drivers, including the external driver "Marketplace arrival". Associate the goal "Speed up delivery" with the assessments.

Model the arrival of foreign marketplaces as a business event "Marketplace entry" –triggering→ business process "Delivery acceleration". Store the results of the analysis (slow delivery, free warehouse capacity) as a business object "SWOT analysis", which the process accesses (access), and assign the chief executive and the head of logistics to the process as business roles responsible for the change.
explanation: A Stakeholder view is meant to show the stakeholders, their concerns expressed as drivers, and the results of analysis (assessments, typically a SWOT), only after which goals follow; an external driver need not have a stakeholder – the 5-point model satisfies this. The 3-point option is valid, but it merges a driver with the result of the analysis, so the answer to the question "why", which management wants to see, is lost. The 1-point option has the assessments right, but models the stakeholders as business actors; a stakeholder is a motivation element, and an actor could at most be assigned to it by an assignment relationship. The 0-point option converts motivation into behaviour and passive structure of the business layer, so the stakeholder analysis is not in the model at all.

scenario: St Luke's Hospital is considering mobile access for doctors to medical records. The deputy director for medical care is pushing the requirement "A doctor has access to a patient's records from a mobile device", which in their view will contribute significantly to the goal "Increase the quality and speed of care". The data protection officer points out that the same requirement increases the risk of data leakage and thus partly threatens the goal "Protect the confidentiality of patient data". They therefore propose adding the requirement "Mobile access only with multi-factor authentication", which would strengthen confidentiality but slightly delay doctors at every login. The hospital director will decide on the proposal at a management meeting, where the two stakeholders defend different interests. They therefore want a single view in which all positive and negative contributions of both requirements to both goals are visible, so that they can assess the conflicts and their balancing.
question: Which way of modelling best matches the director's concern?
options: Requirement "Mobile access" –influence→ goal "Quality and speed of care" positively and goal "Data confidentiality" negatively. Requirement "Multi-factor authentication" –influence→ "Data confidentiality" positively and "Quality and speed of care" negatively. Associate both goals with the stakeholders who push them, so that the conflict of their interests is also visible.

Requirement "Mobile access" –influence→ goal "Quality and speed of care" positively and goal "Data confidentiality" negatively. Requirement "Multi-factor authentication" –realization→ "Data confidentiality", because it directly fulfils it; mention its impact on the speed of care only in the documentation of the requirement.

Requirement "Mobile access" –realization→ goal "Quality and speed of care" and requirement "Multi-factor authentication" –realization→ goal "Data confidentiality". Express the conflicts by a negative influence relationship led from the threatened goal to the threatening requirement, that is, "Data confidentiality" –influence→ "Mobile access" negatively. Associate both goals with the stakeholders.

Model the data protection officer's objection as a business event "Risk warning" –triggering→ requirement "Multi-factor authentication". Further, "Mobile access" –flow→ both goals, with the flow label stating whether the contribution helps or harms. Do not include stakeholders, because the conflicts arise from the requirements, not from people.
explanation: Influence is intended precisely for partial positive and negative contributions to motivation elements, and the sign (+/−) makes visible the conflicts of both requirements with both goals, which the director needs (5). The 3-point option is valid, but for multi-factor authentication it lacks its negative impact on the speed of care, so one of the two conflicts remains hidden. The 1-point option uses permitted relationships, but draws the negative influence the wrong way round – from the goal to the requirement – so the model does not say which requirement threatens the goal. The 0-point option models motivation as behaviour: ArchiMate 3.2 permits neither triggering from a business event to a requirement nor flow from a requirement to a goal.

scenario: The transport company Parcela Logistics, which delivers over 100,000 shipments a day, is preparing its strategy for 2027–2029. The chief strategy officer wants a two-level capability map that shows, for each capability, what ensures it in operation today, so that they can decide where to invest; the budget allows strengthening at most two areas. The capability "Shipment management" consists of the capabilities "Shipment tracking" and "Route planning". Shipment tracking is currently ensured in operation by the business function "Dispatching" with the Track&Trace application, route planning by the business function "Transport planning" with the optimisation application RouteOpt. For route planning, the vehicle fleet of 450 vans owned by the company is also essential. The officer explicitly wants to see the applications too, because most of the investments under consideration are aimed at IT and both applications are over ten years old.
question: Which model best supports the chief strategy officer's decision-making?
options: Compose (composition) the capability "Shipment management" of the capabilities "Shipment tracking" and "Route planning". The business function "Dispatching" and the application component "Track&Trace" –realization→ "Shipment tracking"; the business function "Transport planning" and the application component "RouteOpt" –realization→ "Route planning". The resource "Vehicle fleet" –assignment→ capability "Route planning", because it is essential for it.

Compose (composition) the capability "Shipment management" of the capabilities "Shipment tracking" and "Route planning". The business function "Dispatching" –realization→ "Shipment tracking" and the business function "Transport planning" –realization→ "Route planning". Leave the applications Track&Trace and RouteOpt and the vehicle fleet for the detailed views of the individual departments, so that the map remains clear.

Compose (composition) the capability "Shipment management" of the capabilities "Shipment tracking" and "Route planning". Express the link to operations by a serving relationship led from the capability: "Shipment tracking" –serving→ "Dispatching" and "Track&Trace", "Route planning" –serving→ "Transport planning" and "RouteOpt". The resource "Vehicle fleet" –assignment→ capability "Route planning".

Model the capabilities as business functions: compose "Shipment management" of the business functions "Shipment tracking" and "Route planning". Assign (assignment) the application components "Track&Trace" and "RouteOpt" to these business functions and add the fleet of 450 vans as a business object, which "Route planning" accesses when calculating routes.
explanation: Capabilities express what the company is able to do, and they are realized by operational elements – business functions as well as applications – while resources are assigned to capabilities by an assignment relationship; the map in the 5-point model thus shows exactly what the officer is deciding on. The 3-point option is valid, but it omits the applications, although most of the investment is aimed at them, and also the vehicle fleet. The 1-point option has the correct hierarchy, but ArchiMate 3.2 does not permit serving from a capability to a business function or application component (only association) and it reverses the sense – a capability is realized by operations, it does not serve them. The 0-point option does not model capabilities at all, and assigning an application component to a business function is a construct that 3.2 does not permit.

scenario: Moravian Mortgage Bank came sixth out of eight banks in an independent survey of clients' mortgage experience and wants to change that. The business architect is preparing for the board a Value Stream view "Obtain a mortgage" from the client's perspective. The value stream has the stages "Choose an offer", "Submit an application", "Assess and approve" and "Draw the loan"; a work-in-progress application and supporting documents are passed between the stages. The capability "Credit risk assessment" is key for the assessment stage, and "Loan account management" for the drawdown stage. The stage "Assess and approve" is currently ensured in operation by the business processes "Property valuation" and "Loan approval". The board wants to see what value the stream brings the client ("home ownership with certainty of repayment"), which capabilities enable the individual stages and what ensures them in operation today. The board will have only a quarter of an hour at the meeting, so it wants to see everything in a single view.
question: Which model best matches the board's requirement?
options: Compose (composition) the value stream "Obtain a mortgage" of four value streams representing the stages, with flow relationships between them. Capability "Credit risk assessment" –serving→ stage "Assess and approve", capability "Loan account management" –serving→ stage "Draw the loan", processes "Property valuation" and "Loan approval" –realization→ stage "Assess and approve". Associate the value "Home ownership with certainty of repayment" with the value stream and with the stakeholder "Client".

Compose (composition) the value stream "Obtain a mortgage" of four value streams representing the stages, with flow relationships between them. Capability "Credit risk assessment" –serving→ stage "Assess and approve", capability "Loan account management" –serving→ stage "Draw the loan"; processes "Property valuation" and "Loan approval" –realization→ stage "Assess and approve". Do not include the value for the client or the client itself in the view, because according to the architect they follow from the name of the stream.

Compose (composition) the value stream "Obtain a mortgage" of four value streams representing the stages, with flow relationships between them; capability "Credit risk assessment" –serving→ stage "Assess and approve", capability "Loan account management" –serving→ stage "Draw the loan". Stage "Assess and approve" –composition→ business processes "Property valuation" and "Loan approval". Associate the value "Home ownership with certainty of repayment" with the value stream and with the stakeholder "Client".

Model "Obtain a mortgage" as a business process composed of four subprocesses "Choose an offer", "Submit an application", "Assess and approve" and "Draw the loan" connected by triggering relationships. Capabilities "Credit risk assessment" and "Loan account management" –assignment→ the assessment and drawdown subprocesses, nest (composition) the processes "Property valuation" and "Loan approval" in the assessment subprocess, and capture the value for the client as the business object "Mortgage contract".
explanation: In ArchiMate 3.2 a value stream is divided into stages (value streams joined by composition and connected by flow relationships), serving leads from capabilities to stages, realization from business processes to stages, and the value together with the stakeholder expresses the client's perspective – exactly what the board wants (5). The 3-point option is valid, but it omits the value and the client, that is, precisely the perspective for which the value stream is created. The 1-point option composes a strategic stage of operational processes; 3.2 does not permit composition from a value stream to a business process (only association), and the link should be realization from the process to the stage. The 0-point option confuses a value stream with a business process and assigns a capability to a process by an assignment relationship that does not exist.

scenario: The energy distributor EnerMorava has approved the strategy "Digital first": over three years to move most customer contacts to digital self-service. Part of the strategy is the short-term tactic "Discount for electronic invoicing", which is meant to motivate customers to switch quickly. The strategy is to be enabled by the capabilities "Digital customer service" and "Customer data analytics", which rest on the resources "Customer data platform" and "Team of digital specialists". The supervisory board is sceptical, because the previous digitalisation project did not deliver the promised savings, and asks mainly about measurable results: "60% of meter readings reported online by 2028" and "Customer line costs lower by 25%". Both results are to contribute to the goal "Reduce customer service costs". The chief strategy officer wants to defend the strategy with a model that links the strategy, capabilities, resources and results; the model will be part of the materials for the supervisory board's December meeting.
question: Which model best links the strategy with capabilities, resources and results?
options: Model "Digital first" as a course of action that aggregates the tactic "Discount for electronic invoicing" (also a course of action). The capabilities "Digital customer service" and "Customer data analytics" –realization→ "Digital first" and the resources –assignment→ these capabilities. Further, "Digital first" –realization→ both outcomes –realization→ goal "Reduce customer service costs".

Model "Digital first" as a course of action that aggregates the tactic "Discount for electronic invoicing" (also a course of action). The capabilities "Digital customer service" and "Customer data analytics" –realization→ "Digital first" and the resources –assignment→ these capabilities. Further, "Digital first" –realization→ the goal "Reduce customer service costs" directly, and the target values 60% and 25% are given in its description.

Model "Digital first" as a course of action that aggregates the tactic "Discount for electronic invoicing". Further, "Digital first" –realization→ the capabilities "Digital customer service" and "Customer data analytics" and the resources –assignment→ these capabilities. Finally, "Digital first" –realization→ both outcomes –realization→ goal "Reduce customer service costs".

Model "Digital first" as a work package (programme) and the tactic as its sub-work package starting next quarter. Model the capabilities as deliverables of the programme (deliverable –realization→ goal "Reduce customer service costs") and write the target values 60% and 25% into the description of the programme.
explanation: A course of action is an approach to configuring capabilities and resources: the realization relationship leads from capabilities to the course of action, resources are assigned to capabilities (assignment), and from the course of action realization leads to outcomes and from them to the goal – the supervisory board thus sees the measurable results of the strategy (5). The 3-point option is valid, but it omits the outcomes and hides the measurable results in the description, although the supervisory board asks about them most. The 1-point option reverses the key relationship: 3.2 does not permit realization from a course of action to a capability; it should lead from capabilities to the course of action. The 0-point option confuses strategy with a programme and capabilities with project outputs, that is, elements of the Implementation & Migration layer instead of strategic ones.

scenario: A regional airport currently handles only aircraft with a capacity of up to 180 passengers and wants to acquire the capability "Wide-body aircraft handling", so that it can attract long-haul charter flights. The airport director needs to know which resources are critical for this capability and what ensures it in real operation, so that they can plan investments in the order of tens of millions of crowns and negotiate financing with the region. The analysis identified three resources: "Handling equipment for large aircraft", which in operation consists of specific machines (an aircraft tug, a pallet loader, tall stairs), "Qualified handling staff", who are the employees of the Ground Handling department, and "Handling authorisation", which exists in the form of a permit from the aviation authority. The director wants to be able to read from the model what the airport must buy, whom to train and which permit to extend; the previous textual studies did not capture this link and quickly became outdated.
question: Which model best matches the airport director's concern?
options: The resources "Handling equipment", "Qualified staff" and "Handling authorisation" –assignment→ capability "Wide-body aircraft handling". Further, the equipment "Aircraft tug", "Pallet loader" and "Tall stairs" –realization→ "Handling equipment", the business actor "Ground Handling" –realization→ "Qualified staff" and the business object "Aviation authority permit" –realization→ "Handling authorisation".

The resources "Handling equipment", "Qualified staff" and "Handling authorisation" –assignment→ capability "Wide-body aircraft handling". State the specific machines, the Ground Handling department and the aviation authority permit only in the description of the individual resources, so that the model stays at the strategic level and does not mix with operational elements.

Capability "Wide-body aircraft handling" –assignment→ the resources "Handling equipment", "Qualified staff" and "Handling authorisation". Further, the equipment "Aircraft tug", "Pallet loader" and "Tall stairs" –realization→ "Handling equipment", the business actor "Ground Handling" –realization→ "Qualified staff" and the business object "Aviation authority permit" –realization→ "Handling authorisation".

Model the resources as the business objects "Equipment register", "Staff register" and "Aviation authority permit" and capability "Wide-body aircraft handling" –access→ these objects. Do not include the specific machines and the Ground Handling department in the model.
explanation: A resource is an asset that an organisation owns or controls; assignment leads from a resource to a capability, and realization from specific elements of active or passive structure – equipment, a business actor or a business object – to the resource, so the director sees what to buy, whom to train and which permit to extend (5). The 3-point option is valid, but it hides the link to real elements in text, so what to buy, whom to train and which permit to extend cannot be read directly from the model; it is correct, just incomplete. The 1-point option has the correct realization of the resources, but reverses the key relationship: 3.2 does not permit assignment from a capability to a resource – a resource is assigned to a capability. The 0-point option confuses resources with information objects, and in 3.2 a capability cannot access (access) a business object.

scenario: Horizont Insurance is launching the product "Smart car insurance" – compulsory motor liability insurance with a discount based on driving style, which is measured by a mobile app. The product is to compete with similar offers from two large insurers, and the board is asking why clients should want it. The product manager is therefore preparing a model for marketing and the board. In it she wants to show what value the product brings to the individual stakeholders: lower premiums for safe driving for clients, more accurate risk pricing for the insurer. At the same time she points to a communication problem: the parties understand the business object "Driving score" differently – for the client it is "proof of my discount", for the underwriter "an indicator of the driver's riskiness". Marketing therefore needs to see both interpretations side by side, so as not to mix them up in the campaign, which starts in three months. The product will be sold online and through a network of intermediaries.
question: Which model best captures the value of the product and the differing interpretations of the score?
options: Associate the values "Lower premiums for safe driving" and "More accurate risk pricing" with the product "Smart car insurance" and each with its stakeholder – "Client" and "Insurer" respectively. Associate the meanings "Proof of discount" and "Indicator of driver riskiness" with the business object "Driving score" and with the respective stakeholder.

Associate the values "Lower premiums for safe driving" and "More accurate risk pricing" with the product "Smart car insurance" and each at the same time with the stakeholder for whom it holds – "Client" and "Insurer" respectively. Describe the differing understanding of the business object "Driving score" in detail in its documentation, so that marketing can look it up.

Model the value as the goals "Lower premiums for safe driving" and "More accurate risk pricing" and the product "Smart car insurance" –realization→ these goals, so it is clear what the product is for. Associate the meanings "Proof of discount" and "Indicator of driver riskiness" with the business object "Driving score" and with the respective stakeholder.

Model the value as the business service "Discount for safe driving", which the product "Smart car insurance" aggregates together with the insurance contract. Model both interpretations as representations "Proof of discount" and "Indicator of driver riskiness" –realization→ business object "Driving score", so that each party has its own form of the document in the model.
explanation: A value expresses the relative worth or utility of a concept and is associated with it and with the stakeholder for whom it holds; a meaning expresses the interpretation of a concept in a certain context, and the same business object can have different meanings for different stakeholders – the 5-point model thus covers both needs. The 3-point option captures the value correctly, but the differing interpretations that marketing needs to see remain only in text. The 1-point option has the meanings right, but confuses the value for customers with goals, that is, the organisation's intentions. The 0-point option uses neither value nor meaning: a service is not a value, and a representation is a perceptible form of information, not its interpretation.

scenario: The mobile operator TelNet CZ is losing younger customers, because the competition already offers full self-service in an app. It therefore plans to develop the capability "Customer self-service" in two steps. In the transition architecture (year 2027) self-service will be able to do only invoice and payment management; in the target state (year 2028) tariff changes and SIM card management will be added. The first level of self-service is realized by the new mobile app "My TelNet 1.0", the second level by its version "My TelNet 2.0" connected to the SIM management system. The head of strategy wants capability-based planning: the model must make clear which level of the capability is available in which state of the architecture, what realizes it and in what order the states follow. The model will be the basis for approving investments for both years; both versions of the app are being developed by an external supplier.
question: Which model best supports capability-based planning?
options: Model the levels as capability increments "Invoices and payments" and "Full service management" – specialisations of the capability "Customer self-service". Plateau "Transition state 2027" –aggregation→ the first increment and app 1.0, plateau "Target state 2028" –aggregation→ the second increment and app 2.0; plateau 2027 –triggering→ plateau 2028 and each app version –realization→ its increment.

Model the capability "Customer self-service" once: both plateau "Transition state 2027" and plateau "Target state 2028" –aggregation→ the same capability and the respective app version; plateau 2027 –triggering→ plateau 2028. Both app versions –realization→ the same capability, and the level of self-service reached is stated in the attribute "Level" of this capability.

Model the levels as capability increments "Invoices and payments" and "Full service management" – specialisations of the capability "Customer self-service". Increment "Invoices and payments" –realization→ plateau "Transition state 2027", increment "Full service management" –realization→ plateau "Target state 2028"; plateau 2027 –triggering→ plateau 2028 and each app version –realization→ its increment.

Model the levels of self-service as work packages "Release 1.0" (2027) –triggering→ "Release 2.0" (2028), developed by the external supplier, and both work packages –realization→ capability "Customer self-service". Plateaus are not needed, because the order of the architecture states is evident from the order of the releases and the level reached from their content and acceptance protocols.
explanation: For capability-based planning, the levels of a capability are modelled as capability increments (a specialisation of capability); the aggregation relationship leads from a plateau to the increment that holds in it, plateaus are ordered by a triggering relationship, and the realization relationship leads from concrete elements (applications) to increments – the model thus shows what is available when (5). The 3-point option is valid, but a single capability in two plateaus does not show which level holds in which state – one attribute cannot have two values. The 1-point option has the increments right, but 3.2 does not permit realization from an increment to a plateau; aggregation or realization may lead only from a plateau to a capability. The 0-point option confuses capability levels with projects and does not model the architecture states at all.

scenario: A regional hospital with 1,200 beds is replacing the obsolete hospital information system MedSys, which today covers clinical documentation as well as billing to health insurers. The migration will take place in two steps. In mid-2027 the clinical documentation will move to the new CareOne system, but billing will remain in MedSys for another year, with MedSys connected to CareOne by a temporary interface. In mid-2028 billing will be taken over by the CareOne Billing module, and MedSys and the temporary interface will be switched off. The transition period will last roughly a year, and in it the two systems must share patient data; an outage of billing would mean delayed payments from insurers in the order of tens of millions of crowns. The CIO wants, for the regional council as founder, a Migration view that shows the stable states of the architecture, their order and the differences between them; they are particularly interested in the risk of the temporary coexistence of the two systems.
question: Which model best matches the CIO's concern?
options: Three plateaus: "Baseline" –triggering→ "Transition state 2027" –triggering→ "Target state 2028"; each plateau –aggregation→ the applications valid in that state (the transition one thus MedSys, CareOne and the temporary interface). Between adjacent plateaus model a gap associated with both plateaus and with the applications that are added or retired.

Model two plateaus: "Baseline (MedSys)" –triggering→ "Target state (CareOne and CareOne Billing)" and each plateau –aggregation→ the applications valid in that state. Associate one gap with both plateaus and with the applications that are added or retired, and describe the temporary coexistence of the two systems in 2027 in the documentation of this gap.

Model the plateaus "Baseline" and "Target state 2028"; each plateau –aggregation→ the applications valid in that state. Model the temporary coexistence of MedSys and CareOne in 2027 as a gap between them, associated with both plateaus, with the temporary interface and with the systems that will run simultaneously in that period, so that the risk of coexistence is clearly visible.

Model the work packages "Step 1 – clinical documentation" –triggering→ "Step 2 – billing" and the target state as the deliverable "CareOne in full operation". Capture the differences between the states as deliverables of the individual steps and do not model the baseline, because it will cease to exist when the migration is complete and is no longer essential to the council's decision.
explanation: The stable states of the architecture – baseline, transition and target – are plateaus in ArchiMate, ordered by a triggering relationship, and an aggregation relationship leads from each plateau to the elements valid in that state; a gap is associated with exactly the two plateaus being compared and with the elements that differ between them (5). The 3-point option is valid, but it omits the transition state and with it the temporary coexistence of the systems, which the CIO explicitly asks about. The 1-point option captures the transition state as a gap; a gap, however, is a statement about the difference between two plateaus, not a state of the architecture in which the systems actually run. The 0-point option replaces states with projects and outputs, so no Migration view arises at all.
