scenario: Vltava Bank is launching a two-year programme "New core" with a budget of over CZK 300 million, which will replace the core banking system; more than 60 people from the bank and from suppliers are involved. The programme consists of the projects "Client data migration", "CoreX platform implementation" and "Decommissioning of the old core". Implementation may begin only after the architecture is approved by the steering committee, and decommissioning only after the data migration is completed. The result of the implementation is the "Deployed CoreX platform" (an operational installation of the CoreX application), and the result of the migration is the "Data migration report", which must be approved by internal audit. Audit insists that every delivered output be traceable in the model. The programme is run by the role "Programme manager", and the migration is carried out by the external supplier DataMove s.r.o. The programme manager wants a Project view that will make clear who is responsible for what, in what order the work takes place and what exactly each project is to deliver.
question: Which model best matches the programme manager's need?
options: Compose the programme "New core" (work package) of projects (work packages). Implementation event "Architecture approved" –triggering→ implementation project and migration project –triggering→ decommissioning project. The projects –access→ deliverables "Deployed CoreX platform" and "Data migration report". Role "Programme manager" –assignment→ programme, actor "DataMove s.r.o." –assignment→ migration project.

Compose the programme "New core" (work package) of projects (work packages). Implementation event "Architecture approved" –triggering→ implementation project and migration project –triggering→ decommissioning project. The implementation project –realization→ the application component "CoreX" directly, and the result of the migration is stated in the project description. Role "Programme manager" –assignment→ programme, actor "DataMove s.r.o." –assignment→ migration project.

Compose the programme "New core" (work package) of projects (work packages). Implementation event "Architecture approved" –triggering→ implementation project and migration project –triggering→ decommissioning project. The projects –access→ deliverables "Deployed CoreX platform" and "Data migration report". Both the role "Programme manager" and the actor "DataMove s.r.o." –assignment→ the deliverables whose handover they are responsible for.

Model the programme as a plateau "New core" with the budget in attributes –aggregation→ three business processes corresponding to the migration, implementation and decommissioning projects. Model the architecture approval as a business event –triggering→ the implementation process, the results of the projects as business objects that the processes access (access), and the programme manager and the supplier DataMove as business roles assigned (assignment) to all three processes of the programme.
explanation: The programme and the projects are work packages (a programme composed of projects), the order is determined by triggering relationships and implementation events, the results are deliverables to which access leads from the projects, and responsibility is expressed by assigning a role or actor to a work package – the 5-point model thus answers all three of the manager's questions. The 3-point option is valid (realization from a work package to an application component is permitted), but it omits the deliverables, so the report that the audit approves and that the project is to hand over is missing as well. The 1-point option has deliverables, but neither a business role nor an actor can be assigned to a deliverable – assignment belongs to a work package, a deliverable is merely a result of work. The 0-point option confuses a programme with a plateau and projects with recurring business processes. For the work package → deliverable link, 3.2 recommends modelling it with an access relationship; realization is still permitted for it, but deprecated.

scenario: The ministry is modernising the agenda system for issuing building permits; building offices today receive applications mostly in paper form, and proceedings are taking longer as a result. The architecture board has approved three requirements: "An application can be submitted electronically via the portal", "Proceedings documents are stored in the electronic file" and "The system is available 99.5% of working hours". The project of the selected supplier will hand over three outputs: "Electronic application form", "Integration with the records management service" and "Operational documentation with SLA". Electronic submission must work already in the transition state 2027, the other two requirements only in the target state 2028. The outputs are taken over by a ministry committee, and the results of the check are recorded in a handover report. Before each handover procedure the steering committee wants to check which output fulfils which requirement and which requirements must hold in which state of the architecture.
question: Which model best supports the steering committee's check?
options: Each deliverable –realization→ the requirement it fulfils: form → submission, integration → file, and documentation → availability. Plateau "Transition state 2027" –aggregation→ the requirement for electronic submission, plateau "Target state 2028" –aggregation→ the other two; the project's work package –access→ all three deliverables.

The project (work package) –realization→ all three requirements and, by another relationship, project –access→ the three deliverables that are its results. Plateau "Transition state 2027" –aggregation→ the requirement for electronic submission and plateau "Target state 2028" –aggregation→ the other two, so it is clear when each requirement is to hold.

Each requirement –realization→ the deliverable by which it is fulfilled (electronic submission → form, electronic file → integration with the records management service, availability → operational documentation). Plateau "Transition state 2027" –aggregation→ the requirement for electronic submission and plateau "Target state 2028" –aggregation→ the other two requirements.

Model each requirement as a work package –access→ the respective deliverable and the 2027 and 2028 deadlines as implementation events –triggering→ these work packages. It is not necessary to model the architecture states, because the deadlines and the order of the work follow directly from the implementation events and their mutual sequence in the project's timeline.
explanation: For checking coverage it is most precise when the realization relationship leads from each deliverable to the requirement it fulfils, and the aggregation relationship from a plateau to the requirements valid in that state – the committee thus sees what to verify at every handover (5). The 3-point option is valid, but the realization relationship leads from the whole project, so it is impossible to tell which output fulfils which requirement. The 1-point option has the correct pairing, but realization leads the wrong way – from a requirement to a deliverable, where 3.2 permits only association. The 0-point option confuses requirements with work and states with events, so the requirements disappear from the model entirely. For the work package → deliverable link, 3.2 recommends modelling it with an access relationship; realization is still permitted for it, but deprecated.

scenario: The online bookshop Listek, which sells over two million books a year, is moving from an obsolete e-commerce platform to the ShopNext solution and must not interrupt sales during the migration. In addition, software support for the old platform ends in March. The release manager needs a model of the key milestones and their links to the work. The project "ShopNext implementation" may begin only after the contract with the supplier is signed. Completion of the project leads to the milestone "ShopNext go-live", after which the project "Decommissioning of the old platform" begins. Go-live also means the transition of the architecture to the target state and changes the status of the output of the project, "ShopNext Release 1.0", from "in testing" to "in production". The milestone dates are also followed by the company's management, who want to see what the individual steps depend on. The release manager wants the model to make clear what each milestone triggers and what it acts on.
question: Which model best captures the milestones and their links?
options: Implementation event "Contract signed" –triggering→ work package "ShopNext implementation" –triggering→ implementation event "ShopNext go-live". Go-live –triggering→ work package "Decommissioning of the old platform" and plateau "Target state" and –access→ deliverable "ShopNext Release 1.0", because it changes its status; work package "ShopNext implementation" –access→ this deliverable.

Implementation event "Contract signed" –triggering→ work package "ShopNext implementation" –triggering→ implementation event "ShopNext go-live" –triggering→ work package "Decommissioning of the old platform". Go-live is connected to the plateau "Target state" and to the deliverable "ShopNext Release 1.0" only by an association relationship.

Model the contract signing and the go-live as business events: business event "Contract signed" –triggering→ work package "ShopNext implementation" –triggering→ business event "ShopNext go-live". Go-live then –triggering→ decommissioning of the old platform and plateau "Target state" and changes the status of the deliverable "Release 1.0".

Model the milestones as plateaus "Contract signed" and "Go-live", which are composed of the work packages carried out in the given period. Aggregate the deliverable "Release 1.0" in the plateau "Go-live" and record the change of its status from "in testing" to "in production" in the name of the deliverable, so that it is visible.
explanation: Change milestones are implementation events: triggering relationships lead from them to work packages and to a plateau, and by an access relationship they can act on a deliverable whose status they change – the 5-point model thus shows what each milestone triggers and what it acts on. The 3-point option is valid, but it expresses the link of the go-live to the target state and to the release only by a vague association, so exactly what the release manager wants to see is lost. The 1-point option uses business events from the business layer; these cannot trigger work packages (3.2 permits only association between them), so the key links are invalid. The 0-point option confuses milestones with stable states of the architecture, and 3.2 permits neither composition nor aggregation from a plateau to a work package or to a deliverable. For the work package → deliverable link, 3.2 recommends modelling it with an access relationship; realization is still permitted for it, but deprecated.

scenario: Polabi Waterworks is introducing smart water meters with remote reading. The programme is co-financed from European funds, which require continuous demonstration of benefits, and the benefits manager therefore wants to see what benefits the architecture is to bring in the individual states and which project outputs contribute to them. In the transition state 2027 (40% of customers with a smart meter) the outcome "Remote reading for 40% of customers" is to be achieved, in the target state 2029 the outcomes "Physical reading costs lower by 70%" and "Network leaks detected within 24 hours". The first outcome is contributed to by the output "Installed meters – wave 1", and leak detection by the output "Platform for analysing measurement data". All the outcomes are to contribute to the goal "Make the operation of the distribution network more efficient". The manager will report the benefits to the grant provider every six months.
question: Which model best matches the benefits manager's need?
options: Plateau "Transition state 2027" –aggregation→ outcome "Remote reading for 40% of customers", plateau "Target state 2029" –aggregation→ both target outcomes and plateau 2027 –triggering→ plateau 2029. Deliverables "Meters – wave 1" and "Data analysis platform" –realization→ the respective outcomes, which in turn –realization→ goal "Make the operation of the distribution network more efficient".

Deliverables "Meters – wave 1" and "Data analysis platform" –realization→ the respective outcomes and all three outcomes –realization→ goal "Make the operation of the distribution network more efficient". Model the plateaus of the transition and target states separately in the Migration view without a link to the outcomes, so that the benefits are not mixed with the states of the architecture.

Plateau "Transition state 2027" –aggregation→ outcome "Remote reading for 40% of customers", plateau "Target state 2029" –aggregation→ both target outcomes and plateau 2027 –triggering→ plateau 2029. Outcomes –realization→ deliverables "Meters – wave 1" and "Data analysis platform", which contribute to them, and outcomes –realization→ goal "Make the operation of the distribution network more efficient".

Model the benefits as deliverables of the programme, for example "Reading costs −70%" and "Leaks detected within 24 hours": projects –access→ these deliverables –realization→ the transition and target plateaus. Goal "Make the operation of the distribution network more efficient" –assignment→ the programme, which is responsible for achieving it before the grant provider and reports the benefits to it every six months.
explanation: ArchiMate 3.2 newly permits an aggregation (or composition) relationship from a plateau to an outcome, so it is possible to show which benefits hold in which state; the realization relationship then leads from deliverables to outcomes and from outcomes to the goal (5). The 3-point option is valid, but the benefits are not tied to the states of the architecture, although that is exactly what the benefits manager asks about; it is correct, just incomplete. The 1-point option has the plateaus right, but reverses the key relationship: 3.2 does not permit realization from an outcome to a deliverable (only association); realization leads from the output to the result. The 0-point option confuses benefits (outcomes) with project outputs (deliverables), and assignment from a goal to a work package does not exist. The work package –access→ deliverable link itself is not an error: 3.2 recommends it instead of realization, which is still permitted but deprecated.

scenario: The pharmaceutical distributor FarmaLog, which supplies 900 pharmacies, is preparing the transition of its warehouse management to a new system; the change must take place without any interruption of deliveries. In the baseline state the WMS Classic warehouse system runs and returns are recorded manually in spreadsheets. In the target state the cloud WMS Nova will run with a returns module, and both WMS Classic and the manual records will cease to exist. The business process "Goods receipt" will remain unchanged, it will just be supported by the new system. The change also includes training of warehouse workers, which the architect does not need to model. As part of a gap analysis, the architect needs to capture the difference between the baseline and target states in such a way that the migration work packages can be derived directly from it and that it is clear which elements change and which do not. The list of work packages will be the basis for the tender for a supplier.
question: Which way of capturing the difference is best?
options: "Baseline" –triggering→ "Target state" and associate the gap "WMS replacement" with both plateaus and with the elements that cease to exist or are added – with WMS Classic and the manual returns records, and with WMS Nova and the returns module respectively. Both plateaus –aggregation→ the process "Goods receipt", which is not connected to the gap; work packages are linked to the gap only by association.

"Baseline" –triggering→ "Target state" and associate the gap "WMS replacement" with both plateaus. State the list of retired and new applications, and the information that the process "Goods receipt" remains unchanged, in the textual description of the gap, so that the diagram stays clear and readable also for company management and for future suppliers.

"Baseline" –triggering→ "Target state" and associate the gap "WMS replacement" with both plateaus and with the elements that cease to exist and are added; both plateaus –aggregation→ the process "Goods receipt". The migration work packages –realization→ gap, because they close it; each package thus realizes its part of the difference.

Model the difference as the deliverable "New WMS" –realization→ plateau "Target state"; do not model the baseline, because it will cease to exist after the migration. Aggregate the changing applications in this deliverable and leave out the manual returns records, because they are not an application and, in the architect's view, do not belong in the architecture model, since the returns module will replace them anyway.
explanation: A gap is a statement about the difference between two plateaus: it is associated with both plateaus being compared and with the elements that are in only one of them, while unchanged elements remain in both plateaus – work packages can be derived from such a gap (5). The 3-point option is valid, but it hides the difference in text, so it cannot be read from the model what the change concerns. The 1-point option has the gap right in content, but 3.2 does not permit realization from a work package to a gap – only association is allowed between them; this is a single impermissible side relationship in an otherwise good model. The 0-point option does not model a gap at all, and without the baseline the difference cannot even be determined.

scenario: Atlas Insurance carries out the renewal of car insurance contracts every year from 1 November: the retention department approaches clients, recalculates the premium and issues amendments to the insurance contracts. This year, in addition, the project "Contract migration to PolicyOne" is running, with a fixed start in February and end in September, a budget of CZK 8 million and the result "Migrated contract portfolio", which internal audit will take over only after checking a sample of contracts. A mixed IT and business project team led by a project manager from IT works on the project; the retention department has released two people to it. Management wants to know which part of these people's work is normal operation and which is change. The architect is therefore to capture in one model both the operational activity and the change in such a way that it is clear what is the organisation's repeated behaviour and what is a one-off change activity with its own delivered result.
question: Which model best distinguishes operation from change?
options: Model the renewal as the business process "Car insurance contract renewal" triggered by the business event "Start of the renewal period", performed by the role "Retention specialist" and accessing the business object "Insurance contract". Model the migration as a work package with the dates and budget in attributes: work package –access→ deliverable "Migrated contract portfolio", project team –assignment→ work package.

Model the renewal as the business process "Car insurance contract renewal" triggered by the business event "Start of the renewal period" and performed by the role "Retention specialist". Model the migration as a work package with the dates and budget in attributes, to which the "PolicyOne project team" is assigned; work package –realization→ the business object "Insurance contract" directly.

Model the renewal as the work package "Contract renewal 2026" triggered by the implementation event "1 November", to which the role "Retention specialist", who leads the campaign every year, is assigned. Model the migration as a work package with the dates and budget in attributes: work package –access→ deliverable "Migrated contract portfolio" and "PolicyOne project team" –assignment→ work package.

Model the renewal as a business process triggered by the business event "Start of the renewal period" and performed by the role "Retention specialist". Model the migration as the plateau "Contract migration", to which the project team is assigned, and the delivered result as a gap between the old and new contract systems, which internal audit will take over after checking the sample.
explanation: A work package is a one-off series of activities with a clear start, end and result (a deliverable), whereas a repeated operational activity is a business process triggered by a business event – the 5-point model distinguishes both clearly. The 3-point option is valid, but it omits the deliverable: the derived work package → business object relationship does not capture the result that the audit takes over. The 1-point option models the annual renewal as a one-off work package, so the organisation's repeated behaviour looks like a project. The 0-point option confuses a project with a state of the architecture and a result with a gap, and a project team (a business actor or collaboration) cannot be assigned to a plateau. For the work package → deliverable link, 3.2 recommends modelling it with an access relationship; realization is still permitted for it, but deprecated.
