scenario: The retail chain Pramen has taken over a competitor; together the two chains have 210 stores, two different customer centres, different complaint procedures and differently structured customer services. The architecture team is just entering Phase B (Business Architecture) of the TOGAF ADM cycle, whose goal is to unify the customer service of both networks; it has six weeks for the work in Phase B. The sponsor, the chief operating officer, wants to see how the organisation of customer service, the complaint and return-of-goods processes and the services offered to customers will differ in the baseline and target states. The differences are later to yield a list of candidate projects in Phase E. Neither chain has documented its architecture so far, and the inputs are being created from workshops with store managers. The team will address the application and technology architecture in the following phases; the ArchiMate model is to be the single source for all views.
question: How is ArchiMate best used in this phase?
options: Model the business elements – actors, roles, processes, services, business objects and products – in the baseline and target plateaus and capture the differences as gaps associated with both plateaus and with the changed elements. Show the sponsor the Organization, Business Process Cooperation, Service Realization and Product views of both states.

Model the business elements (actors, roles, processes, services, business objects, products) and show the sponsor the Organization, Business Process Cooperation and Service Realization views of both the baseline and the target state. Summarise the differences between the states in a separate text report, from which Phase E will then select the candidate projects.

Create a Migration view with the plateaus "Baseline" and "Target state" and the gaps between them, named after the changed areas of the service (organisation, complaints, returns of goods). Do not model the business elements in detail, because their concrete form will be refined only in the individual projects anyway.

Model right away the work packages and deliverables of the candidate service unification projects and their order using implementation events, so that the sponsor has an overview of budget and deadlines as early as possible. Fill in the business architecture as needed only during the implementation of the individual projects.
explanation: In Phase B the baseline and target business architecture are modelled; ArchiMate offers business elements for this, plateaus for both states, gaps as input for Phase E, and the Organization, Business Process Cooperation, Service Realization and Product viewpoints (5). The 3-point option has the right content and views, but keeps the differences outside the model, so projects cannot be built on them. The 1-point option has plateaus and gaps, but without business elements it is too abstract – the sponsor will not see what changes in the organisation, processes and services. The 0-point option jumps to the content of Phases E and F (work packages, deliverables) before the target architecture is even defined.

scenario: A university with 25,000 students is starting a TOGAF ADM cycle for the digitalisation of study administration; the study departments of its eight faculties each proceed differently today, and the university has no architecture model yet. In Phase A (Architecture Vision) the architect is to agree with the stakeholders – the rector, the bursar and student representatives – the scope and vision of the change and prepare inputs for the Statement of Architecture Work, which will be approved by the rector's board; the inputs must be concise and understandable to non-experts. The rector wants to see why the change is happening (student complaints about paper applications, new statutory obligations for electronic communication), what it is to achieve and which capabilities of the university the change will strengthen. Detailed processes and applications will be addressed only in Phases B and C, where the architect wants to elaborate the Phase A model further.
question: How is ArchiMate best used in Phase A?
options: In the Stakeholder and Goal Realization views, capture the stakeholders, drivers, assessments, goals, outcomes and the main requirements. In a Capability Map view, mark the capabilities that the change will strengthen, e.g. "Study administration", and possibly the affected stages of the value stream "Complete studies", all only at a high level of abstraction.

In the Stakeholder and Goal Realization views, capture the stakeholders, drivers, assessments, goals, outcomes and the main requirements, so that the rector sees the reasons for and goals of the change. Do not model the university's capabilities yet, because in the architect's view they belong only to the business architecture in Phase B and would merely burden the model in the vision.

Map in detail the current study processes of all eight faculties in the Business Process Cooperation view and their support by applications in the Application Usage view, so that the scope of the change is based on reality. Summarise the rector's motivation and the goals of the change in the introductory chapter of the Architecture Vision document.

Prepare Technology and Implementation and Deployment views of the university's current infrastructure and on that basis propose the digitalisation work packages and their budget. Address the stakeholders and their concerns only when accepting the results of the individual projects, when it will already be clear what is being delivered.
explanation: Phase A needs a high-level view of the motivation (stakeholders, drivers, assessments, goals, outcomes, key requirements) and of the affected capabilities or value streams – ArchiMate offers the Stakeholder and Goal Realization viewpoints for this, as well as strategy viewpoints such as the Capability Map (5). The 3-point option is valid, but it omits the capabilities that the rector explicitly asks about; strategy elements are appropriate to use already in the vision. The 1-point option is too detailed, anticipates Phases B and C and leaves the motivation outside the model. The 0-point option starts with technology and projects and postpones the stakeholders, which contradicts the purpose of the Architecture Vision.

scenario: The head physician of the emergency department at Na Vyhlidce Hospital is the owner of the process "Admission of a patient to the emergency department", through which around 150 patients pass every day. After two recent outages, when staff wrote data on paper for several hours, she wants to understand which applications and application services support the individual steps of the process (triage, patient registration, ordering of examinations), through which interfaces staff work with them and with what data. On this basis she wants to prepare fallback procedures for the case of another outage and train nurses in them. The emergency department uses six applications from four suppliers, and nobody has documented their links to the process. The infrastructure and the mutual integration of the applications do not interest the head physician – the IT department handles those. She needs to see what her process depends on from the point of view of applications. The architect has a complete model of the hospital in all layers in the repository.
question: Which viewpoint should the architect choose for the head physician?
options: Application Usage: the view shows the process steps, the roles that perform them, and the application services, interfaces and components from which serving relationships lead to these steps, including data objects. The head physician thus sees the process's direct dependencies on applications.

Business Process Cooperation: the view shows the relationships of the process "Patient admission" to subsequent processes (hospitalisation, laboratory, radiology), shared business objects and the services the processes provide to one another. Application services can be added for the processes that use them.

Application Cooperation: the view shows the emergency department's applications, their mutual data flows and the interfaces through which they communicate, including the locations where they run. From the data flows between applications it can be inferred indirectly which steps of the process an outage of a particular application will endanger.

Technology Usage: the view shows on which technology services, servers and networks the emergency department's applications depend and where the individual points of failure are. The causes of the past outages can thus be explained directly on the infrastructure and the infrastructure can be strengthened in a targeted way.
explanation: The Application Usage viewpoint shows how business processes are supported by applications – the process steps, roles and the application services, interfaces and data they depend on – which is exactly the process owner's concern (5). Business Process Cooperation may contain application elements, but its focus is the links between processes, so it will show the dependence on applications only marginally (3). Application Cooperation looks at the relationships between applications themselves, and the process's dependency could be estimated from it only indirectly (1). Technology Usage addresses the relationship of applications to the infrastructure, which the head physician explicitly ruled out (0).

scenario: After taking over a competitor, the retail chain Pramen runs 140 applications from two companies, including three different systems for the loyalty programme and two point-of-sale systems. Integrations currently run through two different integration platforms, and their documentation is incomplete. The CIO is preparing a rationalisation of the application portfolio and needs to find duplicate integrations and candidates for decommissioning. They want a single overview of which applications exchange what data, through which interfaces, and which application services they provide to one another; they are also interested in which of the two data centres each application runs in. They are not interested in business processes or server configurations at this stage, nor in the internal structure of the individual applications. They will go through the overview with the heads of the application teams and use it as a basis for next year's budget; the decision on it will be made in two months.
question: Which viewpoint best matches the CIO's concern?
options: Application Cooperation: application components, their interfaces, the services they provide to one another and flow relationships labelled with the data exchanged, with applications grouped by data centre. The view thus shows the whole application landscape and its integrations.

Layered: a single view with all layers from business processes through applications to technology, in which the integrations between applications and their links to servers in both data centres are also visible. The CIO thus gets the complete context for decisions on decommissioning applications.

Application Structure: for each application separately, a view of its internal structure – its sub-components, interfaces and the data objects it works with. From the interfaces of the individual applications a list of possible integrations can then be compiled and searched for duplicate connections.

Organization: a view of the units of both companies, their roles and locations, in which each unit lists which applications it uses. Duplicates then show up as two units using different applications for the same work, and these can then be merged into a single application.
explanation: The Application Cooperation viewpoint is intended for relationships and information flows between applications, the provision of services between them and an overview of the application landscape including locations – exactly for rationalising integrations (5). Layered contains the necessary information too, but overwhelms the CIO with processes and technology that they explicitly do not want (3). Application Structure shows the inside of one application, not the integrations between applications, so it covers the concern only indirectly (1). Organization concerns units and responsibilities, not applications and data flows (0).

scenario: The board of the credit company Kredito is deciding on the allocation of the investment budget for 2027, which is a third lower than this year's. It wants to see on one page which of the company's capabilities are strategically the most important and at the same time the weakest according to the maturity assessment from this year's internal audit (a 1–5 scale for all 42 capabilities), so that it can set investment priorities. The board members are mostly financiers without knowledge of ArchiMate, and the budget meeting will take place next week. The architecture team has the capabilities in the model at three levels, and for each capability it records strategic importance and maturity as attributes. The model also contains processes, applications and ongoing projects, from which realization relationships lead to the capabilities. The board is not interested in the details of processes, applications or projects, however; the division directors will decide on those after the priorities are set.
question: Which view is most suitable for the board?
options: The Capability Map viewpoint: capabilities at two or three levels coloured as a heat map according to the maturity and strategic importance attributes, with a colour legend. It is a view with the purpose Deciding, which shows on one page where to invest.

The Strategy viewpoint: the view shows courses of action, capabilities, value streams, resources and outcomes and their mutual links. The board thus sees the company's strategy in context and can itself derive from it which capabilities need strengthening first.

The Outcome Realization viewpoint: the view shows by which capabilities, value streams and core elements (processes, applications) the individual outcomes are achieved. The board thus also sees the operational elements on which the company's results depend.

The Implementation and Deployment viewpoint: the view shows the applications supporting the individual capabilities and the infrastructure they run on. Weak capabilities will show up as obsolete technologies that need to be invested in as a priority.
explanation: The Capability Map viewpoint is intended for an overview of capabilities at 2–3 levels and for heat maps based on attributes (colours on their own have no semantics in ArchiMate, hence the attributes and the legend) – the board can thus decide on one page (5). The Strategy viewpoint is at the right level, but it shows the relationships of the strategy, not the comparison of the maturity and importance of capabilities that the board asks about (3). Outcome Realization concerns how results are achieved and adds operational detail that the board does not want (1). Implementation and Deployment is a technical viewpoint for mapping applications to infrastructure (0).

scenario: The portfolio manager of the mobile operator TelNet CZ runs 12 concurrent projects with a total budget of CZK 900 million; the portfolio grew gradually and several projects change the same applications. At the quarterly portfolio board she needs to show which projects change which applications and business processes, to which state of the architecture (transition or target) their results belong and which architectural requirements they fulfil. The last board criticised that from the list of projects it cannot tell their impact on the company. The board decides on pausing or accelerating projects on this basis, and therefore needs to see what would be missing from the architecture if a project ended. Detailed tasks, capacities and the schedule are kept in another tool. The board meets once a quarter and has an hour reserved for the topic. The architect has work packages, deliverables, plateaus, requirements and all the core elements in the model.
question: Which viewpoint best matches the portfolio manager's concern?
options: The Implementation and Migration viewpoint: work packages –access→ deliverables –realization→ plateaus, requirements and core elements – applications and processes. The board will see which project changes which part of the architecture and in which state.

The Project viewpoint: work packages, deliverables, implementation events, responsible business roles and the goals to which the projects contribute. The board will thus see the structure of the portfolio, its milestones, responsibilities and the contribution of the individual projects to the company's goals.

The Migration viewpoint: plateaus of the baseline, transition and target states and the gaps between them. The board will thus see how the architecture changes gradually, in what order the states follow and what differences arise between the individual states of the architecture.

The Application Cooperation viewpoint: the operator's applications and their mutual data flows, in which the name of the project is given in a note for applications changed by projects. The board will thus see the application landscape and the places where the individual projects of the portfolio intervene in it.
explanation: The Implementation and Migration viewpoint links programmes and projects with what they realize – with parts of the architecture, plateaus and requirements – exactly what the board needs (5). The Project viewpoint shows projects, milestones and responsibilities, but not their link to applications, processes and architecture states (3). The Migration viewpoint shows only plateaus and gaps, that is, states without projects, so the main subject of the concern is missing (1). Application Cooperation is a view of the application landscape, and projects are not model elements in it, just notes (0). For the work package → deliverable link, 3.2 recommends modelling it with an access relationship; realization is still permitted for it, but deprecated.

scenario: The engineering company Kovotech is moving its press shop from hall A to a new hall C on its premises; the move must take place during a fourteen-day company-wide holiday. Some presses weigh over 40 tonnes, and moving them requires modifications to the floor and the utility distribution. The head of production and the infrastructure administrator need, for planning, a single view that shows which machines (presses, welding robots) stand in which buildings, how they are connected by the conveyor line and the compressed air distribution, what material travels between them and which industrial control computers and industrial network control the machines. They are not interested in applications, business processes or the organisational structure at this stage. The view will also be shared with the external moving company. In addition to the IT infrastructure, the architect has the physical elements of production in the model and wants to choose a suitable viewpoint from the ArchiMate specification.
question: Which viewpoint should the architect choose?
options: The Physical viewpoint: presses and robots as equipment, halls as facilities, the conveyor line and the air distribution as distribution networks, material, and control computers as devices and a communication network. The view thus connects the physical environment with the IT that controls it.

The Technology viewpoint: devices (control computers), nodes, system software, communication networks and paths, including the locations in which they are placed. The view thus shows the control IT and the industrial network that need to be disconnected, moved to hall C and reconnected during the move.

The Implementation and Deployment viewpoint: application components of the control software, artifacts and the system software they run on, and the control computers on which they are deployed. The view thus shows what needs to be reinstalled and verified after the move to hall C.

The Organization viewpoint: the production and maintenance units in hall A, their roles and the locations in which they operate, so that it is clear who is responsible for which machine and who will move it. The machines, buildings and their mutual connections can be given in the description of the units that operate and maintain them.
explanation: The Physical viewpoint is intended for the relationship between the physical environment (equipment, facility, distribution network, material) and the IT that controls it – exactly for moving production (5). The Technology viewpoint covers the control computers and network, but lacks the machines, buildings, distribution systems and material, that is, the main subject of interest (3). Implementation and Deployment focuses on the deployment of software onto infrastructure, so it covers the concern only marginally (1). Organization shows people and responsibilities, which the stakeholders explicitly do not care about (0).

scenario: The secretary of the municipal office of a statutory city wants to explain to all 1,800 employees, on the intranet and on posters in the offices and at the branches, the new organisation of services to citizens after the reorganisation: which departments provide which services and through which channels (counter, citizen portal, data mailbox) a citizen can reach them. The employees do not know the ArchiMate notation and many of them work with IT only minimally. After the last reorganisation the poster was created by hand in a graphics program and within half a year stopped matching reality. The architect has the entire model of the city in a tool and wants the poster this time to be based on the model, remain consistent with it and be easy to update after further changes. The reorganisation will continue next year, so the poster will change several times; the secretary wants the first version by the end of the month.
question: How should the architect proceed according to the ArchiMate viewpoint mechanism?
options: Define a custom viewpoint for the purpose Informing: select only the necessary concepts – business actors for the departments, business services, business interfaces for the channels and the role "Citizen" – and choose as the representation a simplified illustration with icons, clear labels and a legend, generated from the model.

Select from the model the necessary concepts – business actors for the departments, business services, business interfaces for the channels, the role "Citizen" and the relationships between them – and create from them an ordinary diagram in the standard ArchiMate notation. Supplement the poster with a short guide on how to read the notation and update it regularly from the model.

Use the Layered viewpoint with all layers from business services to applications and technology in the standard notation. Add to the poster a legend of the standard icons and a link to the complete model on the intranet, where those interested can look up the details.

Because the example viewpoints in the appendix of the specification are normative, use the closest of them unchanged, the Organization viewpoint with departments, roles and interfaces. Explain the services and channels, which the viewpoint does not contain, in the accompanying text of the poster, which the city office's press department will prepare from the architect's materials.
explanation: The viewpoint mechanism means selecting a subset of concepts relevant to the concern and defining a representation understandable to the stakeholder – for a wide audience this means the purpose Informing and a simplified illustration derived from the model (5). The 3-point option has the right content, but the standard notation is an unsuitable representation for employees without knowledge of ArchiMate. A Layered view is overloaded in content and, moreover, in the standard notation, so it covers the concern only partially (1). The 0-point option rests on a misconception: example viewpoints are informative, and organisations may modify them and define their own.

image.alt: Two dimensions for classifying viewpoints: purpose (Designing, Deciding, Informing) and content (Details, Coherence, Overview) with typical stakeholders.

scenario: A regional authority is rationalising a portfolio of 85 applications whose operation costs over CZK 120 million a year. So far, data about the applications has been collected by e-mail from their administrators into spreadsheets that contradicted one another. The IT controller now needs to record for each application component its status according to the TIME method (Tolerate, Invest, Migrate, Eliminate), annual operating costs in CZK and criticality (high, medium, low). From these data they want to generate automatically colour heat maps of the application landscape for management and at the same time a table for compiling the budget. The data will be updated quarterly, and the heat maps must be regenerated without manual work; management wants the first heat map by the end of the quarter. The model must remain compliant with ArchiMate 3.2 and understandable to the other architects and to the external supplier who occasionally takes over the model in an exchange format.
question: How is the required data best captured in the model?
options: Define a user profile "Application portfolio" with typed attributes, that is, the TIME status and criticality as enumerations and the annual costs as a number, and assign it to the application components. Generate the heat maps from the attribute values with a legend and export the table from the same data.

Write the TIME status, costs and criticality as text in the documentation of each application component, or even in its name, for example "Records Management [Invest; 1.2 million; high]". Colour the heat maps manually according to these entries and compile the budget table by transcribing them.

Add separate motivation elements to each application component: the value "Annual costs CZK 1.2 million" and the assessments "Status: Invest" and "Criticality: high", connected to the component by an association relationship. Colour the heat maps according to these attached elements and compile the table from their names and descriptions.

Express the TIME status, costs and criticality only by the fill colour of the components in the individual views, the meaning of which the architects agree on verbally. Keep the budget table separately in a spreadsheet and adjust and check the colours in the individual views against it manually every quarter.
explanation: In ArchiMate 3.2 attributes are added by means of profiles – data structures of typed attributes attached to elements – so both the heat maps and the table can be generated from a single source (5). Text in the documentation or name is valid, but it is not typed, so automatic colouring and totals do not work reliably (3). The 1-point option gets the data into the model, but misuses value and assessment as carriers of attribute values and burdens the model with elements that mean something else. Colours have no formal semantics in ArchiMate and the data would not be in the model at all (0).

scenario: The risk management unit of the Domov Building Society wants to record operational risks and control measures in the same repository as the architects and link them to the business processes and applications they concern. So far it has kept the risks in spreadsheets that nobody linked to the architecture, and at the last inspection the regulator criticised that it cannot be demonstrated which measure protects which process. There are roughly 180 risks and over 300 measures; the unit has five analysts who have not yet worked with ArchiMate. The unit needs "risk" and "control measure" to be distinguishable types in the model with their own attributes (probability, impact, owner), so that they can be filtered and displayed with their own marker. The model must remain compliant with ArchiMate 3.2, so that the other architects and tools understand it too. The result will be presented to the regulator at the next inspection.
question: How is the language best customised for the needs of the risk management unit?
options: Define the specialisations «Risk» of the assessment element and «Control Measure» of the requirement element, each with a profile of typed attributes for probability, impact and owner. Associate risks with the affected processes and applications; the processes and applications by which the measure is ensured –realization→ «Control Measure», and associate the measure with the risk.

Use ordinary assessment and requirement elements with a prefix in the name, for example "RISK: …" or "MEASURE: …", and record probability, impact and owner as text in their documentation. Associate risks with the affected processes and applications; the processes and applications by which the measure is ensured in operation –realization→ the respective requirement.

Define the specialisations «Risk» of the business event element and «Control Measure» of the business process element, each with a profile of typed attributes for probability, impact and owner. Lead the links as follows: «Risk» –triggering→ «Control Measure» and «Control Measure» –serving→ the processes protected from the impact of the risk.

Introduce into the tool new element types "Risk" and "Control" that are not derived from any ArchiMate element, and between them a new relationship "mitigates" with its own rules. Design custom shapes and colours for both types, so that in diagrams for the regulator they are clearly distinguished from the standard elements of the language.
explanation: A specialisation is, in ArchiMate 3.2, the mechanism for new types derived from existing concepts: they inherit their meaning and permitted relationships, attributes are supplied by a profile, and the specialisation is marked with «guillemets» – a risk as a specialisation of assessment and a control measure as a specialisation of requirement matches their meaning (5). The 3-point option is valid, but it distinguishes the types only by a naming convention and the attributes are not typed. The 1-point option uses the right mechanism, but on unsuitable base elements: a risk is not a change of state and a measure is not a process, so they inherit the wrong meaning and relationships. The 0-point option creates concepts and a relationship outside the metamodel, thereby violating the language, and the model loses understandability.

question: Which conclusion of the impact analysis is the most correct?
options: By valid derivation, “Tour Sales” and “Tour Complaint Handling” are certainly affected, because chains of assignment and realization followed by a serving relationship yield “APP-01” –serving→ process. The complaint subprocesses are affected only potentially; “Manual Payment Verification”, which serves the application, and “Marketing Campaign” do not depend on the server.

By valid derivation, “Tour Sales”, “Tour Complaint Handling” and both of its subprocesses are certainly affected, because a serving relationship leading to a whole applies equally to its parts. According to the model, “Manual Payment Verification” and “Marketing Campaign” do not depend on the server, so the director does not need to inform the accounting department or marketing about them.

“Tour Sales”, “Tour Complaint Handling” and also “Manual Payment Verification” are certainly affected, because all three are connected to “Booking Engine” by a serving relationship. The complaint subprocesses are affected only potentially and this needs to be verified; according to the model, “Marketing Campaign” does not depend on the server, because an association does not prove dependency.

All processes that are connected to the server in any way in the model are certainly affected, including “Marketing Campaign” and both complaint subprocesses. The derived relationship is “APP-01” –assignment→ process, because the chain starts with an assignment relationship and, according to the architect, that is preserved to the end of the chain during derivation.
explanation: The structural chain node → artifact → component → function → service yields a derived realization (the weakest relationship in the chain), and a structural relationship followed by serving yields a valid serving relationship from the server to the process, so both processes are certainly affected; a serving relationship leading to a whole applies to its parts only potentially (5). The 3-point option gets the certain impact right but presents a potential derivation as valid. The 1-point option follows serving in the wrong direction: the serving relationship leads from “Manual Payment Verification” to the application, so the process is the provider, not the dependent consumer. The 0-point option treats an association as proof of dependency and derives the wrong relationship type – the weakest structural relationship is derived from the chain, not the first one.

image.alt: Example of relationship derivation: role assigned to process, process realizes service, derived relationship role realizes service, and the strength ordering of structural relationships.

question: Which derived relationships should the architect draw in the view?
options: “Claims Department” –realization→ “Damage Resolution”, because the weakest structural relationship is derived from the chain of assignment, assignment and realization. “Claims Department” –access→ “Inspection Report”, because a structural chain followed by an access relationship yields a validly derived access.

“Claims Department” –realization→ “Damage Resolution”, because the weakest structural relationship is derived from the chain of assignment, assignment and realization. Connect the department and the report only with an association relationship, because access to an object that only a subprocess works with cannot be validly derived through composition and association is always the safe choice.

“Claims Department” –assignment→ “Damage Resolution”, because according to the architect the derived relationship takes the type of the first relationship in the chain, that is, assignment. “Claims Department” –access→ “Inspection Report”, because a structural chain followed by an access relationship yields a validly derived access.

“Damage Resolution” –realization→ “Claims Department”, because the service is a concrete manifestation of the department’s everyday work. “Inspection Report” –assignment→ “Claims Department”, because the report is created under its responsibility and the department vouches to management for its correctness and completeness.
explanation: A chain of structural relationships yields as the validly derived relationship the weakest of them (realization < assignment < aggregation < composition), so realization from the department to the service; a structural relationship followed by the dependency relationship access yields the same access (5). The 3-point option gets the service right but needlessly weakens the validly derivable access to an association, thereby losing the information about working with the report. The 1-point option takes the type of the first relationship instead of the weakest – assignment would claim that the department directly exposes the service, which does not follow from the model. The 0-point option reverses the direction and uses relationships that 3.2 does not permit between these elements.

image.alt: Example of relationship derivation: role assigned to process, process realizes service, derived relationship role realizes service, and the strength ordering of structural relationships.

question: Which statement about the derived relationships is the most correct?
options: “Client Scoring” –serving→ “Loan Application Processing” and “Credit Analyst” can be validly derived, because a service serving a part also serves the whole, and a service serving behaviour also serves the role that performs it. A relationship to “Contract Signing” cannot be validly derived, at most as a potential one.

The relationships “Client Scoring” –serving→ “Loan Application Processing” and “Client Scoring” –serving→ “Credit Analyst” are only potential derivations, so they can be drawn only after verification with the process owner. A relationship to the subprocess “Contract Signing” cannot be validly derived, at most as a potential one.

“Loan Application Processing” –serving→ “Client Scoring” and “Credit Analyst” –serving→ “Client Scoring” can be validly derived, because both the process and the role use the service, and according to the architect a dependency is drawn from the user to the provider. A relationship to the subprocess “Contract Signing” cannot be validly derived, at most as a potential one.

“ScoreX” –assignment→ “Loan Application Processing” can be validly derived, because the component performs part of the process, and also “Client Scoring” –realization→ “Loan Application Processing”. Relationships to the role “Credit Analyst” cannot be derived, because a role is active structure and, according to the architect, a service serves only behaviour.
explanation: If a dependency relationship (serving) points to a part of a whole or to behaviour, it can validly be carried over to the whole and to the active element assigned to that behaviour; carrying it from the whole over to its other parts is at most potential (5). The 3-point option derives the correct relationships but wrongly labels them as only potential, although they are valid derivations. The 1-point option reverses the direction – serving leads from the provider (the service) to the consumer, not the other way round. The 0-point option derives relationships that 3.2 does not permit: an application component cannot be assigned to a business process and a service cannot realize a process.

question: Which statement is the most correct?
options: “Orders” –flow→ “Warehouse” and “Warehouse” –flow→ “Transport” can be validly derived, because a flow between functions carries over to the components assigned to them. “Orders” –flow→ “Transport” is only a potential derivation: flow is not validly transitive, and whether data from orders actually flows to transport must be verified.

“Orders” –flow→ “Warehouse” and “Warehouse” –flow→ “Transport” can be validly derived, because a flow between functions carries over to the components assigned to them. “Orders” –flow→ “Transport” can also be validly derived, because flow, like triggering, is transitive, and this can be confirmed to the auditors straight away without further verification.

“Orders” –triggering→ “Warehouse” and “Warehouse” –triggering→ “Transport” can be validly derived, because passing on the order triggers picking and passing on the parcels triggers delivery planning. “Orders” –flow→ “Transport” is only a potential derivation and needs to be verified with the teams of both applications.

Nothing can be derived between the components, because flows lead only between functions and do not carry over to active structure. The integration should therefore be captured by the relationships “Orders” –composition→ “Warehouse” and “Orders” –composition→ “Transport”, because both applications provide their data to orders.
explanation: A structural relationship (assignment) followed by a dynamic relationship yields the same dynamic relationship, and a flow pointing to behaviour can be carried over to the active element assigned to that behaviour – so the flows between components can be validly derived; the transitivity of flow, however, is only potential (5). The 3-point option correctly derives the direct flows but presents the transitivity of flow as valid; only triggering is validly transitive. The 1-point option changes the type of the derived relationship – a derived dynamic relationship keeps its type, and flow (a transfer of data) is not triggering. The 0-point option denies a valid derivation and models the integration with composition, which expresses a whole–part relationship.

question: Which derived relationships are the most correct?
options: “Invoicing” –realization→ “Heat Billing”, because assignment and realization yield realization, that is, automation; “om_table” –realization→ business object “Delivery Point” from the chain of two realizations, and “Invoicing” –access→ “Meter Reading”, because a structural relationship followed by access yields access.

“Invoicing” –realization→ “Heat Billing” and “Invoicing” –access→ “Meter Reading” are valid derivations. Connect the artifact “om_table” and the business object “Delivery Point” only with an association relationship, because ArchiMate 3.2 does not permit derivation across two layers at once and a realization would be unsupported.

“Invoicing” –serving→ “Heat Billing”, because the application supports the process, then “om_table” –realization→ business object “Delivery Point” (a chain of two realizations) and “Invoicing” –access→ “Meter Reading” (a structural relationship followed by an access relationship).

“Invoicing” –assignment→ “Heat Billing”, because the component performs the process, and business object “Delivery Point” –realization→ artifact “om_table”, because physical data arises from a business concept. A relationship to the meter reading data cannot be derived, because according to the architect access is not derived.
explanation: The chain assignment + realization yields a derived realization from the component to the business process (the component automates the process), two realizations in a row yield a realization from the artifact to the business object, and a structural relationship followed by an access relationship yields access – the 5-point model preserves all the connections. The 3-point option is valid, but it needlessly weakens a validly derivable realization to an association; derivation across multiple layers is permissible. The 1-point option turns automation into support – serving cannot be derived from the chain of assignment and realization and expresses a different meaning. The 0-point option uses a construct from ArchiMate 2 (an application component assigned to a business process) and a reversed realization, which 3.2 does not permit.

image.alt: Example of relationship derivation: role assigned to process, process realizes service, derived relationship role realizes service, and the strength ordering of structural relationships.

question: Which conclusion of the review is the most correct?
options: (1), (2) and (3) are not permitted. Corrections: (1) “CRM” –realization→ application service –serving→ “Complaint Handling”; (2) “Server APP-02” –assignment→ artifact “crm.war” –realization→ “CRM”, so that it is visible where it runs; (3) reverse it to “Customer Care Department” –assignment→ “Complaints Officer”. The other two relationships are fine.

(1), (2) and (3) are not permitted. Corrections: (1) “CRM” –realization→ application service –serving→ “Complaint Handling”; (2) replace with the relationship “Server APP-02” –serving→ “CRM”, because the server provides the environment for the application; (3) reverse it to “Customer Care Department” –assignment→ “Complaints Officer”. The other two relationships are fine.

(1) and (3) are not permitted. Corrections: (1) “CRM” –realization→ application service –serving→ “Complaint Handling”; (3) reverse it to “Customer Care Department” –assignment→ “Complaints Officer”. Relationship (2) is the standard way to capture the deployment of an application on a server, and relationships (4) and (5) are fine as well.

The view is fine, the directions just need to be unified: (1) reverse it to “Complaint Handling” –assignment→ “CRM”, because the process controls the application, and (4) reverse it to business object “Complaint” –realization→ data object “Complaint”, because data arises from a business concept. The other relationships, including the assignment of the server to the CRM, can be left unchanged.
explanation: In 3.2 an application component cannot be assigned to a business process (a construct from ArchiMate 2; manual work supported by an application is expressed by serving from an application service to the process), a node is tied to an application via an artifact – the node is assigned to the artifact and the artifact realizes the component – and assignment leads from the actor to the role (5). The 3-point option finds all the errors but replaces the deployment with a serving relationship, which is valid but loses the information about where the CRM runs. The 1-point option keeps the impermissible assignment of a node to an application component. The 0-point option considers the faulty view correct and proposes further impermissible relationships, including a reversed realization of the business object.

image.alt: Example of cross-layer alignment: a technology service serves an application component, an application service serves a business process, a data object realizes a business object, and artifacts realize the data object and the application component.

question: Which derived relationships from the “Benefits Portal” to the motivation elements are the most correct?
options: “Benefits Portal” –realization→ requirement “Online submission 24/7” and goal “Simplify contact”, because a chain of assignment and realizations yields realization. To the goal “Reduce costs”, “Benefits Portal” –influence→ goal can be validly derived, because a structural chain followed by an influence relationship yields influence.

“Benefits Portal” –realization→ requirement “Online submission 24/7” and “Benefits Portal” –realization→ goal “Simplify contact” (a chain of assignment and realizations yields realization). Derive nothing to the goal “Reduce costs”, because derivation does not continue past an influence relationship and the relationship would be unsupported.

“Benefits Portal” –realization→ requirement “Online submission 24/7” (a chain of assignment and realizations yields realization). Also derive “Benefits Portal” –realization→ goal for both goals, because the requirement that the portal realizes contributes to both goals, and the derived relationship will thus be the same for both as for the requirement, that is, realization.

“Benefits Portal” –assignment→ requirement “Online submission 24/7”, because the chain starts with an assignment relationship, and goal “Simplify contact” –realization→ “Benefits Portal”, because the goal is fulfilled by means of the portal. Derive nothing to the goal “Reduce costs”, because influence is not derived at all.
explanation: A chain of structural relationships (assignment and three realizations) yields a derived realization from the portal to the requirement and to the goal, and a structural chain followed by the dependency relationship influence yields influence from the portal to the second goal – the IT director thus sees all the requirements and goals that the new solution must take over (5). The 3-point option is correct but omits the validly derivable influence on cost savings. The 1-point option promotes influence to realization; from a chain ending with an influence relationship, influence is derived, so the model would distort the portal’s contribution to savings. The 0-point option derives relationships that 3.2 does not permit: an application component cannot be assigned to a requirement and a goal cannot realize a component.

scenario: The regional railways have completed Phases B–D of the TOGAF ADM cycle for a new ticket sales system: in the model they have the baseline and target architectures and the gaps between them. The new system will replace the ticket offices, the old ticket machines and the e-shop, through which more than 30 million tickets are sold per year, and it must be connected to the nationwide fare system. In Phases E (Opportunities and Solutions) and F (Migration Planning), the architect is to propose, together with the PMO, transition architectures and an implementation plan. The PMO’s concern is: in what order, with what work packages and through what stable intermediate states do we reach the target, so that ticket sales work at every moment. The plan will be approved by the supervisory board, and its execution will be checked in Phase G by the architecture board, which wants the work and the intermediate states to be traceable in a single model.
question: What is the best way to use ArchiMate in Phases E and F?
options: Consolidate the gaps and design transition plateaus ordered by the triggering relationship, with gaps between adjacent plateaus. Group the changes into work packages, from which access leads to deliverables that realize the plateaus; capture milestones as implementation events; present in the Migration and Implementation and Migration views.

Consolidate the gaps, design transition plateaus ordered by the triggering relationship with gaps between adjacent plateaus, and present them in the Migration view. Keep the work packages and their order in the PMO’s planning tool without linking them to the plateaus in the model, so that the plan can easily be changed without the architect’s intervention and without updating the model.

Design work packages for the individual stages, order them with the triggering relationship, and capture the intermediate states as implementation events “Stage 1 completed” and “Stage 2 completed”. Do not model plateaus for the intermediate states, because the state after each stage follows from the completed work packages and their deliverables.

Return to the models from Phases B–D and, instead of planning the migration, create a detailed Layered view of the target architecture with all layers and elements, including the new sales system, ticket offices and the fare interface. The PMO will derive the projects and their order from it on its own, so Implementation and Migration elements are not needed in the model at all.
explanation: In Phases E and F, transition architectures (plateaus ordered by the triggering relationship) and work packages are designed from the consolidated gaps, with a realization relationship leading from their deliverables to these plateaus, including milestones – the Migration and Implementation and Migration views thus answer the order, the work packages and the intermediate states (5). The 3-point option gets the intermediate states right but keeps the work packages outside the model, so the link between the work and the intermediate states is missing. The 1-point option captures transition architectures as implementation events; an event is a moment of change, not a stable state of the architecture in which sales must work. The 0-point option ignores the purpose of Phases E and F and does not use Implementation and Migration elements at all. For the work package → deliverable link, 3.2 recommends modelling with the access relationship; realization is still permissible for it but deprecated.

image.alt: Implementation & Migration elements: work package, deliverable, implementation event, plateau and gap with their relationships, including a note on the deprecated realization.

scenario: The building society Domov operates an architecture completed in the previous TOGAF ADM cycle. New European requirements for the accessibility of digital services now apply, concerning both its client portal and its mobile application; for example, operation without a mouse and legibility for screen-reading software. The requirements take effect in nine months and non-compliance risks a fine, while the IT budget for next year has already been allocated. In Phase H (Architecture Change Management), the architect is to assess the impact of the change and prepare materials for the decision whether to handle it as a change within the existing architecture or to start a new ADM cycle. The IT director wants to see why the change arises, which requirements follow from it and which parts of the architecture it will affect. The building society has a current ArchiMate model of all layers, including motivation and the requirements from the previous cycle.
question: What is the best way to use ArchiMate in Phase H?
options: Model the regulation as a driver associated with stakeholders and with an impact assessment from which new requirements arise. By analysing relationships, including derived ones, from the requirements to the elements that are to realize them, find the affected applications and processes in a Requirements Realization view and, depending on the scope, recommend a change within the architecture or a new cycle.

Model the regulation as a driver associated with stakeholders and with an impact assessment from which new requirements arise, and present everything in Stakeholder and Motivation views. Leave the identification of the affected applications and processes to the projects that will implement the change, because they know the details of the solution best and will assess the impact themselves.

Model work packages “Portal Modification” and “Mobile Application Modification” straight away, with their deliverables –realization→ the modified application components; prepare a Project view with deadlines. Describe the motivation for the change and the new accessibility requirements in the written brief of both projects, which will be prepared by the product owners of both applications.

Model the regulation as a business event –triggering→ the business processes of client service and reflect the change only by updating their descriptions and the user guides for the portal. A new ADM cycle and an impact assessment are not needed, because the architecture has already been approved once and minor changes are handled by operations.
explanation: In Phase H, new impulses for change are captured as drivers and assessments from which requirements arise, and the analysis of relationships determines which elements the change affects – depending on the scope of the impact, a decision is then made between a change within the architecture and a new cycle (5). The 3-point option gets the motivation right, but without an analysis of the impact on the existing architecture the basis for the decision, which is the point of Phase H, is missing. The 1-point option jumps straight to the projects without capturing the reason and the requirements in the model, so traceability and the decision on the scope of the change are missing. The 0-point option confuses a driver with a business event and denies the purpose of architecture change management.

scenario:
The Hradiste City Police is preparing a new competency model for its officers. Every officer, regardless of assignment, performs patrol duty and writes up offences. Dog-handler officers additionally train service dogs, and district officers additionally meet regularly with the citizens of their district. A dog handler and a district officer therefore do everything an ordinary officer does, and in addition have their own special duties. Dog handlers are assigned to the dog handlers group, district officers to the Sever district station.

The chief of the city police wants a model in which the common duties are captured in a single place, so that when a regulation changes, for example on writing up offences, it does not have to be edited separately for each type of officer. At the same time it should be evident from the model that a dog handler and a district officer are a special kind of officer and which unit employs which officers. The model will also serve the personnel department when planning training.
question: Which model best matches the requirement of the chief of the city police?
options: From the Business Roles “Dog Handler” and “District Officer” lead a specialization to the general Business Role “Officer”. Assign the general role to the Business Processes “Patrol Duty” and “Offence Write-up”, and the specialized roles to the processes “Service Dog Training” and “Meeting Citizens of the District”. Assign the Business Actors “Dog Handlers Group” and “Sever Station” to the specialized roles.

Introduce three Business Roles “Officer”, “Dog Handler” and “District Officer” and do not model relationships between them. Assign each of them separately to the Business Processes “Patrol Duty” and “Offence Write-up”, and the roles “Dog Handler” and “District Officer” additionally to the processes “Service Dog Training” and “Meeting Citizens of the District”. Assign the Business Actors “Dog Handlers Group” and “Sever Station” to these two roles.

Model “Officer” as a Business Collaboration that aggregates the Business Roles “Dog Handler” and “District Officer”, and assign it to the Business Processes “Patrol Duty” and “Offence Write-up”. Assign both roles to the processes “Service Dog Training” and “Meeting Citizens of the District”, and assign the Business Actors “Dog Handlers Group” and “Sever Station” to these roles.

Model “Officer” as a Business Function composed by a composition relationship of the Business Roles “Dog Handler” and “District Officer”, and lead a specialization from it to each of the two roles. Connect the Business Processes “Patrol Duty”, “Service Dog Training” and “Meeting Citizens of the District” with an assignment relationship led from the process to the role, and capture the units “Dog Handlers Group” and “Sever Station” as Locations.
explanation: The specialization relationship says that an element is a special kind of another element of the same type; common behaviour therefore needs to be assigned only once to the general role, and the specialized roles carry only their own special duties (5). The 3-point option is valid and factually correct, but it repeats the common duties for three roles and does not express the “is a kind of” relationship. The 1-point option uses valid relationships, but a Business Collaboration means that roles perform collective behaviour together, not that a more general kind of role exists. The 0-point option mixes structure with behaviour (a function composed of roles) and reverses the direction of both the specialization and the assignment relationship, which leads from a role to a process.

scenario:
A regional authority provides municipalities with subsidies for repairs of local roads. As soon as the regional council approves an application, two mutually independent activities follow: the legal department concludes a subsidy agreement with the municipality and the finance department reserves funds in the regional budget. Both activities start immediately after approval, neither waits for the other, and each takes a different amount of time. Payment of the advance may begin only when the agreement has been concluded and, at the same time, the funds have been reserved. Last year it happened twice that the advance was paid out before the municipality signed the agreement.

The head of the control department therefore requires a model of the process “Subsidy Provision” from which it will be unambiguously clear which steps run concurrently and that payment of the advance is conditional on the completion of both preceding activities. The model will become an appendix to the new directive on providing subsidies.
question: Which model best matches the requirement of the head of the control department?
options: Compose the Business Process “Subsidy Provision” of the steps “Application Approval”, “Agreement Conclusion”, “Funds Reservation” and “Advance Payment”. From the step “Application Approval” lead a triggering relationship to an AND junction and from it to the steps “Agreement Conclusion” and “Funds Reservation”. From both of these steps lead triggering to a second AND junction and from it to the step “Advance Payment”.

Compose the Business Process “Subsidy Provision” of the steps “Application Approval”, “Contractual and Budgetary Arrangements” and “Advance Payment”, connected by triggering relationships in this order. Agreement conclusion and funds reservation are thus combined into a single step, to which the Business Roles “Lawyer” and “Budget Officer” are assigned via an AND junction.

Compose the Business Process “Subsidy Provision” of the steps “Application Approval”, “Agreement Conclusion”, “Funds Reservation” and “Advance Payment”. From the step “Application Approval” lead a triggering relationship to an OR junction and from it to the steps “Agreement Conclusion” and “Funds Reservation”. From both of these steps lead triggering to a second OR junction and from it to the step “Advance Payment”.

Model the activities “Agreement Conclusion” and “Funds Reservation” as Business Functions and connect them to the step “Advance Payment” with flow relationships, which express waiting for their completion. Merge into a single AND junction the triggering from the step “Application Approval” together with assignment relationships from the Business Roles “Lawyer” and “Budget Officer”, and lead triggering from the junction to both activities.
explanation: Concurrency is expressed by an AND junction on triggering relationships: the split means that both activities start after approval, and the join means that payment of the advance starts only after both are completed (5). The 3-point option is valid and preserves the condition for payment, but it merges both activities into one step, so the concurrency is not visible in the model. The 1-point option uses an OR junction, which expresses a choice of one of the branches – the advance could then be paid out after either of the activities, which is exactly last year’s error. The 0-point option confuses process steps with functions, attributes to the flow relationship a causality it does not have, and merges relationships of different types in one junction, which ArchiMate does not allow.

image.alt: Two examples of a junction on a triggering relationship between processes: an AND junction (filled circle) and an OR junction (hollow circle), each with its reading.

scenario:
The building materials wholesaler Cihlar Morava is preparing a reorganisation and a replacement of its information system. The operations director complains that nobody has a comprehensive overview of which units permanently exchange what information with each other and with their surroundings. Sales continuously receives enquiries from customers and returns quotations to them. It passes confirmed orders to logistics, which reports delivery dates back to it. Purchasing sends orders to suppliers and receives delivery confirmations from them; it passes notices of incoming goods to logistics. These activities run continuously and concurrently; they are not steps of a single procedure with a fixed order.

The operations director wants a single view that shows the main areas of activity of the individual units, as well as of customers and suppliers, and the information these areas pass between themselves. He is not interested in the order of steps or in process details.
question: Which model best matches the requirement of the operations director?
options: Model the units “Sales”, “Logistics” and “Purchasing” and the external parties “Customer” and “Supplier” as Business Actors and assign to each the Business Function it performs, for example “Selling”, “Delivery Management” and “Procurement”. Between the functions lead flow relationships named after the information passed, for example “enquiry”, “quotation”, “confirmed order” and “notice”.

Model the units “Sales”, “Logistics” and “Purchasing” and the external parties “Customer” and “Supplier” as Business Actors and lead flow relationships between these actors, named after the information passed, for example “enquiry”, “quotation”, “confirmed order” and “notice”. The areas of activity are not included in the view and are given in the description of the actors.

Model the units “Sales”, “Logistics” and “Purchasing” and the external parties “Customer” and “Supplier” as Business Actors and assign to each the Business Function it performs, for example “Selling”, “Delivery Management” and “Procurement”. Between the functions lead triggering relationships in the direction of the information passing, and give the name of the information, for example “enquiry” or “notice”, in the description of the relationship.

Model the units’ activities as Business Services “Selling”, “Delivery Management” and “Procurement”, between which realization relationships lead in the direction of the information passing. Capture the information as Business Objects “Enquiry”, “Quotation” and “Notice” and from each object lead triggering to the service it triggers; model the external parties “Customer” and “Supplier” as Business Interfaces.
explanation: A business function view captures the main functions assigned to actors (including external parties) and the flow relationships between them; flow expresses the passing of information and implies neither order nor causality, which matches continuously and concurrently running activities (5). Flows led only between actors are valid, but the areas of activity that the director explicitly asks for are missing from the view (3). Triggering between functions is a permitted relationship, but it claims that one function triggers another in a given order, and it pushes the transfer of information into the description (1). The 0-point option confuses internal behaviour with services, attributes triggering to information as passive elements, and models the external parties as interfaces.

scenario:
The mobile operator TeleMorava offers households the package “Home Internet”. In it the customer gets an internet connection, telephone technical support and access to a self-service portal; the rules are governed by the general terms and conditions. In January the package “Home Internet Plus” will be added. It provides the customer with the same as the basic package and in addition a technician service visit within 24 hours, the guarantee of which is governed by a separate addendum to the contract. The product manager plans further variants and fears that the common components will be described anew for each variant and will eventually diverge.

He therefore wants an offering model that makes it clear that the Plus variant is a special kind of the basic package, what the two offers have in common and what the Plus variant adds. In the same way he then wants to add to the model the planned variants for seniors and for students.
question: Which model best matches the requirement of the product manager?
options: Model “Home Internet” as a Product that aggregates the Business Services “Internet Connection”, “Telephone Support” and “Self-Service” and the Contract “General Terms and Conditions”. Model “Home Internet Plus” as a second Product, from which a specialization leads to the product “Home Internet” and which aggregates the Business Service “Technician Visit within 24 Hours” and the Contract “Addendum on Visit Guarantee”.

Model “Home Internet” and “Home Internet Plus” as two Products between which no relationship leads. Both aggregate the same Business Services “Internet Connection”, “Telephone Support” and “Self-Service” and the Contract “General Terms and Conditions”; the Plus product additionally aggregates the Business Service “Technician Visit within 24 Hours” and the Contract “Addendum on Visit Guarantee”.

Model “Home Internet” as a Product that aggregates the Business Services “Internet Connection”, “Telephone Support” and “Self-Service” and the Contract “General Terms and Conditions”. Model “Home Internet Plus” as a second Product, to which an aggregation leads from the product “Home Internet” and which aggregates the Business Service “Technician Visit within 24 Hours” and the Contract “Addendum on Visit Guarantee”.

Model “Home Internet” as a Business Process composed of the steps “Internet Connection”, “Telephone Support” and “Self-Service”. Capture “Home Internet Plus” as a Contract, from which a realization leads to this process, and the technician visit as a Business Object connected to the contract by an assignment relationship. From the basic offer lead a specialization to the Plus variant.
explanation: A Product aggregates services and a contract, and a specialization relationship between two products expresses that the variant is a special kind of the basic product: the common components are described once at the basic product and the Plus variant carries only what it adds (5). Two unconnected products with shared services are a valid model that shows both the common and the added components, but the “is a kind of” relationship is missing and the common links are repeated for every further variant (3). An aggregation from the basic product to the Plus variant is formally possible, but it says the opposite of reality – that Plus is a part of the basic package (1). The 0-point option confuses a product with a process, has a contract realize behaviour, and reverses the specialization.

scenario:
The furniture manufacturer Javorina handles orders with the end-to-end process “From Order to Payment”, which has four consecutive steps: “Order Acceptance”, “Made-to-Order Production”, “Dispatch” and “Invoicing”. The company is managed functionally: the long-term stable areas of activity are “Sales”, “Production”, “Logistics” and “Finance”, and each of them also includes a number of other activities outside this process. The organisational units have been merged and split several times in recent years, but the functional areas have remained the same and management does not expect them to change.

The operations director wants a view that shows the course of the end-to-end process and at the same time which functional area each of its steps belongs to. The view should remain valid even after the next reorganisation of the units, which the company is preparing for next year. She later wants to prepare the same view for the complaints process.
question: Which model best matches the requirement of the operations director?
options: Compose the Business Process “From Order to Payment” by a composition relationship of the four steps connected by triggering relationships in the given order. Model the areas “Sales”, “Production”, “Logistics” and “Finance” as Business Functions and from each function lead an aggregation to the step that belongs to it. The step thus remains a component of a single process and is at the same time assigned to its functional area.

Compose the Business Process “From Order to Payment” by a composition relationship of the four steps connected by triggering relationships in the given order. Model the areas “Sales”, “Production”, “Logistics” and “Finance” as Business Functions and connect each function with the step that belongs to it by an association relationship. The view does not further specify the nature of the link between a step and a function.

Compose the Business Process “From Order to Payment” by a composition relationship of the four steps connected by triggering relationships in the given order. Model the areas “Sales”, “Production”, “Logistics” and “Finance” as Business Functions and from each function lead a second composition relationship to the step that belongs to it. The step is thus a component of both the process and the function.

Model the areas “Sales”, “Production”, “Logistics” and “Finance” as Business Roles connected by triggering relationships in the order of the steps. Capture the end-to-end process as a Business Service composed by a composition relationship of these four roles, and its individual steps as the Business Objects “Order”, “Product” and “Invoice”, which the given roles access through an access relationship.
explanation: The steps are components of the process (composition) and a Business Function can at the same time aggregate them: an element may be part of at most one composition, but of any number of aggregations; functions are moreover more stable than units, so the view survives a reorganisation (5). An association between a function and a step is valid and hints at the affiliation, but as a non-specific relationship it does not say that the step is part of the functional area (3). The 1-point option has the right elements, but puts the same step into two compositions, which contradicts the semantics of that relationship. The 0-point option confuses behaviour with roles and objects and composes a service of roles.

scenario:
The Vysocina Regional Library is rebuilding its “Loans” system, which consists of three modules. The module “Reminders” sends readers notices about the approaching end of the loan period and needs data about readers and about loans for this. It does not access this data itself, however: the data about readers is managed by the module “Reader Registry” and made accessible through the interface “Reader API”, the data about loans is managed by the module “Loan Records” and made accessible through the interface “Loan API”. No other module is to have its own access to this data.

For an audit of personal data protection, the data architect needs a model from which it will be evident which module is the sole custodian of which data, through which interfaces the reminders module reaches it, and that this module does not touch the data itself.
question: Which model best matches the need of the data architect?
options: Compose the Application Component “Loans” of the components “Reminders”, “Reader Registry” and “Loan Records”. From the component “Reader Registry” lead access to the Data Object “Reader” and composition to the Application Interface “Reader API”; from the component “Loan Records” access to the Data Object “Loan” and composition to “Loan API”. From both interfaces lead serving to the component “Reminders”.

Compose the Application Component “Loans” of the components “Reminders”, “Reader Registry” and “Loan Records”. From the component “Reader Registry” lead access to the Data Object “Reader”, from the component “Loan Records” access to the Data Object “Loan”. From both of these components lead serving to the component “Reminders”; the interfaces are not modelled as elements and their names are given in the description of the relationships.

Compose the Application Component “Loans” of the components “Reminders”, “Reader Registry” and “Loan Records”. From the component “Reminders” lead composition to the Application Interfaces “Reader API” and “Loan API” and from these interfaces serving to the components “Reader Registry” and “Loan Records”. From them lead access to the Data Objects “Reader” and “Loan”.

Connect the components “Reminders”, “Reader Registry” and “Loan Records” with the Data Objects “Reader” and “Loan” by access relationships led from each component to each object. Model “Reader API” and “Loan API” as Application Services. Lead an assignment relationship from each data object to the respective service and from the service on to the component “Loans”.
explanation: An interface is a component of the component that provides the service, and the serving relationship leads from the interface to the component that uses it; access from the custodian components to the data objects shows who works with the data, and the missing access from reminders demonstrates that it does not touch the data itself (5). The 3-point option is valid – serving between components can be derived – and shows the data custodians and the dependency of reminders, but the interfaces are missing. The 1-point option places the interfaces with the consumer and reverses the direction of serving, so it claims that reminders provide services to both custodian modules. The 0-point option gives every component access to the data, confuses an interface with a service, and leads assignment from a passive element, which is not allowed.

image.alt: ArchiMate generic metamodel: internal and external active structure, internal behavior, service, event and passive structure with the relationships assigned to, realizes, serves, accesses, triggers/flows to and composed of.

scenario:
The electronics e-shop Jiskra is designing a new integration interface for partners and, with it, a unified data model of the application layer. An order contains items; an item has no meaning outside its order and ceases to exist when the order is cancelled. A delivery address is also part of an order. The same address record is, however, also part of the customer profile, where the customer manages it in their address book, and it continues to exist even after the order is deleted. A special kind of order is the express order: it has everything an ordinary order has and in addition a requested delivery time.

The integration architect needs the partners’ developers to be able to tell from the model which data ceases to exist together with the order, which is shared among several wholes, and which data structure is a variant of another. The model will be part of the public documentation of the interface.
question: Which model best matches the need of the integration architect?
options: From the Data Object “Order” lead a composition to the Data Object “Order Item” and an aggregation to the Data Object “Delivery Address”, to which a second aggregation leads from the Data Object “Customer Profile”. From the Data Object “Express Order” lead a specialization to the object “Order”.

From the Data Object “Order” lead an aggregation to the Data Object “Order Item” and another aggregation to the Data Object “Delivery Address”. To the address lead a second aggregation from the Data Object “Customer Profile”, which thus shares it with the order. From the Data Object “Express Order” lead a specialization to the object “Order”.

From the Data Object “Order” lead a composition to the Data Object “Order Item” and another composition to the Data Object “Delivery Address”, to which a second composition leads from the Data Object “Customer Profile”. From the Data Object “Express Order” lead a specialization to the object “Order”.

From the Data Objects “Order Item” and “Delivery Address” lead an assignment to the Data Object “Order”, that is, from the part to the whole. Express the sharing of the address by a realization relationship led from the Data Object “Customer Profile” to the address. From the object “Order” lead a specialization to the Data Object “Express Order”.
explanation: Composition expresses that a part belongs to a single whole and does not exist without it (items), aggregation allows the same element to be part of several wholes (the address in the order and in the profile), and specialization leads from the special kind to the general element (5). Aggregations alone are valid, but the model then does not distinguish data that ceases to exist with the order from shared data (3). The 1-point option puts the address into two compositions, although an element may be a component of at most one, and thus claims that the address ceases to exist with the order. The 0-point option expresses the part–whole relationship with an assignment relationship, whose source cannot be a passive element, the sharing of the address with a realization relationship, which means nothing of the sort, and reverses the specialization.
