scenario:
The ticket seller Hale is splitting its monolithic system into separate applications. The application “Sales” completes the processing of a purchase by verifying the payment. At that moment an event important for the other applications occurs: the purchase is confirmed. The application “Capacity” reacts to it by firmly reserving the seats in the hall, the application “Notifications” by sending the tickets to the customer. The application “Sales” is not supposed to know who reacts to the confirmation; it merely announces that it has happened and, together with the announcement, makes the purchase data available. Next year further subscribers to the announcement will be added, for example a loyalty programme.

The solution architect wants a model of the behaviour of the application layer in which the purchase confirmation is visible as a separate change of state: what triggers it, what data it carries and what behaviour it triggers in the other applications. The model is also to serve the development teams of the individual applications as a shared reference description of their links.
question: Which model best matches the requirement of the solution architect?
options: Assign the Application Component “Sales” to the Application Process “Purchase Processing”, from which a triggering relationship leads to the Application Event “Purchase Confirmed”. From this event lead access to the Data Object “Purchase” and then triggering to the Application Process “Seat Reservation” of the component “Capacity” and to the Application Process “Ticket Sending” of the component “Notifications”.

Assign the Application Component “Sales” to the Application Process “Purchase Processing”, from which a triggering relationship leads to the Application Process “Seat Reservation” of the component “Capacity” and to the Application Process “Ticket Sending” of the component “Notifications”. From both triggered processes lead access to the Data Object “Purchase” and the confirmation is given in the name of the relationships.

Assign the Application Component “Sales” to the Application Process “Purchase Processing” and introduce the Application Event “Purchase Confirmed”, from which access leads to the Data Object “Purchase”. Lead triggering to this event from the process “Seat Reservation” of the component “Capacity” and from the process “Ticket Sending” of the component “Notifications” and from the event on to the process “Purchase Processing”.

Model the confirmation as the Data Object “Purchase Confirmed”, to which access leads from the Application Component “Sales” and from which triggering leads to the components “Capacity” and “Notifications”. Capture the behaviour of these components as Application Interfaces “Seat Reservation” and “Ticket Sending” and lead a realization from them to both components.
explanation: An Application Event is an instantaneous change of state: application behaviour can trigger it (triggering from a process to an event), and the event triggers further behaviour and can access a data object; the source process thus knows nothing about subscribers, and a further subscriber is connected by a new relationship from the event (5). Triggering led directly between processes is valid, but the confirmation as a separate change of state is missing in the model and the applications are tightly coupled (3). The 1-point option introduces the event but reverses the direction of triggering – the subscribers would trigger the event and it would trigger purchase processing. The 0-point option lets a passive data object trigger and confuses behaviour with interfaces.

scenario: The University of Jan Blahoslav was created by merging two universities, and the study agenda is now handled by two different software products: KampusIS for the faculties of the first university and UniMatrika for the faculties of the second. Both do the same thing and the study department perceives them as a single application. The chief architect wants to keep the target application map independent of vendors: its building blocks are to be logical applications, for example “Student Information System”, whose definition does not change even when a specific product is replaced. At the same time he needs to see which deployed products currently fulfil which logical application, because the product UniMatrika will be retired within two years and its faculties will move to KampusIS. The process “Semester Enrolment” uses the study records service regardless of which product currently provides it. The architect wants to present the map to the rector’s board when approving the budget for information systems.
question: Which model best matches the intent of the chief architect?
options: Model “Student Information System” as a logical Application Component, from which a realization leads to the Application Service “Study Records” serving the Business Process “Semester Enrolment”. Model the products “KampusIS” and “UniMatrika” as physical Application Components and from each of them lead a realization to the logical component.

Model the products “KampusIS” and “UniMatrika” as two Application Components and from each of them lead a realization to the same Application Service “Study Records”, which serves the Business Process “Semester Enrolment”. The logical application is not modelled as an element and its name is given in the properties of both components.

Model “Student Information System” as a logical Application Component, from which a realization leads to the Application Service “Study Records” serving the Business Process “Semester Enrolment”. Model the products “KampusIS” and “UniMatrika” as physical Application Components and lead a realization from the logical component to each of the two products.

Model “Student Information System” as a Business Function, to which assignment leads from the Application Components “KampusIS” and “UniMatrika”. From the Business Process “Semester Enrolment” a realization leads to this function, and the difference between the logical and the physical level is expressed by an access relationship led from the function to both products.
explanation: ArchiMate allows realization between two application components: a concrete (physical) component realizes a more abstract (logical) one; the logical component carries the service for the business, and replacing a product changes only the realization relationships beneath it (5). Two components realizing the same service are a valid model and show the independence of the process from the product, but the building block of the target map is missing (3). The 1-point option has the right elements but reverses the realization – the more abstract element would realize the more concrete one. The 0-point option moves the logical application into the business layer, assigns application components to a business function, and leads access to elements of active structure.

scenario:
The statutory city of Dubova wants to make it easier for citizens to deal with official matters. The following conclusions came out of a workshop with the secretary of the city hall. The main goal “Simplify citizens’ contact with the office” breaks down into two sub-goals: “Reduce citizens’ administrative burden” and “Shorten the time to process applications”. A general principle applicable to every future system of the city is to lead to the lower administrative burden: “The office needs to be told a piece of data only once”. From this principle follows a specific requirement for the planned citizen portal, “Forms are pre-filled with data from registers”, which is further divided into “Connection to the population register” and “Connection to the land registry”.

The secretary wants a view in which he can trace the path from each specific requirement to the main goal and see the breakdown of goals and requirements, as well as the principle by which the city’s other projects are to be guided.
question: Which model best matches the secretary’s requirement?
options: Goal “Simplify contact with the office” –aggregation→ goals “Reduce administrative burden” and “Shorten processing time”. Principle “Tell data only once” –realization→ goal “Reduce administrative burden”, and requirement “Pre-filled forms” –realization→ this principle. Requirement “Pre-filled forms” –aggregation→ requirements “Connection to the population register” and “Connection to the land registry”.

Goal “Simplify contact with the office” –aggregation→ goals “Reduce administrative burden” and “Shorten processing time”. Requirement “Pre-filled forms” –realization→ goal “Reduce administrative burden” and –aggregation→ requirements “Connection to the population register” and “Connection to the land registry”. The principle of telling data only once is given in the description of this requirement.

Goal “Simplify contact with the office” –aggregation→ goals “Reduce administrative burden” and “Shorten processing time”. Principle “Tell data only once” –realization→ goal “Reduce administrative burden”, and the same principle further –realization→ requirement “Pre-filled forms”. Requirement “Pre-filled forms” –aggregation→ requirements “Connection to the population register” and “Connection to the land registry”.

Model the main goal as a driver and this driver –triggering→ goals “Reduce administrative burden” and “Shorten processing time”. Capture the principle of telling data only once as a constraint and that –assignment→ stakeholder “Secretary”. Requirement “Pre-filled forms” –composition→ goal “Reduce administrative burden” and –serving→ requirements “Connection to the population register” and “Connection to the land registry”.
explanation: The breakdown of a goal into sub-goals and of a requirement into sub-requirements is expressed by aggregation between elements of the same type; realization leads from the more specific to the more abstract, that is, from the requirement to the principle and from the principle to the goal, so the path from a requirement to the main goal is traceable (5). The 3-point option is valid, because a requirement can realize a goal (by derivation), but the principle for the other projects has dropped out of the view. The 1-point option reverses the realization between the principle and the requirement: the general principle would realize the specific requirement. The 0-point option confuses a goal with a driver and uses triggering, assignment, serving and composition relationships between motivation elements of different types, which the language does not permit.

scenario:
The dairy Orlice has approved the strategy “Returnable glass packaging”: within two years to switch yoghurts and milk from plastic cups and bottles to returnable glass. The board is following two goals – “Reduce the ecological footprint of production” and “Keep production costs at today’s level”. The analysis by the operations division expects two results of the strategy. The intended result is the share of returnable packaging raised to 80%, which fulfils the goal of a lower ecological footprint. The side effect, an unintended result, is increased costs of collecting and washing the packaging, which, on the contrary, threaten the goal of keeping production costs. The strategy is to be enabled by the capability “Packaging reverse logistics”.

The chairman of the board wants to see, before the vote, in a single view both expected results of the strategy and how each of them affects the dairy’s goals, including the direction of this effect. The board members will receive the material a week before the meeting together with the financial analysis.
question: Which model best matches the requirement of the chairman of the board?
options: Course of action “Returnable glass packaging” –realization→ outcome “Share of returnable packaging raised to 80%” and that –realization→ goal “Reduce the ecological footprint of production”. The same course of action –influence→ outcome “Costs of collecting and washing packaging increased” with a positive sign and this outcome –influence→ goal “Keep production costs” with a negative sign. Capability “Packaging reverse logistics” –realization→ this course of action.

Course of action “Returnable glass packaging” –realization→ outcome “Share of returnable packaging raised to 80%” and that –realization→ goal “Reduce the ecological footprint of production”. The same course of action –influence→ outcome “Costs of collecting and washing packaging increased” and this outcome –influence→ goal “Keep production costs”; signs are not given. Capability “Packaging reverse logistics” –realization→ course of action.

Course of action “Returnable glass packaging” –realization→ outcome “Share of returnable packaging raised to 80%” and that –realization→ goal “Reduce the ecological footprint of production”. The same course of action –influence→ outcome “Costs of collecting and washing packaging increased” with a positive sign and this outcome –influence→ goal “Keep production costs” with the same sign. Capability “Packaging reverse logistics” –realization→ course of action.

Goals “Reduce the ecological footprint of production” and “Keep production costs” –triggering→ course of action “Returnable glass packaging”. Model the increase in the costs of collecting and washing packaging as a constraint with a link –assignment→ capability “Packaging reverse logistics”. Model the higher share of returnable glass packaging as a resource with links –realization→ course of action and –serving→ goal “Reduce the ecological footprint of production”.
explanation: A course of action can both realize and influence an outcome, and motivation elements can influence one another; the influence relationship carries a sign, so the intended result realizes the goal of a lower ecological footprint, whereas the unintended result influences the goal of keeping costs negatively (5). The 3-point option is valid and shows both results, but an influence with no sign given expresses only an unspecified effect, so the direction the chairman asks about cannot be read from it. The 1-point option captures both results, but with a positive sign it claims that the increased costs of collecting and washing contribute to the goal of keeping costs – the effect is in reality the opposite. The 0-point option has goals trigger the strategy and confuses the results with a constraint and a resource with impermissible relationships.
