scenario:
The Bystrice transport company is preparing a reorganisation and is considering spinning off some units into a subsidiary. The strategy director has a capability map and wants to link it with the business functions that currently provide the capabilities. The capability “Timetable planning” requires the cooperation of two functions, “Transport planning” and “Transport data analysis”: without either of them the company cannot compile timetables. The capability “Fare sales” is provided by the function “Sales and tariffs” alone. In addition, the function “Transport data analysis” alone provides the capability “Line load evaluation”.

The director needs the model to show which functions are jointly necessary for a given capability and thus cannot be separated from one another during the spin-off, and where a capability rests on a single function. She will present the model to the supervisory board together with the reorganisation proposal.
question: Which model best matches the need of the strategy director?
options: Business functions “Transport planning” and “Transport data analysis” –realization→ AND junction –realization→ capability “Timetable planning”. Business function “Sales and tariffs” –realization→ capability “Fare sales” and business function “Transport data analysis” by a further relationship –realization→ capability “Line load evaluation”.

Business functions “Transport planning” and “Transport data analysis” –realization→ AND junction –realization→ capability “Timetable planning”. Business function “Sales and tariffs” –realization→ capability “Fare sales”. The capability “Line load evaluation” remains unconnected in the view and its provision is described by the accompanying documentation of the capability map.

Business functions “Transport planning” and “Transport data analysis” –realization→ OR junction –realization→ capability “Timetable planning”. Business function “Sales and tariffs” –realization→ capability “Fare sales” and business function “Transport data analysis” by a further relationship –realization→ capability “Line load evaluation”.

Capability “Timetable planning” –assignment→ AND junction and into the same junction there also leads a realization from business function “Transport planning” and a serving from business function “Transport data analysis”. Capabilities “Fare sales” and “Line load evaluation” –composition→ business functions “Sales and tariffs” and “Transport data analysis”.
explanation: A capability is realized by internal behaviour, here business functions, and an AND junction on realization relationships explicitly says that the capability is provided by both functions together; a separate realization relationship shows a capability resting on a single function (5). The 3-point option uses the AND junction correctly, but for the capability “Line load evaluation” it does not show that it rests on a single function that is, moreover, tied into the joint realization of timetables – which is exactly what matters for the spin-off. An OR junction claims that the capability is provided by either function alone, which contradicts the brief (1). The 0-point option joins relationships of different types in one junction, which ArchiMate does not allow, and composes a capability of business functions with a composition relationship that does not exist between these types of elements.

image.alt: Two examples of a junction on a triggering relationship between processes: an AND junction (filled circle) and an OR junction (hollow circle), each with its reading.

scenario:
The family brewery Podhoran from the Jeseniky Mountains is preparing a strategy for the next five years. At a strategic workshop the owners wrote down four statements:
(1) “We have decided to move from selling through wholesalers to direct subscription sales to households.”
(2) “We can brew small batches of special beers and change the assortment quickly.”
(3) “From ordering the subscription to delivering the crate to the door – that is how value is created for the customer.”
(4) “We have our own brewhouse with protected recipes and an experienced team of brewers.”
The architect is to convert the statements into elements of the ArchiMate strategy layer and connect them so that the owners can see what the chosen direction rests on: what the brewery can do, with what it can do it, and where this shows up in creating value for the customer. The resulting view will serve as material for negotiations with the bank about a loan to expand the brewhouse.
question: Which model best converts the statements into the strategy layer and matches the owners’ need?
options: Capture the statements as (1) course of action, (2) capability, (3) value stream and (4) two resources. Both resources –assignment→ capability “Special beer production”. This capability –realization→ course of action “Direct subscription sales” and –serving→ value stream “Deliver the beer subscription”.

Capture the statements as (1) course of action, (2) capability, (3) value stream and (4) two resources. Both resources –assignment→ capability “Special beer production” and this capability –realization→ course of action “Direct subscription sales”. The value stream “Deliver the beer subscription” remains in the view as an unconnected element.

Capture the statements as (1) course of action, (2) capability, (3) value stream and (4) two resources. Both resources –assignment→ capability “Special beer production”. Course of action “Direct subscription sales” –realization→ this capability, which further –serving→ value stream “Deliver the beer subscription”.

Capture the statements as (1) goal, (2) business function, (3) business process and (4) two business objects. Business function “Special beer production” –composition→ both business objects and –triggering→ goal “Direct subscription sales”. Business process “Deliver the beer subscription” –access→ this goal and –assignment→ business function.
explanation: A decision about what the company will do is a course of action, what it can do is a capability, the sequence of activities creating value for the customer is a value stream, and the brewhouse, recipes and brewers are resources; a resource is assigned to a capability by an assignment relationship, a capability realizes a course of action and serves a value stream (5). The 3-point option is valid, but it leaves the value stream unconnected, so it does not show where the capability manifests in value creation. The 1-point option reverses the realization: a course of action does not realize a capability; on the contrary, it is realized by capabilities. The 0-point option chooses elements of other layers and aspects and connects them with impermissible relationships.

image.alt: Strategy elements and relationships: resource assigned to capability, capability serves value stream, strategy elements realize course of action, which realizes outcome, and core elements realize strategy elements.

scenario: The Beskydy Regional Hospital wants to offer chronic patients remote check-ups. The motivation model yielded the outcome “Chronic patient check-ups take place remotely” and two requirements: “The consultation takes place via a secure video call” and “The doctor has the measured values available before the consultation”. The hospital is not yet selecting specific systems or suppliers. The deputy for strategy first wants a solution concept at the strategic level: which resources the hospital needs for each requirement to be met and the outcome achieved. According to the working group, the video calls will be provided by the “Video consultation platform”, the measured values will be supplied by the “Patients’ home measuring devices”, and the outcome can be achieved only by combining the platform with “Doctors trained in telemedicine”. All three resources belong to the capability “Remote care”. The view should show, for each requirement and for the outcome, which resource fulfils it.
question: Which model best matches the requirement of the deputy for strategy?
options: Resource “Video consultation platform” –realization→ requirement “Secure video call” and resource “Home measuring devices” –realization→ requirement “Values before consultation”. Resources “Video consultation platform” and “Doctors trained in telemedicine” –realization→ AND junction –realization→ outcome “Remote check-ups”. Each of these three resources –assignment→ capability “Remote care”.

Resources “Video consultation platform”, “Home measuring devices” and “Doctors trained in telemedicine” –assignment→ capability “Remote care”. This capability –realization→ requirements “Secure video call” and “Values before consultation” and –realization→ outcome “Remote check-ups”. No relationships lead between the individual resources and requirements.

Requirement “Secure video call” –realization→ resource “Video consultation platform” and requirement “Values before consultation” –realization→ resource “Home measuring devices”. Outcome “Remote check-ups” –realization→ AND junction –realization→ resources “Video consultation platform” and “Doctors trained in telemedicine”. Each of these three resources further –assignment→ capability “Remote care”.

Model the resources as business objects “Video consultation platform”, “Home measuring devices” and “Doctors trained in telemedicine”; the requirements “Secure video call” and “Values before consultation” access them through an access relationship. Outcome “Remote check-ups” –assignment→ capability “Remote care” and that –composition→ these business objects.
explanation: A resource can realize a requirement, and the combination of several jointly necessary resources is expressed by an AND junction on realization relationships; assignment to a capability shows which capability the resources belong to; the concept thus stays at the strategic level and for each requirement and for the outcome the resource that fulfils it is visible (5). The 3-point option is valid – a capability can realize requirements and an outcome – but it does not say which resource fulfils which requirement. The 1-point option has the right elements, but reverses the realization: an abstract requirement would realize a concrete resource. The 0-point option confuses resources with business objects and uses access, assignment and composition relationships where the language does not permit them.

question: Which summary of the view is the most correct?
options: Receiving the order triggers collection planning, and after it both follow-up activities begin, container delivery and advance invoice issuing. Planning passes the route plan to vehicle fleet management; triggering of the function does not follow from this. Planning writes the collection plan and container delivery reads it. The driver role is a member of the crew and at the same time of the service call-out.

Receiving the order triggers collection planning, and after it both follow-up activities begin, container delivery and advance invoice issuing. Planning is also connected in some way with the vehicle fleet management function. Both planning and container delivery work with the collection plan. The crew consists of the driver and loader roles, the driver takes part in the service call-out.

Receiving the order triggers collection planning, and after it one of the follow-up activities begins, container delivery or advance invoice issuing. Planning passes the route plan to vehicle fleet management; triggering of the function does not follow from this. Planning writes the collection plan and container delivery reads it. The driver role is a member of the crew and at the same time of the service call-out.

Receiving the order triggers collection planning, and it reads the collection plan, whereas container delivery writes it. Completed planning triggers vehicle fleet management by passing the route plan and only after it one of the two follow-up activities, container delivery or advance invoice issuing. The driver role belongs to a single collaboration, and that is the collection crew.
explanation: An AND junction on triggering relationships means that both activities begin after planning; flow expresses the passing of information and does not imply causality; the arrowhead of an access relationship at the object denotes writing, the arrowhead at the behaviour denotes reading; and an element can be part of more than one aggregation (5). The 3-point option contains nothing untrue, but it does not distinguish the nature of the flow, the direction of access to the object or the sharing of the role. The 1-point option reads the AND junction as a choice of one branch, the rest is correct. The 0-point option swaps reading and writing, attributes triggering to the flow, reads the junction as a choice and interprets aggregation as exclusive membership.

image.alt: Overview of the notation of all ArchiMate relationships divided into structural, dependency, dynamic and other, including the AND and OR junctions.

question: Which conclusion of the check is the most correct?
options: Three relationships contradict the rules. Replace relationship (2) with an association between the driver and the goal, reverse relationship (3) to requirement –realization→ goal, and reverse relationship (5) to resource “UX team” –assignment→ capability. Relationships (1), (4) and (6) are fine and remain unchanged.

Three relationships contradict the rules. Replace relationship (2) with an association between the driver and the goal, reverse relationship (3) to requirement –realization→ goal, and replace relationship (5) with an association between the capability and the resource “UX team”. Relationships (1), (4) and (6) are fine.

Two relationships contradict the rules. Replace relationship (2) with an association between the driver and the goal and reverse relationship (3) to requirement –realization→ goal. Relationship (5) is a common way of connecting a resource to a capability and relationships (1), (4) and (6) are fine as well.

Two relationships contradict the rules. Reverse relationship (4) to course of action –realization→ capability “Customer experience design” and reverse relationship (6) to capability –realization→ business process. Relationships (1), (2), (3) and (5) are fine and remain unchanged.
explanation: A driver is connected to a goal by an association relationship; triggering belongs among behaviour elements, not among motivation elements; realization leads from the more specific requirement to the goal and assignment from the resource to the capability, not the other way round; a capability realizes a course of action and a business process realizes a capability, so relationships (4) and (6) are correct (5). The 3-point option finds the same errors, but replaces relationship (5) with a generic association, which is valid but does not say that the resource is assigned to the capability. The 1-point option keeps the impermissible assignment from a capability to a resource. The 0-point option marks exactly the correct relationships as faulty and proposes reversing them to an impermissible direction.

image.alt: Strategy elements and relationships: resource assigned to capability, capability serves value stream, strategy elements realize course of action, which realizes outcome, and core elements realize strategy elements.

scenario:
The Technical University in Tabor operates two physical servers, HV-01 and HV-02, in its server room. On each of them runs a hypervisor that hosts virtual servers. On HV-01 these are the virtual server of the study system with the Linux operating system and the virtual server of the finance system with the Windows Server operating system; HV-02 hosts the virtual servers of the library and of e-learning. The hypervisor vendor has released a critical security patch whose installation requires a restart of the hypervisor, and thereby of all the virtual servers running on it.

The head of infrastructure plans to patch physical server by physical server so that all of the university’s systems never stand still at the same time. He needs a technology-layer model that distinguishes hardware from software, shows that the operating systems of the virtual servers run on the hypervisor and that it runs on the physical server, and captures the virtual servers as separate units onto which applications are deployed.
question: Which model best matches the need of the head of infrastructure?
options: Device “HV-01” –assignment→ System Software “Hypervisor” and that –assignment→ System Software “Linux” and “Windows Server”. Each of the two operating systems is part (composition) of its own Node: “Study system virtual server” and “Finance system virtual server” respectively. Server HV-02 is modelled in the same way.

Node “HV-01 virtualisation platform” is composed (composition) of Device “HV-01” and of System Software “Hypervisor”, “Linux” and “Windows Server”, which are listed in it side by side. The virtual servers do not appear separately in the model, their names are written in the description of the operating systems. Server HV-02 is modelled in the same way.

System Software “Linux” and “Windows Server” –assignment→ System Software “Hypervisor” and that –assignment→ Device “HV-01”. Each of these operating systems is part (composition) of its own Node: “Study system virtual server” and “Finance system virtual server” respectively. Server HV-02 is modelled in the same way.

Facility “HV-01” –realization→ Application Component “Hypervisor” and that –aggregation→ Artifacts “Study system” and “Finance system”, which are the virtual servers. The operating systems “Linux” and “Windows Server” are Technology Services of which these artifacts are composed (composition). Server HV-02 is modelled in the same way.
explanation: The assignment relationship leads from the host to what runs on it: from the Device to the System Software (hypervisor) and from it to further System Software (the hosted operating systems); a virtual server as a separate unit is expressed by a Node composed of its system software (5). The 3-point option is valid – a Node is composed of a device and system software – but it does not show what runs on what, nor the virtual servers as units, so the impact of a hypervisor restart cannot be read from it. The 1-point option has the right elements, but reverses the assignment chain: the operating systems would host the hypervisor and that the physical server on which it actually runs. The 0-point option confuses layers and aspects – a hypervisor is not an application component, a physical server is not a Facility and an operating system is not a service.

image.alt: Deployment chain: a node composed of a device and system software, system software assigned to an artifact, an artifact realizes an application component and a data object.

scenario:
The payment institution PlatimTo processes instant payments through a pair of message brokers: one node runs in a data centre in Prague, the other in Brno. A message with a payment order is considered received only at the moment when both nodes jointly confirm it by a two-phase commit; neither node on its own therefore provides guaranteed delivery. The pair is neither a separately managed device nor a product – each node has its own operations team and the nodes cooperate only in this confirmation. The institution’s payment applications use guaranteed message delivery as a technology service.

The infrastructure architect is preparing a risk analysis for the case of an outage of one data centre. He needs a model that makes it clear that the service arises from the joint behaviour of both nodes, not from the behaviour of either of them, and that the pair of nodes is merely a logical connection of two separate elements.
question: Which model best captures how the guaranteed delivery service arises?
options: Technology Collaboration “Broker pair” –aggregation→ Node “Broker Prague” and Node “Broker Brno”. The collaboration –assignment→ Technology Interaction “Two-phase message confirmation” and this interaction –realization→ Technology Service “Guaranteed message delivery”, which serves (serving) the payment applications.

Node “Broker cluster” is composed of Node “Broker Prague” and Node “Broker Brno”. The cluster –assignment→ Technology Function “Message confirmation” and this function –realization→ Technology Service “Guaranteed message delivery”, which serves (serving) the institution’s payment applications.

Technology Collaboration “Broker pair” –aggregation→ Node “Broker Prague” and Node “Broker Brno”. The collaboration –assignment→ Technology Interaction “Two-phase message confirmation” and Technology Service “Guaranteed message delivery” –realization→ this interaction; the service serves (serving) the payment applications.

Technology Interaction “Broker pair” –aggregation→ Node “Broker Prague” and Node “Broker Brno”. Technology Collaboration “Two-phase message confirmation” is a joint behaviour that –triggering→ Technology Interface “Guaranteed message delivery”; this interface serves (serving) the institution’s payment applications.
explanation: The joint behaviour of two or more technology elements is a Technology Interaction performed by a Technology Collaboration – a logical grouping aggregating both nodes that does not exist as a separate entity; the interaction then realizes the service (5). The 3-point option is valid, but it turns the pair into a single composite node with its own function, so the fact that it is only a logical connection and joint behaviour is lost. The 1-point option has the collaboration and the interaction right, but reverses the realization: a service is realized by internal behaviour, not the other way round. The 0-point option confuses structure and behaviour – an interaction cannot aggregate nodes, a collaboration is not behaviour and an interface is not a service.

scenario:
The Podhuri Roads Authority monitors the condition of 900 km of roads using devices distributed in the field: weather stations, road surface temperature sensors and traffic counters. All these devices work the same way – after being switched on they download their settings, for example the measurement interval, from a central telemetry server and then continuously send it the measured values. The server is located at the organisation’s headquarters; it offers the distribution of settings and the reception of measurements as its services through a single MQTT interface. In winter, the measured values are used to decide on gritter deployments.

The telemetry administrator is preparing to purchase further types of sensors from a new supplier. He needs a model that shows that the individual types of device are kinds of the same thing, where their data flows, and which server services the devices use and through which access point. Based on the model he wants to give the supplier an unambiguous brief for connecting the new sensors.
question: Which model best matches the need of the telemetry administrator?
options: Equipment “Weather station”, “Road sensor” and “Traffic counter” are specializations of Equipment “Field device”, from which a flow relationship leads to Node “Telemetry server”. Part of the server is Technology Interface “MQTT interface” assigned to Technology Service “Settings distribution” and “Measurement reception”; a serving relationship leads from these services to the field device.

Equipment “Weather station”, “Road sensor” and “Traffic counter” are specializations of Equipment “Field device”, from which a flow relationship leads to Node “Telemetry server”. The server’s services and its interface do not appear separately in the model; the way settings are downloaded and measurements are passed on is described by technical documentation attached to the node.

Equipment “Weather station”, “Road sensor” and “Traffic counter” are specializations of Equipment “Field device”, from which a flow relationship leads to Node “Telemetry server”. Part of the server is Technology Interface “MQTT interface” assigned to Technology Service “Settings distribution” and “Measurement reception”; a serving relationship leads from the field device to these two services.

Business Actor “Weather station”, “Road sensor” and “Traffic counter” are specializations of Business Role “Field device”, to which a flow leads from Application Component “Telemetry server”. Part of the server is Business Interface “MQTT interface” assigned to Business Service “Settings distribution” and “Measurement reception”; a serving relationship leads from the device to the server.
explanation: The individual types of sensor are specializations of a general Equipment, the flow of data to the server is expressed by flow, and the server’s services are made accessible through a Technology Interface that is part of it and is assigned to the services serving the devices (5). The 3-point option is valid, but it lacks the services and the access point, that is, the main thing the administrator is to hand over to the supplier. The 1-point option has all the elements, but reverses serving: the server provides functionality to the devices, not the devices to the server’s services. The 0-point option moves the physical devices and the server into the business and application layers and leads the data flow in the opposite direction.

scenario:
The dairy Jasna pasteurises milk in a pasteurisation station located in production hall 2. The station consists of a plate pasteuriser and control software that runs directly in the station. Every second the software takes measured temperatures and flow rates from the pasteuriser and sends it back commands for setting the valves and heating; without this exchange the pasteuriser does not maintain the prescribed temperature of 72 °C. The supplier has announced the end of support for the current version of the control software.

The automation manager is preparing to replace the software with a new version during a planned shutdown. He needs a model that shows what is the machine and what is the software, that together they form one station, in which building the station stands, and what exchange between the machine and the software takes place in both directions. He does not require production procedures or raw materials in this model; the dairy has those described in a separate production view.
question: Which model best matches the need of the automation manager?
options: Part of Facility “Production hall 2” is Node “Pasteurisation station”, which is composed of Equipment “Plate pasteuriser” and System Software “Pasteurisation control software”. From the pasteuriser a flow relationship “measurements” leads to the software and from the software to the pasteuriser a flow relationship “commands”.

Part of Facility “Production hall 2” is Node “Pasteurisation station”, which is composed of Equipment “Plate pasteuriser” and System Software “Pasteurisation control software”. The pasteuriser and the software are connected by a single association relationship; the measurements and commands are described in the station documentation.

Equipment “Plate pasteuriser” is composed of Node “Pasteurisation station” and Facility “Production hall 2”; part of the station is System Software “Pasteurisation control software”. From the pasteuriser a flow relationship “measurements” leads to the software and from the software to the pasteuriser a flow relationship “commands”.

Part of Business Actor “Production hall 2” is Business Process “Pasteurisation station”, to which Material “Plate pasteuriser” and Data Object “Pasteurisation control software” are assigned. From the pasteuriser a triggering relationship “measurements” leads to the software and from the software to the pasteuriser a triggering relationship “commands”.
explanation: ArchiMate 3.2 allows a Node to be composed of both Equipment and System Software and such a node to be part of a Facility; the two-way exchange between the machine and the software is expressed by two flow relationships (5). The 3-point option has the same valid structure, but a non-specific association replaces the flows of measurements and commands that the manager explicitly asks about. The 1-point option has the right elements and flows, but reverses the composition: a machine cannot be composed of a station or of the building in which it stands. The 0-point option confuses the station with a business process, the machine with material, the software with data and the building with an actor.

scenario:
The leasing company AutoKredit operates two web applications: the Instalment Calculator and the Client Portal. The supplier delivers them as deployable archives kalkulacka.war and portal.war. Both archives are built according to the same standard web archive, a fixed part of which is the library pdf-export.jar for printing documents. The archives are deployed on the WildFly application server. A serious vulnerability was published last week in the library pdf-export.jar.

The security manager must decide within 48 hours on the scope of an emergency fix. He needs a model from which the relationships between elements will show which deployable units contain the vulnerable library, on which system software they are deployed, and which application components they realize. He wants to use the same model for future vulnerability reports in other libraries, and therefore does not want to look up information about libraries in text descriptions.
question: Which model best serves the security manager?
options: Artifact “Standard web archive” is composed (composition) of Artifact “pdf-export.jar”; Artifacts “kalkulacka.war” and “portal.war” are its specializations. From System Software “WildFly” an assignment relationship leads to both archives, which realize Application Component “Instalment Calculator” and “Client Portal” respectively.

Artifacts “kalkulacka.war” and “portal.war” have pdf-export.jar recorded in their “libraries” attribute (property); the library is not a separate element of the model. From System Software “WildFly” an assignment relationship leads to both archives, which realize Application Component “Instalment Calculator” and “Client Portal” respectively.

Artifact “pdf-export.jar” is composed (composition) of Artifact “Standard web archive”, whose specializations are “kalkulacka.war” and “portal.war”. From System Software “WildFly” an assignment relationship leads to both archives, which realize Application Component “Instalment Calculator” and “Client Portal” respectively.

Data Object “pdf-export.jar” is composed (composition) of Application Components “Instalment Calculator” and “Client Portal”; the archives kalkulacka.war and portal.war are Application Interfaces of these components. From both components a realization relationship leads to Application Service “WildFly”, on which both web applications are deployed.
explanation: An artifact can be composed of sub-artifacts and concrete archives can be modelled as specializations of a general archive, so a chain of relationships leads from the library to both deployable units, to the system software on which they are deployed, and to the components they realize (5). The 3-point option is valid, but it hides the library in an attribute, so the impact of the vulnerability cannot be read from the relationships. The 1-point option reverses the composition – the library would be composed of the archive of which it is in fact a part. The 0-point option leaves the technology layer: a library is not a data object, archives are not interfaces and an application server is not an application service.

scenario:
The wooden toy manufacturer Drevik has three operations: a sawmill in Hlinsko, a production plant in Vsetin and a distribution warehouse in Olomouc. The sawmill supplies beech timber to the plant. In the plant a machining and lacquering line makes construction sets from it, which are transported to the distribution warehouse and from there to customers. After last year’s outage of timber supplies, production stood still for two weeks and nobody knew in advance which operation depends on what.

The supply chain manager wants a simple model of the physical layer that shows what happens to the material in each operation and what material moves between the operations and in which direction. She is not dealing with routes, carriers or transport infrastructure now; she will add those in the next stage, in which she will assess alternative ways of transport between the operations.
question: Which model best matches the need of the supply chain manager?
options: Facility “Hlinsko sawmill” –flow→ Facility “Vsetin plant” –flow→ Facility “Olomouc warehouse”; Material “Beech timber” is associated with the first flow, Material “Construction sets” with the second. Part of the plant is Equipment “Machining and lacquering line” assigned to Technology Process “Construction set production”, which reads the timber and writes the construction sets.

Facilities “Hlinsko sawmill”, “Vsetin plant” and “Olomouc warehouse” are connected by two Paths realized by Distribution Network “Road network”. Part of the plant is Equipment “Machining and lacquering line” assigned to Technology Process “Construction set production”, which reads Material “Beech timber” and writes Material “Construction sets”.

Facility “Olomouc warehouse” –flow→ Facility “Vsetin plant” –flow→ Facility “Hlinsko sawmill”; Material “Construction sets” is associated with the first flow, Material “Beech timber” with the second. Part of the plant is Equipment “Machining and lacquering line” assigned to Technology Process “Construction set production”, which reads the beech timber and writes the construction sets.

Business Actor “Hlinsko sawmill” –triggering→ Business Actor “Vsetin plant” –triggering→ Business Actor “Olomouc warehouse”; Business Object “Beech timber” is associated with the first relationship, Business Object “Construction sets” with the second. The line is represented by an Application Component assigned to Business Process “Construction set production”, which reads the timber.
explanation: The movement of material between operations is expressed by a flow relationship between Facilities, with which the transferred Material can be associated; the processing is shown by Equipment assigned to a technology process that accesses the material (5). The 3-point option is valid, but Path and Distribution Network say only that the operations are connected – not what travels between them and in which direction – and the manager is not dealing with routes yet. The 1-point option uses the right elements, but leads both flows in the opposite direction, so the warehouse would supply the sawmill. The 0-point option replaces the physical elements with business and application ones and the material with information.

scenario:
The health insurer Zdravi Plus issues payers of insurance premiums certificates of no arrears. A payer can request one at a branch, where an officer handles the request in the process “Certificate issuing at a branch”. Since last year the same service can be obtained in the client portal: after login the portal itself verifies the status of the payer’s account and issues the certificate with an electronic seal, without any employee intervening. From the point of view of both the payer and the law it is one and the same service of the insurer, only provided in a different way. Today 60% of certificates are created through the portal.

The head of client services wants a model that makes it clear that one business service is provided in two ways – by human work at a branch and fully automatically by the portal. She will use the model when assessing the impact of a portal outage and when planning the further transfer of clients to the online channel.
question: Which model best matches the requirement of the head of client services?
options: Business Service “Issuing a certificate of no arrears” –serving→ Business Role “Premium payer”. A realization leads to the service from two elements: from Business Process “Certificate issuing at a branch”, to which Business Role “Officer” is assigned, and from Application Service “Online certificate issuing”, which is realized by Application Component “Client Portal”.

Business Role “Premium payer” is served by two services: Business Service “Certificate at a branch”, to which a realization leads from Business Process “Certificate issuing at a branch” with the assigned role “Officer”, and Business Service “Certificate online”, to which a realization leads from Application Service “Online certificate issuing” of the component “Client Portal”.

Business Service “Issuing a certificate of no arrears” –serving→ Business Role “Premium payer”. A realization leads to the service from Business Process “Certificate issuing at a branch”, to which Business Role “Officer” is assigned; from this business service a realization then leads to Application Service “Online certificate issuing”, which is realized by Application Component “Client Portal”.

The Client Portal is a Business Role assigned to Business Process “Certificate issuing at a branch” together with the role “Officer”. Application Service “Online certificate issuing” is composed of Business Service “Issuing a certificate of no arrears” and that is assigned to Business Role “Premium payer”, who obtains the certificate at a branch and also online in the client portal.
explanation: Cross-layer relationships allow an application service to realize a business service – this is how a fully automated provision of a service is modelled; the same business service can at the same time be realized by a business process, so the 5-point model shows one service with two ways of provision. The 3-point option uses valid relationships, but splits the service in two, losing the fact that it is the same service. The 1-point option reverses the realization between layers: the more concrete application service realizes the more abstract business service, not the other way round. The 0-point option turns an application into a business role, composes an application service of a business service and assigns a service to a role, which are impermissible confusions of structure and behaviour.

scenario:
The Emergency Medical Service of the Vysoka Region dispatches crews with the application Operations Control. The application is delivered as a single deployable package operacni-rizeni.ear. The same package is deployed on two server clusters: on the primary one in Jihlava and on the standby one in Trebic, which takes over operation if the primary fails. The application provides the application services “Emergency call reception” and “Crew dispatch”, without which the business process “Incident management” at the operations centre cannot function.

After a recent power outage in Jihlava, the region’s crisis manager wants to demonstrate that the process “Incident management” does not depend on a single location. He needs a model across all layers that shows that the same application is carried by two different clusters and that leads from the process through the application services to the specific clusters. The model will be presented to the region’s security council.
question: Which model best demonstrates that the process does not depend on a single cluster?
options: From Device “Primary cluster Jihlava” and likewise from Device “Standby cluster Trebic” an assignment relationship leads to the same Artifact “operacni-rizeni.ear”, from which a realization leads to Application Component “Operations Control”. The component realizes Application Service “Emergency call reception” and “Crew dispatch”, which serve Business Process “Incident management”.

From a single Device “EMS server infrastructure”, which includes both clusters, an assignment relationship leads to Artifact “operacni-rizeni.ear”, from which a realization leads to Application Component “Operations Control”. The component realizes Application Service “Emergency call reception” and “Crew dispatch”, which serve Business Process “Incident management”.

From the same Artifact “operacni-rizeni.ear” an assignment relationship leads to Device “Primary cluster Jihlava” and to Device “Standby cluster Trebic”; from the artifact a realization leads to Application Component “Operations Control”. The component realizes Application Service “Emergency call reception” and “Crew dispatch”, which serve Business Process “Incident management”.

From Business Process “Incident management” a composition relationship leads to Device “Primary cluster Jihlava” and to Device “Standby cluster Trebic”; the package operacni-rizeni.ear is a Business Object, from which a realization leads to both clusters. Application Service “Emergency call reception” and “Crew dispatch” are assigned to Application Component “Operations Control”.
explanation: The same deployment in two places is expressed by two assignment relationships from two devices to a single artifact that realizes the application component; from it a chain leads through the application services to the process, so it is visible that the process survives the outage of one cluster (5). The 3-point option is valid, but it merges both clusters into one device, so independence of a single location cannot be read from it. The 1-point option has the right elements, but reverses the assignment: an artifact is a passive element and cannot be the source of an assignment relationship – deployment is expressed by an assignment led from the device to the artifact. The 0-point option composes a business process of devices, makes the package a business object and assigns services to the component in the opposite direction.

scenario:
The online pharmacy Zdravenka, which dispatches around 2,000 parcels a day, dispatches orders only after payment. When the bank confirms the payment, the system Cash Desk Online records it as the state change “Payment confirmed” and immediately starts its own application process “Tax document issuing”. For the pharmacy’s operations the same moment means the event “Order paid”, which starts the business process “Order picking” performed by dispatchers. Last month the payment confirmations from the bank were delayed twice by several hours and dispatch stood still without anyone knowing why.

The owner of the picking process wants a model that keeps the business and application views separate but shows what stands behind the event that starts her process in IT. Based on the model she wants to agree with IT on monitoring of delayed confirmations and on a fallback procedure for the case of another delay.
question: Which model best matches the requirement of the process owner?
options: Application Event “Payment confirmed” –realization→ Business Event “Order paid” and that –triggering→ Business Process “Order picking”, to which Business Role “Dispatcher” is assigned. The application event at the same time –triggering→ Application Process “Tax document issuing” of the component “Cash Desk Online”.

Business Event “Order paid” –triggering→ Business Process “Order picking”, to which Business Role “Dispatcher” is assigned. Separately from that, Application Event “Payment confirmed” –triggering→ Application Process “Tax document issuing” of the component “Cash Desk Online”; the two events are not connected to each other.

Business Event “Order paid” –realization→ Application Event “Payment confirmed” and –triggering→ Business Process “Order picking”, to which Business Role “Dispatcher” is assigned. The application event at the same time –triggering→ Application Process “Tax document issuing” of the component “Cash Desk Online”.

Application Service “Payment confirmed” –assignment→ Business Role “Dispatcher” and Business Process “Order picking” –realization→ Application Process “Tax document issuing” of the component “Cash Desk Online”. The event “Order paid” is a Business Object that this component passes to the pharmacy’s dispatch for picking.
explanation: Between layers an application event can realize a business event: the 5-point model thus keeps both views separate while showing that behind the start of the picking process stands a change of state in Cash Desk Online. The 3-point option uses valid relationships, but leaves the events unconnected, so the owner cannot tell from the model what in IT her process depends on. The 1-point option has the right elements, but reverses the realization – the more abstract business event cannot realize an application one. The 0-point option confuses an event with a service and with a business object and assigns a service to a role, which ArchiMate does not permit.

scenario:
The roastery Zrnko offers households a “Coffee subscription”. For a monthly price the customer receives a package of freshly roasted coffee, its delivery home and the ability to manage the subscription in a web self-service portal (changing the type of coffee, pausing deliveries). The rights and obligations of both parties are governed by the Subscription Terms. The roastery roasts the coffee itself: a roaster in the production plant in Kromeriz processes green coffee into roasted coffee. Four thousand households currently subscribe, and management is considering a second variant with capsules instead of coffee beans.

The product manager needs a model that shows everything the customer receives as part of the subscription as one whole – including the goods themselves – and that links the goods to their production. Based on the model she wants to assess which parts of the offer can be used unchanged in the new variant and which will be replaced.
question: Which model best captures the Coffee subscription?
options: Product “Coffee subscription” aggregates Material “Roasted coffee”, Business Service “Home delivery”, Application Service “Online subscription management” and Contract “Subscription terms”. Equipment “Roaster” is assigned to Technology Process “Roasting”, which reads Material “Green coffee” and writes Material “Roasted coffee”.

Product “Coffee subscription” aggregates Business Service “Home delivery”, Application Service “Online subscription management” and Contract “Subscription terms”; the goods are given in the text description of this product. Equipment “Roaster” is assigned to Technology Process “Roasting”, which reads Material “Green coffee” and writes Material “Roasted coffee”.

Product “Coffee subscription” aggregates Equipment “Roaster”, Technology Process “Roasting”, Business Service “Home delivery”, Application Service “Online subscription management” and Contract “Subscription terms”. Technology process “Roasting” reads Material “Green coffee” and writes Material “Roasted coffee”.

Business Process “Coffee subscription” aggregates Data Object “Roasted coffee”, Business Service “Home delivery”, Application Service “Online subscription management” and Requirement “Subscription terms”. Business Actor “Roaster” is assigned to Application Process “Roasting”, which reads Material “Green coffee” and writes Data Object “Roasted coffee”.
explanation: A Product brings together the services and passive elements offered as a whole together with a contract; physical goods are Material, which can be aggregated into the product and at the same time shown as the output of a technology process performed by equipment (5). The 3-point option is valid, but the goods are missing in the product, although it is precisely they that are to change in the new variant. The 1-point option puts into the product the means of production instead of the goods – neither equipment nor an internal technology process can be aggregated by a product, and the customer does not receive them. The 0-point option confuses a product with a process, goods with data, a contract with a requirement and a machine with an actor.

scenario:
The construction company Stavby Morava is replacing two outdated systems: accounting and the construction management system. It cannot afford both at once, and is therefore considering two paths. In path A it first introduces a new ERP and operates it for a year with the old construction management system; in path B, on the contrary, it first introduces the new construction management system alongside the old accounting. Both paths end in the same target state with both new systems. Only one of them will be taken; the board will decide in June based on supplier offers.

The finance director wants a single migration view for the board from which it will be evident that paths A and B are alternatives leading from the same baseline to the same target state, and what applications make up the architecture in each of the intermediate states. He does not want to see work, projects or dates in this view.
question: Which model best captures both considered paths?
options: Plateau “Baseline” –triggering→ OR junction, from which triggering leads to plateau “Transition A: new ERP” and to plateau “Transition B: new construction management”; from both triggering leads through another OR junction to plateau “Target”. Each plateau –aggregation→ the applications valid in that state.

Plateau “Baseline” –triggering→ plateau “Transition A: new ERP” –triggering→ plateau “Target”; path B is described in a note at the baseline as a fallback option in case of unfavourable offers. Each of the three plateaus –aggregation→ the applications valid in that state.

Plateau “Baseline” –triggering→ AND junction, from which triggering leads to plateau “Transition A: new ERP” and to plateau “Transition B: new construction management”; from both triggering leads through another AND junction to plateau “Target”. Each plateau –aggregation→ the applications valid in that state.

Paths A and B are work packages “ERP first” and “Construction management first”, which –aggregation→ the applications introduced in that step and of which plateau “Target” is composed. The baseline is not modelled in the view; the difference between the two paths is shown by a gap associated with both work packages.
explanation: Alternative intermediate states are separate plateaus, and the fact that only one of them will occur is expressed by an OR junction on triggering relationships between plateaus; the aggregated applications show the architecture of each state (5). The 3-point option is valid, but it shows one path, so the board has nothing to compare. The 1-point option has the right plateaus, but an AND junction claims that both intermediate states will occur, that is, that it is concurrency, not a choice. The 0-point option confuses architecture states with work – a work package cannot aggregate applications, a plateau is not composed of work packages and a gap is tied to two plateaus.

image.alt: Two examples of a junction on a triggering relationship between processes: an AND junction (filled circle) and an OR junction (hollow circle), each with its reading.

scenario:
The Zlaty Klas bakeries are introducing a new production planning system. The programme has three consecutive projects. The project “Analysis and Design” creates the “Requirements Catalogue” and the “Target Architecture Design”; together, the two documents make up the “Tender Documentation”. The project “Supplier Selection” builds on the tender documentation and its result is the “Supplier Contract”. The project “Implementation” then works according to the target architecture design and according to the contract. The analysis already has a month’s delay and there is a risk that the whole programme will be delayed.

The head of the project office needs a model from which it will be visible, for each output, which project creates it and which later projects need it as an input. Based on it, she wants to evaluate everything that a delay of a single output will put at risk. She does not require milestones or responsible persons in this view.
question: Which model best matches the need of the head of the project office?
options: Work package “Analysis and Design” writes, via an access relationship, deliverables “Requirements Catalogue” and “Target Architecture Design”; deliverable “Tender Documentation” aggregates both. Work package “Supplier Selection” reads the tender documentation via an access relationship and writes deliverable “Supplier Contract”; work package “Implementation” reads the architecture design and the contract.

Work package “Analysis and Design” writes, via an access relationship, deliverables “Requirements Catalogue” and “Target Architecture Design”, and work package “Supplier Selection” writes deliverable “Supplier Contract”. The sequence of projects is expressed by triggering from the analysis to the supplier selection and from it to the implementation; the projects’ inputs are not captured in the model.

Work package “Analysis and Design” writes, via an access relationship, deliverables “Requirements Catalogue” and “Target Architecture Design”; deliverable “Tender Documentation” aggregates both. From the tender documentation triggering leads to work package “Supplier Selection”, which writes deliverable “Supplier Contract”; from the contract and from the architecture design triggering leads to work package “Implementation”.

Work package “Analysis and Design” realizes plateaus “Requirements Catalogue” and “Target Architecture Design”; the difference between them is expressed by gap “Tender Documentation”. From these plateaus triggering leads to plateau “Supplier Contract” and the projects “Supplier Selection” and “Implementation” are implementation events that aggregate these plateaus.
explanation: A deliverable is a passive element: a work package creates it through an access relationship (write) or uses it as an input (read), and a composite output is expressed by aggregation of deliverables, so for each output both its origin and its consumers are visible; for the link between a work package and a deliverable, ArchiMate 3.2 recommends access and labels the earlier realization deprecated (5). The 3-point option is valid, but it shows the order of the projects, not which output is whose input. The 1-point option has the outputs right, but a deliverable as a passive element cannot be the source of a triggering relationship. The 0-point option confuses outputs with architecture states and projects with events.

image.alt: Implementation & Migration elements: work package, deliverable, implementation event, plateau and gap with their relationships, including a note on the deprecated realization.

scenario:
The retail cooperative Jednota Podlesi is merging the IT of three formerly independent cooperatives in the programme “IT Consolidation”. The project “Cash Register Unification” replaces the cash register systems Register A and Register B with a single system Register Uni. The project “Sales Analytics” brings the new application Reporting and, for it, the node Analytics Platform. The project “Server Renewal” delivers the new Cluster 2 and the old Server S1 will be retired. The accounting system Accounting remains unchanged. Board members cannot find their way around the existing project schedules and are asking what exactly they will get for their money.

The IT director wants a single view that shows, for each project, which specific applications and nodes it brings, and for each application and node whether it exists today, in the target state, or in both. The projects’ partial outputs and milestones are not to be in the view.
question: Which model best matches the requirement of the IT director?
options: From each work package a realization leads to the elements it brings: “Cash Register Unification” → “Register Uni”, “Sales Analytics” → “Reporting” and “Analytics Platform”, “Server Renewal” → “Cluster 2”. Plateau “Baseline” and plateau “Target” aggregate the elements that belong to them; “Accounting” is aggregated by both and the view distinguishes membership by colour.

From each work package an access leads to its deliverable, for example “Deployed registers”, “Sales analytics put into operation” and “New servers”, and from the deliverables a realization leads to plateau “Target”. Plateau “Baseline” –triggering→ plateau “Target”; the individual applications and nodes are listed in the description of the deliverables.

From the elements a realization leads to the work package that brings them: “Register Uni” → “Cash Register Unification”, “Reporting” and “Analytics Platform” → “Sales Analytics”, “Cluster 2” → “Server Renewal”. Plateau “Baseline” and plateau “Target” aggregate the elements that belong to them; “Accounting” is aggregated by both and the view distinguishes membership by colour.

From each plateau a composition leads to the elements changed by the project: plateau “Cash Register Unification” → the cash register systems, plateau “Sales Analytics” → “Reporting”, plateau “Server Renewal” → both servers. The baseline and target states are implementation events between which a flow relationship leads, and “Accounting” is left out of the model.
explanation: A work package can realize the core elements it brings, and a plateau aggregates the elements valid in a given state; the 5-point view thus links the projects with specific applications and nodes and shows by colour their membership in the states. The 3-point option is valid, but it hides the specific applications and nodes in the description of the deliverables, which the IT director moreover does not want in the view. The 1-point option has the right elements and plateaus, but leads the realization from the applications and nodes to the projects, that is, the wrong way round. The 0-point option confuses projects with states and states with events, and leaves out the unchanged system, although it belongs to both states.

scenario:
The Bela city transport company is replacing the ticketing system in its vehicles. The architect received the following statements from the project management and is to capture them with Implementation and Migration elements:
(1) By the end of March an audit of the existing ticketing system will take place.
(2) The result of the audit will be a report with recommendations, which will be approved by the company’s management.
(3) From July to December the old and the new system will run side by side in the vehicles.
(4) On 1 January the old system will be switched off in all vehicles.
(5) Compared to today, in the target state payment by bank card will be added and the sale of paper tickets by the driver will cease.

Management wants the model to make clear what is work of limited duration, what is its result, what is a moment in time, what is a stable state of the architecture and what is a statement of a difference. The model will serve as the basis of a migration plan approved by the city council.
question: Which capture of the statements best corresponds to ArchiMate 3.2?
options: (1) work package, (2) deliverable, (3) plateau, (4) implementation event and (5) gap. Plateau “Baseline” –triggering→ plateau “Parallel operation” –triggering→ plateau “Target”; implementation event “Old system switched off” –triggering→ plateau “Target” and the gap is associated with the baseline and target plateaus.

(1) work package, (2) deliverable, (3) plateau and (4) implementation event; statement (5) is not modelled with a separate element and is written into the description of the target state. Plateau “Baseline” –triggering→ plateau “Parallel operation” –triggering→ plateau “Target” and implementation event “Old system switched off” –triggering→ plateau “Target”.

(1) work package, (2) deliverable, (3) implementation event, (4) implementation event and (5) gap. Implementation event “Parallel operation” –triggering→ implementation event “Old system switched off” –triggering→ plateau “Target”, which is preceded by plateau “Baseline”; the gap is associated with the baseline and target plateaus.

(1) plateau, (2) gap, (3) work package, (4) deliverable and (5) implementation event. Plateau “Audit” –triggering→ work package “Parallel operation” –access→ deliverable “Old system switched off”; gap “Audit report” is associated with plateau “Audit” and implementation event “Cards instead of tickets” describes the difference between the states.
explanation: An audit is work with a start and an end (work package), the report is its precisely defined result (deliverable), parallel operation is a relatively stable state of the architecture for a limited time (plateau), the switch-off is a moment without duration (implementation event), and the statement about the difference between states is a gap associated with two plateaus – this is how the 5-point option captures it. The 3-point option classifies correctly and uses valid relationships, but it does not model the difference between the states with an element, so it cannot be analysed further. The 1-point option errs in the key element: a six-month parallel operation has a duration and therefore cannot be an event. The 0-point option confuses almost all the elements – work for a state, a result for a difference and a moment for an output.

image.alt: The five ArchiMate implementation and migration elements with icons: Work Package, Deliverable, Implementation Event, Plateau and Gap.

scenario:
The logistics company NordTrans must replace, in the next quarter, the disk array on which the data of most of its systems resides. The array has been in operation for eight years and the supplier is ceasing to supply spare parts for it. The replacement means a shutdown of several hours. The head of IT operations is to decide on which of the offered dates the shutdown will cause the least damage, and defend his proposal before the heads of the warehouses and dispatching. To do so he needs to know which servers depend on the array, which applications run on them and which business processes – for example night route planning or goods receipt – the shutdown would stop. The architecture team has a complete model of all layers in its repository and is considering four kinds of views.

In making the choice the architect follows the ArchiMate classification of viewpoints by purpose (Designing, Deciding, Informing) and by content (Details, Coherence, Overview).
question: Which view should the architect prepare for the head of IT operations?
options: A view with the purpose Deciding and the content Coherence: across layers it shows the disk array, servers, applications and business processes connected by serving, realization and assignment relationships. It is supplemented by a table of the processes affected by the shutdown on each of the offered dates.

A view with the purpose Designing and the content Coherence: a complete design model across layers with all functions, interfaces, artifacts and data objects between the disk array and the business processes, in the form in which architects work with it when designing a solution.

A view with the purpose Designing and the content Details: a detailed diagram of a single layer that shows the disk array, its controllers, connected servers, networks and system software including versions. In this form it will be used by the supplier’s technicians during the replacement.

A view with the purpose Informing and the content Overview: an illustrated overview of the company’s strategic capabilities and the main areas of IT with icons and short captions. It will be posted on the company intranet and will acquaint employees with the planned modernisation of the infrastructure.
explanation: The head of operations is deciding (Deciding) and needs to analyse dependencies and the impact of a change across layers, which is the content Coherence – a view expressing relationships of the type uses, realizes and is assigned to, summarised for the decision in a table. The 3-point option has the right content, but the level of detail and the form of a design model suit architects, not a manager who is to choose a date. The 1-point option stays in a single layer: it shows what is changing, but not which applications and processes the shutdown will affect. The 0-point option targets a different audience and a different concern and says nothing about dependencies.

image.alt: Two dimensions of the viewpoint classification: purpose (Designing, Deciding, Informing) and content (Details, Coherence, Overview) with typical stakeholders.

scenario:
The credit union Uspora is introducing a new loan-arranging solution at its 25 branches, on which two external suppliers are working. The architect has the whole solution in one model and printed from it, for all concerned, a single large diagram across all layers. The reactions were poor. The integration developers did not find in it the details of interfaces and data objects that they need for the design. The IT director, who is to decide on the order of investments, got lost in the diagram. The branch employees, who are to learn what will change in their work, did not understand it at all; they do not know the ArchiMate notation.

The head of architecture wants the architect to proceed according to the ArchiMate viewpoint mechanism and everything presented to those concerned to remain mutually consistent even after further changes to the solution, which are expected in the coming months.
question: How should the architect proceed?
options: Keep one model and define above it three viewpoints, each with stakeholders and their concerns, with a purpose and content: Designing and Details for the developers, Deciding and Overview for the IT director and Informing with a simplified representation for the branches. Then create a view from the model according to each viewpoint.

Keep one model and derive from the original diagram three versions that differ in the number of elements shown: the full one for the developers, a shortened one for the IT director and the most concise one for the branches. These three versions keep the standard notation and the same layout for easy comparison.

For each group draw its own model, independent of the others, in a tool close to it: a detailed interface design for the developers, an investment overview in a table for the IT director and an illustrated leaflet for the branches. After these three new materials are completed, do not maintain the common model any further.

Keep the single complete diagram on the grounds that, according to the standard, there is only one viewpoint for the whole architecture and it shows it the same way to everyone. Add a legend to the diagram and train each of the three groups, including the branch employees, in the ArchiMate notation, before the next printing.
explanation: According to the viewpoint mechanism, different views arise from one model according to viewpoints, each of which targets certain stakeholders and their concerns and is determined by a purpose and content; views derived from the same model remain consistent (5). The 3-point option keeps one model but changes only the number of elements – it does not adapt the purpose or the way of presentation, so it helps neither the branches nor the IT director. The 1-point option accommodates the audience, but three independent models are not views of one architecture and their consistency will fall apart. The 0-point option rests on a mistake: there can be any number of viewpoints and they are chosen precisely according to stakeholders and their concerns.

scenario:
After the merger of two regional hospitals, Posazavi Hospital was created with two campuses. The HR director needs to clarify competences, powers and responsibilities: which units the new hospital has, how they are incorporated into one another, who reports to whom and on which campus each unit is based. According to her, heads of clinics and new employees will ask the same question next year. The architecture office keeps a library of viewpoints, thanks to which views for recurring questions are produced uniformly and can be recreated at any time from the current model.

The architect is first to describe in the library the viewpoint according to which she will create the view for the HR director. The description is to enable anyone in the office to create the same kind of view for another part of the hospital and to judge whether the view really answers the question posed.
question: Which description of the viewpoint is the best?
options: Stakeholders: HR director, heads of clinics and employees. Concerns: competences, powers and responsibilities. Purpose: Deciding and Informing. Scope: one layer and one aspect. Elements: business actors, roles and locations with composition, aggregation and assignment relationships, possibly by nesting.

Elements: business actors, roles and locations with composition, aggregation and assignment relationships, possibly by nesting. Presentation: standard ArchiMate notation with colour differentiation of the two campuses and with a legend. Stakeholders, their concerns and the purpose are not given in the description; they are determined separately for each view.

Stakeholders: HR director, heads of clinics and employees. Concerns: competences, powers and responsibilities. Purpose: Deciding and Informing. Scope: multiple layers. Elements: business processes, application components and nodes with serving, flow and realization relationships, grouped by campuses.

The viewpoint is the organisation chart of the merged hospital itself, which the architect draws and stores in the library as a binding template. A view is then the angle from which the HR director, the heads of clinics and new employees look at the diagram, and the architect describes it in a single short sentence in the diagram’s legend.
explanation: A viewpoint is a specification of conventions for a certain kind of view: it says which stakeholders and concerns it is intended for, what purpose and scope it has, and which elements and relationships it contains – for questions of competences and responsibilities these are actors, roles and locations in one layer and one aspect (5). The 3-point option selects the right elements, but without stakeholders, concerns and purpose it cannot be judged whether the view answers the question. The 1-point option has a formally complete description, but the chosen content – processes, applications and nodes – does not answer the question of who reports to whom. The 0-point option confuses the concepts: a view is what a stakeholder sees, and a viewpoint is where they look from, that is, a specification, not a diagram.
